sentences.zh: 衛操，字德元，代人也。

translations.literal: Wei Cao, style name Deyuan, was a man of Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Cao, styled Deyuan, came from Dai.

sentences.zh: 少通俠，有才略。

translations.literal: In youth he mastered chivalry and had talent and stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he excelled at chivalric ways and showed talent and strategic sense.

sentences.zh: 晉征北將軍衛瓘以操為牙門將。

translations.literal: Jin's General Who Pacifies the North Wei Guan took Cao as gate commander.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin General Who Pacifies the North, Wei Guan, appointed Cao gate commander.

sentences.zh: 當魏神元時，頗自結附。

translations.literal: In the time of Divine Yuan he often attached himself to the court.
translations.idiomatic: During the reign of Emperor Shenyuan he cultivated close ties with the state.

sentences.zh: 及神元崩後，與從子雄及其宗室鄉親姬淡等來歸，說桓、穆二帝招納晉人。

translations.literal: After Shenyuan's death, with his nephew Xiong and kinsmen and fellow-townsmen Ji Dan and others he came to submit, urging the Huan and Mu emperors to recruit Jin men.
translations.idiomatic: After Shenyuan died, he came in with his nephew Xiong, kinsmen, and fellow-townsmen such as Ji Dan and urged the Huan and Mu emperors to enlist Jin subjects.

sentences.zh: 桓帝以為輔相，任以國事。

translations.literal: Emperor Huan made him chief minister and entrusted him with state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Huan made him chief minister and gave him charge of state affairs.

sentences.zh: 及劉、石之亂，桓帝匡助晉氏。

translations.literal: When the Liu and Shi disorders broke out, Emperor Huan aided the Jin house.
translations.idiomatic: When turmoil engulfed the Liu and Shi regimes, Emperor Huan supported the Jin.

sentences.zh: 操稍遷至右將軍，封定襄侯。

translations.literal: Cao was gradually promoted to Right General and enfeoffed Marquis of Dingxiang.
translations.idiomatic: Cao rose step by step to Right General and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Dingxiang.

sentences.zh: 皇興初，雍州別駕雁門段榮於大邗掘得此碑，文雖非麗，事宜載焉，故略附於傳。

translations.literal: In early Huangxing, Yan Province Aide Duan Rong of Yanmen unearthed this stele at Dahang; though the text is not elegant, the matter deserves record, so it is briefly appended to the biography.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Huangxing, Duan Rong, aide of Yan Province from Yanmen, dug up this stele at Dahang; the prose is plain, but the matter is worth preserving, so it is summarized here.

sentences.zh: 操以穆帝三年卒。

translations.literal: Cao died in the third year of Emperor Mu.
translations.idiomatic: Cao died in the third year of Emperor Mu's reign.

sentences.zh: 始操所與宗室鄉親入國者，衛勤安樂亭侯，衛崇、衛清並都亭侯，衛沈、段繁並信義將軍、都鄉侯，王發建武將軍、都亭侯，范班折沖將軍、廣武亭侯，賈慶建武將軍、上洛亭侯，賈循都亭侯，李壹關中侯，郭乳關內侯，皆為桓帝所表授也。

translations.literal: At first those kinsmen and fellow-townsmen who entered the state with Cao—Wei Qin, Marquis of Anle Pavilion; Wei Chong and Wei Qing, both Marquises of the Capital Pavilion; Wei Shen and Duan Fan, both Generals of Trust and Righteousness and Marquises of the Capital District; Wang Fa, General Who Establishes Martial Might and Marquis of the Capital Pavilion; Fan Ban, General Who Breaks the Foe and Marquis of Guangwu Pavilion; Jia Qing, General Who Establishes Martial Might and Marquis of Shangluo Pavilion; Jia Xun, Marquis of the Capital Pavilion; Li Yi, Marquis Within the Passes; Guo Ru, Marquis Within the Domains—all were enfeoffed and appointed by Emperor Huan.
translations.idiomatic: The kinsmen and fellow-townsmen who had entered the state with Cao were enfeoffed by Emperor Huan: Wei Qin as Marquis of Anle Pavilion; Wei Chong and Wei Qing as Marquises of the Capital Pavilion; Wei Shen and Duan Fan as Generals of Trust and Righteousness and Marquises of the Capital District; Wang Fa as General Who Establishes Martial Might and Marquis of the Capital Pavilion; Fan Ban as General Who Breaks the Foe and Marquis of Guangwu Pavilion; Jia Qing as General Who Establishes Martial Might and Marquis of Shangluo Pavilion; Jia Xun as Marquis of the Capital Pavilion; Li Yi as Marquis Within the Passes; and Guo Ru as Marquis Within the Domains.

sentences.zh: 六修之難，存者多隨劉琨任子遵南奔。

translations.literal: In the turmoil of Liuxiu, most of those who survived followed Liu Kun's envoy Ren Zun south in flight.
translations.idiomatic: During the crisis of Liuxiu, most survivors followed Liu Kun's envoy Ren Zun in flight to the south.

sentences.zh: 衛雄、姬淡、莫含等名皆見碑。

translations.literal: The names of Wei Xiong, Ji Dan, Mo Han, and others all appear on the stele.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Xiong, Ji Dan, Mo Han, and others are all named on the stele.

sentences.zh: 雄字世遠，淡字世雅，並勇健多計，桓帝並以為將，常隨征伐。

translations.literal: Xiong, style name Shiyuan, and Dan, style name Shiya, were both bold and resourceful; both emperors Huan made them generals and they constantly followed campaigns.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong, styled Shiyuan, and Dan, styled Shiya, were bold and full of schemes; both were made generals by Emperor Huan and regularly joined campaigns.

sentences.zh: 雄稍遷至左將軍、雲中侯。

translations.literal: Xiong was gradually promoted to Left General and Marquis of Yunzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong rose to Left General and Marquis of Yunzhong.

sentences.zh: 淡亦以勇績著名，桓帝末，至信義將軍、樓煩侯。

translations.literal: Dan also became famous for martial deeds; late in Emperor Huan's reign he reached General of Trust and Righteousness and Marquis of Loufan.
translations.idiomatic: Dan likewise won renown in battle; late in Emperor Huan's reign he became General of Trust and Righteousness and Marquis of Loufan.

sentences.zh: 穆帝初，並見委任，衛操卒後，俱為左右輔相。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Mu both were entrusted with office; after Wei Cao's death they both served as left and right chief ministers.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Emperor Mu's reign both were heavily relied upon; after Wei Cao died they served together as chief ministers of the left and right.

sentences.zh: 六修之逆，國內大亂，雄、淡並為群情所附，乃與劉遵率烏丸、晉人數萬而叛。

translations.literal: In Liuxiu's rebellion the realm fell into great disorder; Xiong and Dan were both embraced by popular sentiment, and with Liu Zun they led tens of thousands of Wuhuan and Jin men in revolt.
translations.idiomatic: When Liuxiu rebelled and the realm convulsed, Xiong and Dan won popular support and, with Liu Zun, led tens of thousands of Wuhuan and Jin subjects in revolt.

sentences.zh: 劉琨聞之，大悅，如平城撫納之，欲因以滅石勒。

translations.literal: Liu Kun heard of it and was greatly pleased; he came to Pingcheng to comfort and accept them, intending thereby to destroy Shi Le.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Kun was delighted, went to Pingcheng to welcome them, and hoped to use them to destroy Shi Le.

sentences.zh: 後為勒將孔長所滅。

translations.literal: Later they were destroyed by Le's general Kong Chang.
translations.idiomatic: They were later destroyed by Kong Chang, a general of Shi Le.

sentences.zh: 莫含，雁門繁畦人也。

translations.literal: Mo Han was a man of Fanchi in Yanmen.
translations.idiomatic: Mo Han came from Fanchi in Yanmen.

sentences.zh: 劉琨為并州，辟含從事。

translations.literal: When Liu Kun held Bing Province he recruited Han as an aide.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Kun governed Bing Province he took Han on as an aide.

sentences.zh: 含居近塞下，常交通國中。

translations.literal: Han lived near the frontier and often had dealings within the state.
translations.idiomatic: Han lived near the border and kept up regular contact with the court.

sentences.zh: 穆帝愛其才器。

translations.literal: Emperor Mu prized his talent and capacity.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Mu admired his ability.

sentences.zh: 及為代王，備置官屬，求含於琨，琨喻遣之。

translations.literal: When he became King of Dai he fully staffed his officials and sought Han from Kun; Kun instructed Han to go.
translations.idiomatic: When he became King of Dai he formed a full bureaucracy and asked Kun for Han; Kun urged Han to go.

sentences.zh: 乃入參國官，常參軍國大謀。

translations.literal: He then entered to take part in state office and constantly joined in great plans of state.
translations.idiomatic: He entered government service and regularly took part in major state deliberations.

sentences.zh: 卒于左將軍、關中侯。

translations.literal: He died holding Left General and Marquis Within the Passes.
translations.idiomatic: He died as Left General and Marquis Within the Passes.

sentences.zh: 其故宅在桑乾川南，世稱莫含壁，含音訛，或謂之莫回城云。

translations.literal: His old residence lay south of the Sanggan River; the world calls it Mo Han's cliff—"Han" being a corrupted pronunciation—or sometimes Mo Hui City.
translations.idiomatic: His old home stood south of the Sanggan; people call it Mo Han's Cliff—"Han" being a corrupted form of the name—or Mo Hui City.

sentences.zh: 子顯，昭成世為左常侍。

translations.literal: His son Xian, in the age of Zhaocheng, was Left Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xian served as Left Regular Attendant under Emperor Zhaocheng.

sentences.zh: 顯子題，道武初，為大將，以功賜爵東宛侯。

translations.literal: Xian's son Ti, at the beginning of Daowu, was a great general and for merit was granted the title Marquis of Dongwan.
translations.idiomatic: Xian's son Ti, in Emperor Daowu's early reign, became a great general and was enfeoffed Marquis of Dongwan for his achievements.

sentences.zh: 常與李栗侍宴，栗坐不敬獲罪，題亦被黜為濟陽太守。

translations.literal: He often attended banquets with Li Li; Li was punished for disrespect in seating, and Ti was also demoted to Governor of Jiyang.
translations.idiomatic: He often shared banquets with Li Li; when Li was punished for irreverence at table, Ti was demoted to Governor of Jiyang.

sentences.zh: 後道武欲廣宮室，規度平城四方數十里，將模鄴、洛、長安之制，運材數百萬根。

translations.literal: Later Daowu wished to enlarge the palaces and measured several tens of li around Pingcheng, intending to model Ye, Luoyang, and Chang'an, and transported several million timbers.
translations.idiomatic: Later Emperor Daowu planned to expand the palace complex, surveyed tens of li around Pingcheng on the model of Ye, Luoyang, and Chang'an, and requisitioned millions of beams.

sentences.zh: 以題機巧，征令監之。

translations.literal: Because Ti was ingenious in craft, he was summoned to supervise the work.
translations.idiomatic: Ti's mechanical skill led to his appointment as overseer of construction.

sentences.zh: 召入，與論興造之制，題久侍頗怠，賜死。

translations.literal: Summoned in to discuss the design of the works, after long attendance he grew quite negligent and was granted death.
translations.idiomatic: Called in to discuss the building plans, he grew slack during long attendance at court and was put to death.

sentences.zh: 題弟雲，好學善射。

translations.literal: Ti's younger brother Yun loved learning and was skilled at archery.
translations.idiomatic: Ti's younger brother Yun loved study and excelled at archery.

sentences.zh: 道武時，常典選曹，賜爵安德侯。

translations.literal: In Daowu's time he regularly managed the Selection Bureau and was granted Marquis of Ande.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Daowu he ran the Selection Bureau and was enfeoffed Marquis of Ande.

sentences.zh: 遷執金吾，參軍國謀議。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Commandant of the Imperial Carriages and joined in state deliberations.
translations.idiomatic: He became Commandant of the Imperial Carriages and took part in state counsel.

sentences.zh: 太武克赫連昌，詔雲與常山王素留鎮統萬，進爵安定公。

translations.literal: When Taiwu conquered Helian Chang, an edict ordered Yun and the Prince of Changshan, Su, to remain and garrison Tongwan, and he was advanced to Duke of Anding.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taiwu took Helian Chang, Yun and Prince Su of Changshan were ordered to hold Tongwan; Yun was promoted to Duke of Anding.

sentences.zh: 雲撫慰新舊，皆得其所。

translations.literal: Yun comforted old and new alike, and all found their place.
translations.idiomatic: Yun reassured old subjects and new, and all were settled.

sentences.zh: 卒，諡敬公。

translations.literal: On his death he was posthumously titled Duke Jing.
translations.idiomatic: After his death he received the posthumous title Duke Jing.

sentences.zh: 劉庫仁字沒根，獨孤部人，劉武之宗也。

translations.literal: Liu Kuren, style name Meigen, was of the Dugu tribe, a clansman of Liu Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Kuren, styled Meigen, belonged to the Dugu tribe and was kin to Liu Wu.

sentences.zh: 少豪俠，有智略。

translations.literal: In youth he was bold and chivalrous, with wisdom and stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he was daring and chivalrous, with wit and strategy.

sentences.zh: 母平文皇帝之女。

translations.literal: His mother was a daughter of Emperor Pingwen.
translations.idiomatic: His mother was a daughter of Emperor Pingwen.

sentences.zh: 昭成皇帝復以宗女妻之，為南部大人。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhaocheng again gave him a clanswoman in marriage and made him Grand Chieftain of the Southern Tribes.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhaocheng again married him to a clanswoman and appointed him Grand Chieftain of the Southern Tribes.

sentences.zh: 建國三十九年，照成暴崩，道武未立，苻堅以庫仁為陵江將軍、關內侯。

translations.literal: In the thirty-ninth year of Jianguo Zhaocheng died suddenly; Daowu was not yet enthroned, and Fu Jian made Kuren General Who Crosses the River and Marquis Within the Passes.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-ninth year of Jianguo, Zhaocheng died suddenly before Daowu had taken the throne; Fu Jian made Kuren General Who Crosses the River and Marquis Within the Passes.

sentences.zh: 令與衛辰分國眾統之，河西屬衛辰，河東屬庫仁。

translations.literal: He ordered him and Wei Chen to divide the tribal masses and rule them—the west of the river to Chen, the east to Kuren.
translations.idiomatic: He set Kuren and Wei Chen to divide the tribal following: the west of the river to Chen, the east to Kuren.

sentences.zh: 於是獻明皇后攜道武及衛、秦二王自賀蘭部來居焉。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Xianming Empress brought Daowu and the princes of Wei and Qin from the Helan tribe to dwell there.
translations.idiomatic: The Xianming Empress then brought Daowu and the Wei and Qin princes from the Helan tribe to live under Kuren's protection.

sentences.zh: 庫仁盡忠奉事，不以興廢易節。

translations.literal: Kuren served with full loyalty and did not change his devotion with rise or fall.
translations.idiomatic: Kuren served with steadfast loyalty, unmoved by fortune or ruin.

sentences.zh: 苻堅處衛辰在庫仁下，衛辰怒，叛，攻庫仁。

translations.literal: Fu Jian placed Wei Chen beneath Kuren; Chen was enraged, rebelled, and attacked Kuren.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian ranked Wei Chen below Kuren; Chen in anger rebelled and attacked him.

sentences.zh: 庫仁伐衛辰，破之。

translations.literal: Kuren attacked Chen and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: Kuren struck Chen and routed him.

sentences.zh: 苻堅賜庫仁妻公孫氏，厚其資送。

translations.literal: Fu Jian granted Kuren's wife the Lady Gongsun and enriched her dowry.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian gave Kuren's wife the surname Gongsun and sent a lavish dowry.

sentences.zh: 慕容垂圍苻丕於鄴，又遣將平規攻堅幽州刺史王永于薊。

translations.literal: Murong Chui besieged Fu Pi at Ye and also sent a general, Ping Gui, to attack Fu Jian's Yan Province governor Wang Yong at Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Chui besieged Fu Pi at Ye and sent Ping Gui to attack Wang Yong, Fu Jian's governor of Yan Province, at Ji.

sentences.zh: 庫仁遣妻兄公孫希助永擊規，大破之。

translations.literal: Kuren sent his wife's elder brother Gongsun Xi to aid Yong in striking Gui and inflicted a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Kuren sent his brother-in-law Gongsun Xi to help Yong against Gui and won a crushing victory.

sentences.zh: 庫仁復將大舉以救丕。

translations.literal: Kuren again was about to lead a major force to rescue Pi.
translations.idiomatic: Kuren prepared to march in force to relieve Pi.

sentences.zh: 發雁門、上穀、代郡兵，次於繁畤。

translations.literal: He mobilized troops from Yanmen, Shanggu, and Dai commanderies and halted at Fanzhi.
translations.idiomatic: He raised troops from Yanmen, Shanggu, and Dai and camped at Fanzhi.

sentences.zh: 先是，慕容文等當徙長安，遁依庫仁部，常思東歸。

translations.literal: Earlier, Murong Wen and others, who were to be relocated to Chang'an, had fled to Kuren's tribe and constantly thought of returning east.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Murong Wen and others, slated for relocation to Chang'an, had taken refuge with Kuren and longed to go east again.

sentences.zh: 是役也，文等夜率三郡人，攻殺庫仁，乘其駿馬，奔慕容垂。

translations.literal: In this campaign Wen and others by night led men of the three commanderies, attacked and killed Kuren, seized his swift horses, and fled to Murong Chui.
translations.idiomatic: On this campaign Wen and others led men of the three commanderies by night, killed Kuren, took his best horses, and fled to Murong Chui.

sentences.zh: 公孫希聞亂走丁零。

translations.literal: Gongsun Xi, hearing of the turmoil, fled to the Dingling.
translations.idiomatic: Gongsun Xi, hearing of the upheaval, fled to the Dingling.

sentences.zh: 庫仁弟眷，繼攝國事。

translations.literal: Kuren's younger brother Juan succeeded to govern the tribe's affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Kuren's younger brother Juan took charge of tribal affairs.

sentences.zh: 眷第三子羅辰，機警有智謀，謂眷曰：「從兄顯，忍人也，願早圖之。

translations.literal: Juan's third son Luo Chen, alert and wise in stratagem, said to Juan, "Cousin Xian is a cruel man—I wish you would plot against him early.
translations.idiomatic: Juan's third son Luo Chen, sharp and full of schemes, told Juan, "Cousin Xian is ruthless; you should deal with him soon.

sentences.zh: 」眷不以為意。

translations.literal: " Juan paid no heed.
translations.idiomatic: Juan paid no attention.

sentences.zh: 後庫仁子顯果殺眷而代立。

translations.literal: Later Kuren's son Xian indeed killed Juan and replaced him.
translations.idiomatic: Later Kuren's son Xian killed Juan and seized power.

sentences.zh: 顯既殺眷，又謀逆。

translations.literal: Once Xian had killed Juan he also plotted rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: After killing Juan, Xian also plotted rebellion.

sentences.zh: 及道武即位，討顯于馬邑，追至彌澤，大破之。

translations.literal: When Daowu took the throne he attacked Xian at Mayi, pursued him to Mize, and inflicted a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: When Daowu came to the throne he attacked Xian at Mayi, pursued him to Mize, and routed him.

sentences.zh: 後奔慕容驎，驎徙之中山。

translations.literal: Later he fled to Murong Lin; Lin moved him to Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: He later fled to Murong Lin, who resettled him at Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 羅辰即宣穆皇后兄也。

translations.literal: Luo Chen was also the elder brother of the Xuanmu Empress.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Chen was the elder brother of the Xuanmu Empress.

sentences.zh: 顯既殺眷，羅辰遂奔道武。

translations.literal: After Xian killed Juan, Luo Chen fled to Daowu.
translations.idiomatic: When Xian killed Juan, Luo Chen fled to Daowu.

sentences.zh: 顯恃強，每謀逆，羅辰輒先聞奏。

translations.literal: Xian relied on his strength and often plotted rebellion; Luo Chen always reported it first.
translations.idiomatic: Xian, trusting in his power, repeatedly plotted revolt; Luo Chen always warned the throne in advance.

sentences.zh: 拜南部大人。

translations.literal: He was appointed Grand Chieftain of the Southern Tribes.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Grand Chieftain of the Southern Tribes.

sentences.zh: 從平中原，以功賜爵永安公。

translations.literal: Following the pacification of the Central Plains, for merit he was granted Duke of Yong'an.
translations.idiomatic: After the conquest of the Central Plains he was enfeoffed Duke of Yong'an for his service.

sentences.zh: 以軍功除征東將軍、定州刺史。

translations.literal: For military achievement he was made General Who Pacifies the East and Governor of Ding Province.
translations.idiomatic: For military merit he became General Who Pacifies the East and Governor of Ding Province.

sentences.zh: 卒，諡曰敬。

translations.literal: On his death his posthumous title was Jing.
translations.idiomatic: He died with the posthumous title Jing.

sentences.zh: 子殊暉襲爵，位并州刺史，卒。

translations.literal: His son Shuhui inherited the title, held the post of Governor of Bing Province, and died.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shuhui inherited the title, served as Governor of Bing Province, and died.

sentences.zh: 子求引，位武衛將軍。

translations.literal: His son Qiuyin held the post of General of the Martial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: His son Qiuyin was General of the Martial Guard.

sentences.zh: 卒，諡曰貞。

translations.literal: On his death his posthumous title was Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: He died with the posthumous title Zhen.

sentences.zh: 子爾頭，位魏昌、癭陶二縣令，贈钜鹿太守。

translations.literal: His son Ertou held the posts of magistrate of Weichang and Yingtao counties and was posthumously made Governor of Julu.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ertou was magistrate of Weichang and Yingtao and was posthumously named Governor of Julu.

sentences.zh: 子仁之，字山靜，少有操尚，粗涉書史。

translations.literal: His son Renzhi, style name Shanjing, in youth had moral resolve and had roughly browsed histories.
translations.idiomatic: His son Renzhi, styled Shanjing, showed moral fiber in youth and had read history in a general way.

sentences.zh: 歷位衛將軍、西兗州刺史，在州有當時之譽。

translations.literal: He held the posts of General of the Guard and Governor of Western Yan Province and at his post won contemporary renown.
translations.idiomatic: He served as General of the Guard and Governor of Western Yan Province and earned a reputation in his day.

sentences.zh: 武定二年卒，贈衛大將軍、吏部尚書、青州刺史，諡曰敬。

translations.literal: He died in the second year of Wuding and was posthumously made Grand General of the Guard, Minister of the Civil Service, and Governor of Qing Province, with posthumous title Jing.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the second year of Wuding and was posthumously made Grand General of the Guard, Minister of the Civil Service, and Governor of Qing Province, with the posthumous title Jing.

sentences.zh: 仁之外示長者，內多矯詐。

translations.literal: Outwardly Renzhi appeared a man of virtue; inwardly he was full of pretense.
translations.idiomatic: Renzhi posed as a man of virtue while inwardly he was full of artifice.

sentences.zh: 其對賓客，破床弊席，粗飯冷菜，衣服故惡，乃過逼下。

translations.literal: Toward guests he broke beds and worn mats, served coarse rice and cold dishes, and wore old, foul clothes—yet he overbore his subordinates.
translations.idiomatic: With guests he used broken beds and threadbare mats, coarse rice and cold dishes, and shabby clothes—yet he bullied those beneath him.

sentences.zh: 善候當塗，能為詭激。

translations.literal: He was skilled at watching those in power and could perform crafty provocations.
translations.idiomatic: He watched those in power keenly and knew how to stage theatrical outbursts.

sentences.zh: 每於稠人廣眾中，或撾一奸吏，或縱一孤貧，大言自眩，淺識皆稱其美。

translations.literal: Often in dense crowds he would beat some corrupt official or release some lone poor man, declaiming loudly to dazzle others; shallow minds all praised his goodness.
translations.idiomatic: In crowded gatherings he might thrash a corrupt clerk or spare a lone beggar, declaiming for effect; the shallow praised him as noble.

sentences.zh: 公能之譽，動過其實。

translations.literal: His reputation for public ability far exceeded the fact.
translations.idiomatic: His fame for public spirit far outran the reality.

sentences.zh: 性又酷虐，在晉陽曾營城雉，仁之統監作役。

translations.literal: His nature was also cruel; at Jinyang he once undertook city-wall works, and Renzhi directed the labor.
translations.idiomatic: He was also brutal; at Jinyang he once oversaw repairs to the city walls under Renzhi's supervision.

sentences.zh: 以小稽緩，遂杖前殷州刺史裴瑗、并州刺史王綽。

translations.literal: For slight delay he beat the former Governor of Yin Province Pei Yuan and the Governor of Bing Province Wang Chuo.
translations.idiomatic: For minor tardiness he had Pei Yuan, former governor of Yin Province, and Wang Chuo, governor of Bing Province, flogged.

sentences.zh: 齊神武大加譴責。

translations.literal: Qi Emperor Shenwu rebuked him severely.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Emperor Shenwu censured him harshly.

sentences.zh: 性好文字。

translations.literal: He loved written texts by nature.
translations.idiomatic: He had a natural love of the written word.

sentences.zh: 吏書失體，便加鞭撻；

translations.literal: If clerical writing lost proper form he would add flogging;
translations.idiomatic: Clerical errors in format earned a beating;

sentences.zh: 言韻微訛，亦見捶楚，吏人以此苦之。

translations.literal: if pronunciation was slightly off he also met the cudgel, and clerks suffered greatly for it.
translations.idiomatic: even slight slips in tone brought the rod, and clerks suffered for it.

sentences.zh: 而愛好文史，敬重人流。

translations.literal: Yet he loved literature and history and respected men of talent.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he cherished literature and history and treated men of talent with respect.

sentences.zh: 與齋帥馮元興交款。

translations.literal: He was on intimate terms with the guard officer Feng Yuanxing.
translations.idiomatic: He was close to the guard officer Feng Yuanxing.

sentences.zh: 元興死後積年，仁之營視其家，常出隆厚，時人以此尚之。

translations.literal: Years after Yuanxing's death Renzhi still looked after his household and often gave lavish aid; people esteemed him for this.
translations.idiomatic: Years after Yuanxing died, Renzhi still tended his family with generous support, and contemporaries admired him for it.

sentences.zh: 仁之伯乞歸，真君中，除中散大夫。

translations.literal: Renzhi's elder uncle Qi Gui, in the Zhenjun era, was made Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Renzhi's elder uncle Qi Gui was appointed Palace Attendant in the Zhenjun era.

sentences.zh: 性寬和，與物無競，未嘗言人善惡。

translations.literal: By nature he was mild and did not contend with others, and he never spoke of others' good or ill.
translations.idiomatic: Mild by nature, he shunned rivalry and never spoke of others' virtues or faults.

sentences.zh: 曾遇患晝寢，有奴偷竊，乞歸詐睡不見，亦不泄之。

translations.literal: Once when ill he slept by day and a slave stole from him; Qi Gui feigned sleep and did not see, nor did he reveal it.
translations.idiomatic: Once, ill, he napped by day while a slave stole from him; Qi Gui pretended to sleep, saw nothing, and said nothing.

sentences.zh: 此奴走入蠕蠕，方笑言之，亦無嗔色。

translations.literal: That slave fled into the Rouran; only then did he laugh and speak of it, yet showed no anger.
translations.idiomatic: The slave later fled to the Rouran; only then did Qi Gui laugh and mention the theft, without a trace of anger.

sentences.zh: 獻文末，除主客尚書。

translations.literal: Late in Xianwen's reign he was made Minister of Guests.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Emperor Xianwen's reign he became Minister of Guests.

sentences.zh: 孝文初，位東雍州刺史，賜爵永安侯。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xiaowen he held Eastern Yong Province and was granted Marquis of Yong'an.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Emperor Xiaowen's reign he governed Eastern Yong Province and was enfeoffed Marquis of Yong'an.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 子嵩，字阿龍，好周人之急。

translations.literal: His son Song, style name Along, loved to aid others in urgent need.
translations.idiomatic: His son Song, styled Along, delighted in helping others through emergencies.

sentences.zh: 與王仲興自平城被追赴洛，家貧不能自達，嵩事事資遣。

translations.literal: With Wang Zhongxing he was driven from Pingcheng toward Luoyang; the household was poor and could not manage the journey, and Song supplied everything for the road.
translations.idiomatic: Driven from Pingcheng toward Luoyang with Wang Zhongxing, too poor to travel, Song funded their entire journey.

sentences.zh: 宣武時，仲興寵倖，乃奏除給事。

translations.literal: In Emperor Xuanwu's time Zhongxing became a favored intimate and then memorialized to appoint Song as attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Xuanwu, when Zhongxing won favor at court, he had Song appointed palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 請疏黃河，以通船漕，授龍門都將。

translations.literal: He requested dredging the Yellow River to open shipping and was made Commandant of Longmen.
translations.idiomatic: He petitioned to dredge the Yellow River for shipping and was made Commandant of Longmen.

sentences.zh: 歷年功不就，坐流。

translations.literal: After years the work was not completed and he was sentenced to exile.
translations.idiomatic: Years passed without finishing the work, and he was exiled.

sentences.zh: 元曄僭立，授大鴻臚卿。

translations.literal: When Yuan Ye seized the throne unlawfully he was made Grand Minister of the Imperial Clan.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Ye usurped the throne he was appointed Grand Minister of the Imperial Clan.

sentences.zh: 子桃湯，位終奉朝請。

translations.literal: His son Taotang ended his career as Court Gentleman for Attendance.
translations.idiomatic: His son Taotang ended his career as Court Gentleman for Attendance.

sentences.zh: 尉古真，代人也。

translations.literal: Wei Guzhen was a man of Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Guzhen came from Dai.

sentences.zh: 道武之在賀蘭部，賀染幹遣侯引乙突等將肆逆。

translations.literal: When Daowu was in the Helan tribe, He Ranggan sent Hou Yin, Yituo, and others to attempt treason.
translations.idiomatic: While Daowu dwelt with the Helan tribe, He Ranggan sent Hou Yin, Yituo, and others to plot treason.

sentences.zh: 古真知之，密以馳告。

translations.literal: Guzhen learned of it and secretly sent a swift messenger to report.
translations.idiomatic: Guzhen learned of the plot and sent a secret courier to warn him.

sentences.zh: 染幹疑古真泄其謀，乃執拷之，以兩車軸押其頭，傷其一目。

translations.literal: Ranggan suspected Guzhen had leaked the plot, seized and tortured him, pressing his head between two cart axles and injuring one eye.
translations.idiomatic: Ranggan suspected Guzhen had betrayed the plot, seized him, and tortured him by crushing his head between cart axles until he lost an eye.

sentences.zh: 不服，乃免之。

translations.literal: He did not confess and was then released.
translations.idiomatic: He would not confess and was finally released.

sentences.zh: 後從平中原，以功賜爵束州侯。

translations.literal: Later, following the pacification of the Central Plains, for merit he was granted Marquis of Dong Province.
translations.idiomatic: After the conquest of the Central Plains he was enfeoffed Marquis of Dong Province for his service.

sentences.zh: 明元初，為鴻飛將軍，鎮大洛。

translations.literal: In early Mingyuan he was General of Soaring Flight and garrisoned Daluo.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Emperor Mingyuan's reign he was General of Soaring Flight and garrisoned Daluo.

sentences.zh: 卒于定州刺史。

translations.literal: He died as Governor of Ding Province.
translations.idiomatic: He died while serving as Governor of Ding Province.

sentences.zh: 子億萬襲。

translations.literal: His son Yiwang inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yiwang inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 古真弟諾，以忠謹著稱。

translations.literal: Guzhen's younger brother Nuo was famed for loyalty and prudence.
translations.idiomatic: Guzhen's younger brother Nuo was known for loyalty and discretion.

sentences.zh: 從道武圍中山，先登，傷一目。

translations.literal: Following Daowu in the siege of Zhongshan he was first to scale the wall and lost an eye.
translations.idiomatic: In the siege of Zhongshan under Emperor Daowu he was first over the wall and lost an eye.

sentences.zh: 道武歎曰：「諾兄弟並毀目以建功效，誠可嘉也！

translations.literal: Daowu sighed and said, "The Nuo brothers have both ruined their eyes to build merit—truly worthy of praise!
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Daowu exclaimed, "Both Nuo brothers have sacrificed an eye for merit—truly praiseworthy!

sentences.zh: 」賜安樂子。

translations.literal: " He granted him the title of Viscount of Anle.
translations.idiomatic: He enfeoffed him as Viscount of Anle.

sentences.zh: 從平姚平，還，拜國部大人。

translations.literal: Following the pacification of Yao Ping, on return he was made Grand Chieftain of the National Tribes.
translations.idiomatic: After the pacification of Yao Ping he returned and was made Grand Chieftain of the National Tribes.

sentences.zh: 太武時，改邑遼西公。

translations.literal: In Taiwu's time his fief was changed to Duke of Liaoxi.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Taiwu his fief was raised to Duke of Liaoxi.

sentences.zh: 卒，第八子歡襲。

translations.literal: On his death his eighth son Huan inherited.
translations.idiomatic: At his death his eighth son Huan inherited.

sentences.zh: 多侯少有武幹。

translations.literal: Duohou in youth had martial talent.
translations.idiomatic: Duohou showed martial promise in youth.

sentences.zh: 獻文時，假節、領護羌戎校尉、敦煌鎮將。

translations.literal: In Xianwen's time he held provisional authority as Colonel Protecting the Qiang and Rong and General Garrisoning Dunhuang.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Xianwen he held provisional authority as Colonel Protecting the Qiang and Rong and as garrison general of Dunhuang.

sentences.zh: 至，求輕騎五千，西入于闐，兼平諸國，因敵取資，平定為效。

translations.literal: On arrival he requested five thousand light horsemen to enter Khotan in the west, subdue the states together, take supplies from the enemy, and achieve pacification.
translations.idiomatic: On reaching his post he asked for five thousand light cavalry to push into Khotan, subdue the western states, live off the enemy, and pacify the region.

sentences.zh: 弗許。

translations.literal: It was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: The request was denied.

sentences.zh: 孝文初，又求北取伊吾，斷蠕蠕通西域路。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xiaowen he again requested to take Yiwu in the north and cut the Rouran route to the Western Regions.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Emperor Xiaowen's reign he again asked to seize Yiwu in the north and sever Rouran access to the Western Regions.

sentences.zh: 帝善其計，以東作方興，難之。

translations.literal: The emperor approved the plan but, with eastern works just underway, found it difficult.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved the plan but, with major construction in the east under way, could not spare the forces.

sentences.zh: 為妻元所害。

translations.literal: He was killed by his wife Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: His wife, of the Yuan clan, murdered him.

sentences.zh: 多侯弟子慶賓，善騎射，有將略，稍遷太中大夫。

translations.literal: Duohou's nephew Qingbin was skilled at mounted archery, had general's stratagem, and was gradually promoted to Grand Palace Counselor.
translations.idiomatic: Duohou's nephew Qingbin excelled at mounted archery, showed a commander's mind, and rose to Grand Palace Counselor.

sentences.zh: 明帝時，朝議送蠕蠕主阿那瑰還國。

translations.literal: In Emperor Ming's time the court debated sending the Rouran ruler Anagui back to his country.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Ming the court debated sending the Rouran ruler Anagui home.

sentences.zh: 慶賓上表固爭，不從。

translations.literal: Qingbin memorialized firmly in opposition; they did not follow him.
translations.idiomatic: Qingbin memorialized forcefully against it; the court ignored him.

sentences.zh: 後蠕蠕遂執行台元孚。

translations.literal: Later the Rouran indeed seized the acting commander Yuan Fu.
translations.idiomatic: The Rouran later seized the acting commander Yuan Fu.

sentences.zh: 慶賓後拜肆州刺史。

translations.literal: Qingbin was later made Governor of Si Province.
translations.idiomatic: Qingbin was later appointed Governor of Si Province.

sentences.zh: 時爾硃榮兵威漸盛，曾經肆州，慶賓惡之，據城不納。

translations.literal: At that time Erzhu Rong's military power grew daily; he once passed through Si Province, and Qingbin detested him and shut the city, refusing entry.
translations.idiomatic: As Erzhu Rong's power grew he once passed through Si Province; Qingbin loathed him and barred the gates.

sentences.zh: 榮襲之，拘還秀容，呼為假父。

translations.literal: Rong attacked, seized him, and brought him back to Xiurong, calling him "foster father."
translations.idiomatic: Rong assaulted the city, took him captive, brought him to Xiurong, and mockingly called him "foster father."

sentences.zh: 後以憂還都。

translations.literal: Later, through grief, he returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He later returned to the capital in distress.

sentences.zh: 尋起為光祿大夫、都督，鎮汝陰。

translations.literal: Soon he was raised as Grand Minister of Splendor and Commander, garrisoning Ruyin.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon reappointed Grand Minister of Splendor and commander garrisoning Ruyin.

sentences.zh: 還朝，卒，贈司空。

translations.literal: On return to court he died and was posthumously made Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He died after returning to court and was posthumously named Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 子瑾。

translations.literal: His son Jin.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Jin.

sentences.zh: 瑾少而敏悟，好學慕善。

translations.literal: Jin from youth was quick and perceptive, loved learning, and admired goodness.
translations.idiomatic: Jin was quick-witted from childhood, loved study, and admired worthy conduct.

sentences.zh: 以國姓門資，稍遷直後。

translations.literal: Because of his surname and family standing he was gradually promoted to Palace Attendant Behind the Throne.
translations.idiomatic: Through his clan name and pedigree he rose to Palace Attendant Behind the Throne.

sentences.zh: 司馬子如執政，瑾娶其甥皮氏為妻，由此除中書舍人。

translations.literal: When Sima Ziru held power, Jin married his niece Lady Pi and thereby was made Secretariat Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: When Sima Ziru governed, Jin married his niece Lady Pi and was made Secretariat Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 後除吏部郎中。

translations.literal: Later he was made Bureau Director of the Ministry of the Civil Service.
translations.idiomatic: He was later made Bureau Director in the Ministry of the Civil Service.

sentences.zh: 齊文襄崩，文宣命瑾在鄴北宮，共高德正典機密。

translations.literal: When Qi Emperor Wenxiang died, Wenxuan ordered Jin at the Northern Palace in Ye, together with Gao Dezheng, to manage secrets.
translations.idiomatic: After Qi Emperor Wenxiang's death, Wenxuan set Jin at Ye's Northern Palace with Gao Dezheng to handle confidential affairs.

sentences.zh: 天保中，累遷七兵尚書侍郎。

translations.literal: In the Tianbao era he was repeatedly promoted to Vice Minister of the Seven Armies.
translations.idiomatic: During Tianbao he rose repeatedly to Vice Minister of the Seven Armies.

sentences.zh: 孝昭輔政，除吏部尚書。

translations.literal: When Xiaozhao assisted in government he was made Minister of the Civil Service.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaozhao took up regency he became Minister of the Civil Service.

sentences.zh: 武成踐祚，趙彥深本子如賓寮，元文遙、和士開並帝鄉故舊，共相薦達，任遇彌重。

translations.literal: When Wucheng ascended the throne, Zhao Yanshen was originally Ziru's guest and follower; Yuan Wenyao and He Shikai were all old acquaintances of the imperial clan; they jointly recommended him, and his appointments grew heavier.
translations.idiomatic: When Wucheng took the throne, Zhao Yanshen had been Ziru's client, and Yuan Wenyao and He Shikai were childhood friends of the imperial house; together they advanced Jin, and his power deepened.

sentences.zh: 又吏部銓衡所歸，事多秘密，由是朝之機事，頗亦預聞。

translations.literal: The Ministry of the Civil Service also controlled appointments, and many matters were secret; thereby he came to hear much of the court's confidential affairs.
translations.idiomatic: As Minister he controlled appointments, many of them secret, and so heard a great deal of the court's inner business.

sentences.zh: 後為尚書右僕射，卒。

translations.literal: Later he was Right Vice Minister of the Masters of Writing and died.
translations.idiomatic: He later became Right Vice Minister of the Masters of Writing and died.

sentences.zh: 武成方在三台饗宴，文遙奏聞，遂命撤樂罷飲。

translations.literal: Wucheng was then feasting at Santai; Wenyao reported the news, and he at once ordered the music withdrawn and drinking stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Wucheng was feasting at Santai when Wenyao announced Jin's death; he immediately ordered the music stopped and the cups set down.

sentences.zh: 瑾外雖通顯，內關風訓；

translations.literal: Outwardly Jin was eminent, yet inwardly his household lacked moral discipline;
translations.idiomatic: Though eminent in public, Jin's household lacked moral discipline;

sentences.zh: 閨門穢雜，為世所鄙。

translations.literal: the inner quarters were foul and mixed, and the world despised him.
translations.idiomatic: his private life was sordid, and the world despised him.

sentences.zh: 有女在室，忽從奔誘，瑾遂以適婦侄皮逸人。

translations.literal: He had a daughter still in the maiden chamber who was suddenly seduced into elopement; Jin then married her to his wife's nephew Pi Yiren.
translations.idiomatic: A daughter still at home was suddenly carried off in elopement; Jin then married her to his wife's nephew Pi Yiren.

sentences.zh: 瑾又通寡嫂元氏。

translations.literal: Jin also had relations with his widowed sister-in-law Lady Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: Jin also lay with his widowed sister-in-law, Lady Yuan.

sentences.zh: 瑾嘗譏吏部郎中頓丘李構云：「郎不稽古。

translations.literal: Jin once mocked the Bureau Director of the Ministry of the Civil Service, Li Gou of Dunqiu, saying, "Sir, you do not study antiquity."
translations.idiomatic: Jin once mocked Li Gou of Dunqiu, bureau director in the Ministry of the Civil Service, saying, "You never study antiquity."

sentences.zh: 」構對令史云：「我實不稽古，未知通嫂得作稽古不？

translations.literal: Gou replied to the clerks, "I truly do not study antiquity—but is bedding one's sister-in-law what you call studying antiquity?"
translations.idiomatic: Gou told the clerks, "It is true I do not study antiquity—but is taking one's sister-in-law what you call antiquity?"

sentences.zh: 」瑾聞大慚。

translations.literal: Jin heard it and was greatly ashamed.
translations.idiomatic: Jin heard this and was deeply shamed.

sentences.zh: 然亦能折節下士，意在引接名流，但不之別也。

translations.literal: Yet he could also humble himself toward scholars, intending to draw in famous men, but could not distinguish them.
translations.idiomatic: He could still humble himself before scholars and meant to gather famous men, yet could not tell quality from pretense.

sentences.zh: 有賈彥始者，儀望雖是儒生，稱堪充聘陳使。

translations.literal: There was one Jia Yanshi whose bearing seemed that of a Confucian scholar and who was said fit to serve as envoy to Chen.
translations.idiomatic: One Jia Yanshi looked the part of a Confucian and was said fit to serve as envoy to Chen.

sentences.zh: 司徒戶曹祖崇儒，文辯俱不足，言將為當世莫及。

translations.literal: Zuchongru of the Household Bureau of the Minister of Education had insufficient literary polish and eloquence, yet spoke as though unmatched in the age.
translations.idiomatic: Zuchongru of the Minister of Education's household bureau lacked literary polish and eloquence yet talked as if unequaled in the age.

sentences.zh: 好學吳人搖脣振足，為人所哂。

translations.literal: He loved to study the Wu people's lip-quivering and foot-shaking and was laughed at by others.
translations.idiomatic: He imitated Wu performers' lip-trembling and foot-jigging and was mocked for it.

sentences.zh: 見人好笑，時論比之寒蟬。

translations.literal: When he saw people he would laugh; contemporaries compared him to the winter cicada.
translations.idiomatic: He laughed at everyone he met; wits compared him to a winter cicada.

sentences.zh: 又少威儀。

translations.literal: He also lacked dignity in youth.
translations.idiomatic: He had little dignity even as a young man.

sentences.zh: 子德載，以蒲鞭責之，便自投井。

translations.literal: His son Dezai, beaten with a cattail whip, threw himself into a well.
translations.idiomatic: His son Dezai, flogged with a cattail whip, threw himself into a well.

sentences.zh: 瑾自臨井上，呼云：「兒出！

translations.literal: Jin himself came to the well and called, "Boy, come out!
translations.idiomatic: Jin came to the well himself and shouted, "Boy, come out!

sentences.zh: 聞者皆笑。

translations.literal: " All who heard laughed.
translations.idiomatic: All who heard burst out laughing.

sentences.zh: 及位任重，便大躁急，省內郎中將論事者，逆即瞋罵。

translations.literal: When his position grew weighty he became very irritable; any bureau director within the ministry who came to discuss business he would at once glare at and revile.
translations.idiomatic: As his power grew he turned furious; any director in his ministry who came to discuss business was met with a glare and a torrent of abuse.

sentences.zh: 既居大選，彌自驕狠。

translations.literal: Once he held the great selection he became all the more arrogant and harsh.
translations.idiomatic: Once he controlled appointments he grew still more arrogant and cruel.

sentences.zh: 皮子賤恃其親通，多所談薦，大有受納。

translations.literal: The Lady Pi's son Jian, relying on his mother's connection, made many recommendations and took heavy bribes.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Pi's son Jian, trading on the family tie, pushed many candidates and took large bribes.

sentences.zh: 瑾死後，其弟靜忿而發之。

translations.literal: After Jin's death his younger brother Jing in anger exposed the matter.
translations.idiomatic: After Jin died his younger brother Jing exposed the affair in anger.

sentences.zh: 子賤坐決鞭二百，配北營州。

translations.literal: Jian was sentenced to two hundred strokes of the rod and assigned to North Ying Province.
translations.idiomatic: Jian was sentenced to two hundred strokes of the rod and sent to North Ying Province.

sentences.zh: 初，瑾為聘梁使，梁人陳昭善相，謂瑾曰：「二十年後當為宰相。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Jin was envoy to Liang to arrange a marriage, the Liang man Chen Zhao was skilled at physiognomy and told Jin, "Twenty years hence you will be chief minister."
translations.idiomatic: When Jin went to Liang as marriage envoy, Chen Zhao of Liang, skilled in physiognomy, told him, "In twenty years you will be chief minister."

sentences.zh: 」瑾出，私謂人曰：「此公宰相後，不過三年，當死。

translations.literal: Jin went out and privately told others, "After this gentleman becomes chief minister, within three years he will die."
translations.idiomatic: Jin left and told others privately, "Three years after that man becomes chief minister, he will die."

sentences.zh: 」昭後為陳使主，兼散騎常侍，至齊。

translations.literal: Zhao later was chief Liang envoy and concurrently Regular Attendant and came to Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao later came to Qi as chief Liang envoy and Regular Attendant.

sentences.zh: 瑾時兼右僕射，鳴騶鐃吹。

translations.literal: Jin was then also Right Vice Minister; drums and clarions sounded before him.
translations.idiomatic: Jin was then Right Vice Minister, with drums and clarions before his carriage.

sentences.zh: 昭復謂人曰：「二年當死。

translations.literal: Zhao again told others, "Within two years he will die."
translations.idiomatic: Zhao again told others, "He will die within two years."

sentences.zh: 」果如言焉。

translations.literal: It came to pass exactly as he said.
translations.idiomatic: Events proved him right.

sentences.zh: 德載位通直散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: Dezai held the post of Regular Attendant of the Palace Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Dezai served as Regular Attendant of the Palace Gate.

sentences.zh: 眷弟地幹，機悟有才藝，馳馬立射五的，時人莫能及。

translations.literal: Juan's younger brother Diggan was quick-witted and had artistic talent; riding at full gallop he could shoot five targets standing—no one of the time could match him.
translations.idiomatic: Juan's younger brother Diggan was clever and gifted in the arts; galloping, he could hit five standing targets—none could equal him.

sentences.zh: 太武時，位庫部尚書，加散騎常侍，領侍輦郎。

translations.literal: In Taiwu's time he was Minister of the Storehouse, added as Regular Attendant, and led the Palace Carriage Attendants.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Taiwu he was Minister of the Storehouse, also Regular Attendant, and led the Palace Carriage Attendants.

sentences.zh: 奉上忠謹，尤善嘲笑。

translations.literal: In serving the throne he was loyal and prudent, and especially skilled at mimicry.
translations.idiomatic: He served the throne with loyal care and excelled at mimicry.

sentences.zh: 太武見其效人舉措，忻悅不能自勝。

translations.literal: Taiwu, seeing him imitate others' gestures, was so delighted he could not contain himself.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taiwu, watching him imitate others' manners, was so delighted he could hardly contain himself.

sentences.zh: 甚見親愛，參軍國大謀。

translations.literal: He was greatly beloved and joined in great plans of state.
translations.idiomatic: He was deeply favored and took part in major state plans.

sentences.zh: 時征平原，試沖車以攻塚。

translations.literal: At that time they were campaigning on the plain and tested battering rams against tombs.
translations.idiomatic: During the campaign on the plain they tested siege engines against tombs.

sentences.zh: 地幹為索所摐，折脅而卒。

translations.literal: Diggan was struck by a cable, his ribs broken, and he died.
translations.idiomatic: A cable struck Diggan, broke his ribs, and killed him.

sentences.zh: 帝親往哭慟，贈中領軍、燕郡公，諡曰惠。

translations.literal: The emperor went in person to mourn with anguish and posthumously made him General of the Central Guard and Duke of Yan Commandery, with posthumous title Hui.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor mourned him in person and posthumously made him General of the Central Guard and Duke of Yan Commandery, with the posthumous title Hui.

sentences.zh: 子長壽，位右曹殿中尚書，賜爵會稽公，卒于涇州刺史。

translations.literal: His son Changshou held the post of Director of the Right Bureau in the Palace Secretariat, was granted Duke of Kuaiji, and died as Governor of Jing Province.
translations.idiomatic: His son Changshou was Director of the Right Bureau in the Palace Secretariat, enfeoffed Duke of Kuaiji, and died as Governor of Jing Province.

sentences.zh: 古真族玄孫聿，字成興，性耿介。

translations.literal: Guzhen's collateral descendant by the sixth generation, Yu, style name Chenxing, was upright by nature.
translations.idiomatic: Guzhen's sixth-generation collateral descendant Yu, styled Chenxing, was stiffly upright.

sentences.zh: 明帝時，為武衛將軍。

translations.literal: In Emperor Ming's time he was General of the Martial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Ming he was General of the Martial Guard.

sentences.zh: 時領軍元叉執權，百寮莫不加敬，聿獨長揖不拜。

translations.literal: At that time the camp commander Yuan Cha held power; the hundred officials all added respect, but Yu alone made a long bow without kneeling.
translations.idiomatic: When camp commander Yuan Cha held power every official bowed low; Yu alone gave a long bow without kneeling.

sentences.zh: 尋出為氵京州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon he went out as Governor of Cen Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon sent out as Governor of Cen Province.

sentences.zh: 氵京州緋色，天下之最，叉送白綾二千匹令染，聿拒不受。

translations.literal: Cen Province's scarlet dye was the finest under Heaven; Cha sent two thousand bolts of white silk to be dyed, and Yu refused to accept them.
translations.idiomatic: Cen Province produced the finest scarlet dye in the realm; Cha sent two thousand bolts of white silk to be dyed, and Yu refused.

sentences.zh: 叉諷御史劾之，驛徵至京。

translations.literal: Cha had the censorate memorialize against him; he was summoned by post to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Cha prompted the censorate to impeach him; couriers summoned him to the capital.

sentences.zh: 覆，無狀。

translations.literal: On review there was no substance.
translations.idiomatic: Review found no case.

sentences.zh: 還任，卒。

translations.literal: He returned to his post and died.
translations.idiomatic: He resumed his post and died.

sentences.zh: 穆崇，代人也，其先代效節於神元、桓、穆之時。

translations.literal: Mu Chong, a man of Dai—his ancestors for generations showed loyalty in the ages of Shenyuan and the Huan and Mu emperors.
translations.idiomatic: Mu Chong came from Dai; his forebears had served loyally since the reigns of Emperor Shenyuan and the Huan and Mu emperors.

sentences.zh: 崇少以盜竊為事。

translations.literal: In youth Chong took theft as his occupation.
translations.idiomatic: In youth Chong lived by theft.

sentences.zh: 道武之居獨孤部，崇往來奉給，時人無及者。

translations.literal: When Daowu dwelt in the Dugu tribe Chong came and went supplying him—no one of the time could match it.
translations.idiomatic: While Daowu stayed with the Dugu tribe Chong supplied him back and forth as no one else could.

sentences.zh: 後劉顯之逆，平文皇帝外孫梁眷知之，密遣崇告道武。

translations.literal: Later, in Liu Xian's rebellion, Emperor Pingwen's maternal grandson Liang Juan learned of it and secretly sent Chong to inform Daowu.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Liu Xian rebelled, Liang Juan—Emperor Pingwen's grandson by a daughter—learned of the plot and secretly sent Chong to warn Daowu.

sentences.zh: 眷謂崇曰：「顯若知之，雖刀劍刳割勿泄也。

translations.literal: Juan told Chong, "If Xian learns of it, though swords cut and carve you, do not reveal it."
translations.idiomatic: Juan told Chong, "If Xian finds out, let them cut you with swords—do not speak."

sentences.zh: 」因以寵妻及所乘良馬付崇曰：「事覺，吾當以此自明。

translations.literal: He therefore gave Chong his favored wife and the fine horse he rode, saying, "If the matter is exposed, I shall use these to clear myself."
translations.idiomatic: He gave Chong his favorite wife and his best horse, saying, "If we are found out, I will clear myself with these."

sentences.zh: 」崇來告難，道武馳如賀蘭部。

translations.literal: Chong came to report the peril; Daowu galloped to the Helan tribe.
translations.idiomatic: Chong brought word of danger; Daowu galloped to the Helan tribe.

sentences.zh: 顯果疑眷泄，將囚之。

translations.literal: Xian indeed suspected Juan had leaked and was about to imprison him.
translations.idiomatic: Xian indeed suspected Juan had leaked the plot and was about to seize him.

sentences.zh: 崇乃唱言：「梁眷不顧恩義，將顯為逆。

translations.literal: Chong then proclaimed aloud, "Liang Juan has forgotten grace and righteousness and would make Xian rebel.
translations.idiomatic: Chong then shouted aloud, "Liang Juan has forgotten grace and would make Xian rebel!

sentences.zh: 今我掠得其妻、馬，足以雪忿。

translations.literal: Today I have seized his wife and horse—enough to settle the score."
translations.idiomatic: I have taken his wife and horse—that settles the score."

sentences.zh: 」顯聞信之。

translations.literal: Xian heard and believed it.
translations.idiomatic: Xian heard him and believed it.

sentences.zh: 窟咄之難，崇外甥于植等與崇謀執道武以應之。

translations.literal: In the turmoil of Kudu, Chong's sister's son Yu Zhi and others with Chong plotted to seize Daowu in response.
translations.idiomatic: During Kudu's revolt, Chong's nephew Yu Zhi and others plotted with Chong to seize Daowu in collusion.

sentences.zh: 崇夜告道武，道武誅植等。

translations.literal: Chong by night informed Daowu; Daowu executed Zhi and the rest.
translations.idiomatic: Chong warned Daowu by night; Daowu executed Zhi and his fellows.

sentences.zh: 北逾陰山，復幸賀蘭部。

translations.literal: North across the Yin Mountains he again came to favor the Helan tribe.
translations.idiomatic: He crossed the Yin Mountains to the north and again took refuge with the Helan tribe.

sentences.zh: 初，道武避窟咄難，遣崇還察人心。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Daowu fled Kudu's turmoil he sent Chong back to observe men's hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, fleeing Kudu's revolt, Daowu had sent Chong back to gauge loyalties.

sentences.zh: 崇留馬與從者，微服入其營。

translations.literal: Chong left his horse with attendants and in plain dress entered their camp.
translations.idiomatic: Chong left his horse with attendants and entered the camp in disguise.

sentences.zh: 會有火光，為舂妾所識，賊皆驚起。

translations.literal: There happened to be firelight; a pounding-woman recognized him and the bandits all sprang up in alarm.
translations.idiomatic: Firelight betrayed him; a woman pounding grain recognized him and the rebels leapt up in alarm.

sentences.zh: 崇求從者不得，因匿坑中，徐乃竊馬奔走。

translations.literal: Chong could not find his attendants; he hid in a pit, then slowly stole a horse and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Unable to find his men, he hid in a pit, then slowly stole a horse and fled.

sentences.zh: 宿于大澤，有白狼向崇號，崇覺悟，馳隨狼奔，遂免難。

translations.literal: He lodged in the great marsh; a white wolf came toward Chong and howled; Chong took warning, galloped after the wolf, and thus escaped peril.
translations.idiomatic: He spent the night in a great marsh; a white wolf howled at him; taking it as a sign, he galloped after the wolf and escaped.

sentences.zh: 道武異之，命崇立祀，子孫世奉焉。

translations.literal: Daowu marveled at it and ordered Chong to establish a shrine; descendants for generations have offered sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Daowu marveled and ordered a shrine to Chong; descendants have sacrificed there ever since.

sentences.zh: 太和中，追錄功臣，以崇配饗。

translations.literal: In the Taihe era, recording meritorious subjects, Chong was granted joint sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: In the Taihe era, when meritorious subjects were recorded, Chong was granted joint sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 崇長子逐留，以功賜爵零陵侯。

translations.literal: Chong's eldest son Zhuliu, for merit, was granted Marquis of Lingling.
translations.idiomatic: Chong's eldest son Zhuliu was enfeoffed Marquis of Lingling for merit.

sentences.zh: 後以罪廢。

translations.literal: Later he was dismissed for crime.
translations.idiomatic: He was later stripped of rank for a crime.

sentences.zh: 子乙，以功賜爵富城公。

translations.literal: His son Yi, for merit, was granted Duke of Fucheng.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yi was enfeoffed Duke of Fucheng for merit.

sentences.zh: 卒於侍中，諡曰靜。

translations.literal: He died as Palace Attendant with posthumous title Jing.
translations.idiomatic: He died as Palace Attendant with the posthumous title Jing.

sentences.zh: 子真，尚長城公主，拜駙馬都尉。

translations.literal: His son Zhen married the Princess of Changcheng and was made Commandant of the Imperial Son-in-Law.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhen married the Princess of Changcheng and became Commandant of the Imperial Son-in-Law.

sentences.zh: 後敕離婚，納文明後姊。

translations.literal: Later an edict ordered divorce; he took the elder sister of the Civilized Empress.
translations.idiomatic: Later an edict forced divorce; he married the Civilized Empress's elder sister.

sentences.zh: 位南部尚書、侍中、卒，諡曰宣。

translations.literal: He held Southern Tribal Grand Chieftain, Palace Attendant, and died with posthumous title Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Southern Tribal Grand Chieftain and Palace Attendant and died with the posthumous title Xuan.

sentences.zh: 孝文追思崇勳，令著作郎韓顯宗與真撰定碑文，建于白登山。

translations.literal: Xiaowen, recalling Chong's merit, ordered the Compiler Han Xianzong and Zhen together to fix the text of a stele and erect it on Mount Bai.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen, remembering Chong's service, ordered Han Xianzong of the Compilation Bureau and Zhen to draft a stele and set it up on Mount Bai.

sentences.zh: 真子泰，本名石洛，孝文賜名焉。

translations.literal: Zhen's son Tai, original name Shiluo, was given his present name by Xiaowen.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen's son Tai, originally named Shiluo, received his new name from Emperor Xiaowen.

sentences.zh: 以功臣子孫，尚章武長公主，拜駙馬都尉，典羽獵四曹事。

translations.literal: As a meritorious descendant he married the Princess of Zhangwu Chang and was made Commandant of the Imperial Son-in-Law, in charge of the Four Bureaus of the Imperial Hunt.
translations.idiomatic: As a meritorious scion he married the Princess of Zhangwu Chang, became Commandant of the Imperial Son-in-Law, and oversaw the Four Bureaus of the Imperial Hunt.

sentences.zh: 後為尚書右僕射、馮翊侯，出為定州刺史。

translations.literal: Later he was Right Vice Minister of the Masters of Writing and Marquis of Fufeng, then went out as Governor of Ding Province.
translations.idiomatic: He later became Right Vice Minister of the Masters of Writing and Marquis of Fufeng, then went out as Governor of Ding Province.

sentences.zh: 初，文明太后幽孝文於別室，將謀黜廢，泰切諫乃止。

translations.literal: At first the Civilized Empress had confined Xiaowen in a separate chamber and was about to plot deposition and removal; Tai remonstrated sharply and she stopped.
translations.idiomatic: When the Civilized Empress first confined Xiaowen apart and plotted to depose him, Tai remonstrated fiercely and she desisted.

sentences.zh: 孝文德之，故寵待隆至。

translations.literal: Xiaowen was grateful for his virtue and therefore favored him to the utmost.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaowen owed him gratitude and favored him accordingly.

sentences.zh: 自陳久病，乞為恆州，許之。

translations.literal: He himself reported long illness and begged for Heng Province; it was granted.
translations.idiomatic: He pleaded chronic illness and asked for Heng Province; the request was granted.

sentences.zh: 泰不願遷都，潛圖叛，乃與定州刺史陸睿及安樂侯元隆等，謀推朔州刺史陽平王頤為主。

translations.literal: Tai did not wish to move the capital and secretly plotted rebellion; with the Governor of Ding Province Lu Rui and the Marquis of Anle Yuan Long and others he plotted to set up the Prince of Yangping, Yi, of Shuozhou, as ruler.
translations.idiomatic: Unwilling to see the capital moved, Tai secretly plotted rebellion with Lu Rui, governor of Ding Province, Yuan Long, Marquis of Anle, and others to make Yi, Prince of Yangping in Shuozhou, their sovereign.

sentences.zh: 頤密表其事，帝乃遣任城王澄發並、肆兵討之。

translations.literal: Yi secretly memorialized the matter; the emperor then sent the Prince of Rencheng, Cheng, to raise Bing and Si troops to attack them.
translations.idiomatic: Yi reported them in a secret memorial; the emperor sent Prince Cheng of Rencheng with troops from Bing and Si to suppress them.

sentences.zh: 澄先遣書侍御史李煥單騎入代，出其不意。

translations.literal: Cheng first sent the Palace Writing Attendant Li Huan alone on horseback into Dai, taking them unawares.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng first sent Li Huan of the Palace Writing Bureau alone on horseback into Dai to catch them off guard.

sentences.zh: 泰等驚駭，計無所出。

translations.literal: Tai and the rest were alarmed and had no plan.
translations.idiomatic: Tai and his party were thrown into panic with no plan left.

sentences.zh: 煥曉喻逆徒，示以禍福，於是凶党離心，莫為之用。

translations.literal: Huan enlightened the rebels with gain and loss, showing fortune and calamity; the wicked party lost heart and none would serve them.
translations.idiomatic: Huan explained fortune and ruin to the rebels; the plotters lost heart and none would fight for them.

sentences.zh: 泰自度必敗，乃率麾下攻煥郭門，不克。

translations.literal: Tai judged he must fail and led his followers to attack Huan at the outer gate but could not take it.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing defeat inevitable, Tai led his men against Huan at the outer gate and failed.

sentences.zh: 走出，為人禽送。

translations.literal: He went out and was seized and sent in.
translations.idiomatic: He fled, was captured, and sent to the capital.

sentences.zh: 孝文幸代，泰等伏誅。

translations.literal: Xiaowen came to Dai; Tai and the rest were executed.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaowen came to Dai; Tai and his fellows were executed.

sentences.zh: 子士儒，字叔賢，徙涼州。

translations.literal: His son Shiru, style name Shuxian, was moved to Liang Province.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shiru, styled Shuxian, was relocated to Liang Province.

sentences.zh: 後得還，為太尉參軍事。

translations.literal: Later he was able to return and was made aide to the Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: He later returned and served as aide to the Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 子子容，少好學，無所不覽。

translations.literal: His son Zirong in youth loved learning and viewed nothing without reading.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zirong loved learning from youth and read whatever he could find.

sentences.zh: 求天下書，逢即寫錄，所得萬餘卷。

translations.literal: He sought books from all under Heaven; whenever he met one he copied it, obtaining more than ten thousand scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: He sought books across the realm, copying every text he found until he had more than ten thousand scrolls.

sentences.zh: 魏末，為兼通直散騎常侍聘梁。

translations.literal: Late in Wei he was concurrently Regular Attendant and envoy to Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Wei he served concurrently as Regular Attendant on an embassy to Liang.

sentences.zh: 齊受禪，卒于司農卿。

translations.literal: When Qi received the mandate he died as Minister of the Imperial Granaries.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi took the mandate he died as Minister of the Imperial Granaries.

sentences.zh: 逐留弟觀，字闥拔，襲崇爵。

translations.literal: Zhuliu's younger brother Guan, style name Tabo, inherited Chong's title.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuliu's younger brother Guan, styled Tabo, inherited Chong's title.

sentences.zh: 少以文藝知名。

translations.literal: In youth he was famed for literary accomplishment.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he was known for literary talent.

sentences.zh: 明元中，位為左衛將軍，綰門下、中書，出納詔命，及訪舊事，未嘗有遺漏。

translations.literal: In Mingyuan's time he was Left General of the Guard, managed the Gate and Secretariat, issued edicts, and inquired into old affairs—never was anything lost.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Mingyuan he was Left General of the Guard, oversaw the Gate and Secretariat, issued edicts, and traced precedents without ever losing a detail.

sentences.zh: 尚宜陽公主，拜駙馬都尉，位太尉。

translations.literal: He married the Princess of Yiyang and was made Commandant of the Imperial Son-in-Law and Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: He married the Princess of Yiyang, became Commandant of the Imperial Son-in-Law, and rose to Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 太武監國，觀為右弼，出則統攝朝政，入則應對左右，事無巨細，皆關決焉。

translations.literal: When Taiwu supervised the state Guan was right-hand aide; going out he commanded the court, coming in he answered at the emperor's side—nothing great or small did not pass through his decision.
translations.idiomatic: While Taiwu supervised the realm Guan was his right-hand man: abroad he directed government, at court he answered the heir—nothing large or small escaped his judgment.

sentences.zh: 終日怡怡，無慍色。

translations.literal: All day he was cheerful, without anger on his face.
translations.idiomatic: He remained cheerful all day, never showing anger.

sentences.zh: 勞謙善誘，不以富貴驕人。

translations.literal: He toiled, was modest, and skillfully guided others, not arrogant because of wealth and rank.
translations.idiomatic: He worked hard, stayed modest, and guided others well, never arrogant in wealth or rank.

sentences.zh: 泰常八年，暴疾薨，年三十五。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Taichang he died suddenly of illness, age thirty-five.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Taichang he died suddenly of illness at thirty-five.

sentences.zh: 明元親臨其喪，悲動左右。

translations.literal: Mingyuan came in person to his funeral and grieved so that those beside him were moved.
translations.idiomatic: Mingyuan attended his funeral in person and grieved until those around him wept.

sentences.zh: 賜以通身隱起金飾棺，喪禮一依安城王叔孫俊故事。

translations.literal: He was granted a coffin of gold with hidden relief over the whole body; funeral rites followed entirely the precedent of the Prince of Ancheng, Shu Sun Jun.
translations.idiomatic: He was given a coffin of gold with relief over the whole body; rites followed the precedent of Prince Shu Sun Jun of Ancheng.

sentences.zh: 贈宜都王，諡曰文成。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Prince of Yidu with posthumous title Wencheng.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Prince of Yidu with the title Wencheng.

sentences.zh: 太武即位，每與群臣談宴，未嘗不歎息殷勤，以為自道武以來，佐命勳臣文武兼濟無及之者。

translations.literal: When Taiwu took the throne, whenever he talked and feasted with the ministers he never failed to sigh with earnest praise, thinking that since Daowu there had been no founding minister combining civil and military like him.
translations.idiomatic: After Taiwu took the throne he never feasted with his ministers without sighing in praise, saying that since Daowu no founding minister had matched Guan's civil and military gifts.

sentences.zh: 子壽襲爵，尚樂陵公主，拜駙馬都尉。

translations.literal: His son Shou inherited the title, married the Princess of Leling, and was made Commandant of the Imperial Son-in-Law.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shou inherited the title, married the Princess of Leling, and became Commandant of the Imperial Son-in-Law.

sentences.zh: 明敏有父風。

translations.literal: Bright and keen, he had his father's manner.
translations.idiomatic: Clever and sharp, he had his father's bearing.

sentences.zh: 太武愛重之，擢為下大夫。

translations.literal: Taiwu loved and valued him and promoted him to Lower Grand Master.
translations.idiomatic: Taiwu cherished him and promoted him to Lower Grand Master.

sentences.zh: 敷奏機辯，有聲內外。

translations.literal: In memorials and debate he was quick and had a voice within and without the court.
translations.idiomatic: His memorials and debate were nimble, and his reputation rang inside and outside the court.

sentences.zh: 遷侍中、中書監、領南部尚書，進爵宜都王，加征東大將軍。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Palace Attendant, Director of the Secretariat, and Southern Tribal Grand Chieftain, advanced to Prince of Yidu, and added General Who Pacifies the East.
translations.idiomatic: He became Palace Attendant, Director of the Secretariat, and Southern Tribal Grand Chieftain, was advanced to Prince of Yidu, and named General Who Pacifies the East.

sentences.zh: 壽辭曰：「臣祖崇，先皇之世，屢逢艱危。

translations.literal: Shou declined, saying, "My grandfather Chong, in the former emperor's age, often met hardship and peril.
translations.idiomatic: Shou declined, saying, "My grandfather Chong, in the former emperor's day, met danger again and again.

sentences.zh: 幸天贊梁眷，誠心先告，故得效功前朝，流福於後。

translations.literal: Fortune favored Liang Juan's sincere early warning, and so he could build merit for the former court and leave blessing for those after.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven favored Liang Juan's loyal warning, so he served the earlier reign and left blessing for later generations.

sentences.zh: 昔陳平受賞，歸功無知。

translations.literal: In antiquity Chen Ping received reward yet attributed the merit to one without knowledge.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity Chen Ping took reward yet credited one who knew nothing.

sentences.zh: 今眷元勳未錄，臣獨奕世受榮，豈惟仰愧古賢，抑亦有虧國典。

translations.literal: Now Juan's founding merit is unrecorded while I alone through generations receive glory—is this not to look up ashamed before the ancient worthies and also to harm the state's statutes?"
translations.idiomatic: Yet Juan's founding service goes unrecorded while I alone inherit glory age after age—should I not blush before the ancients and breach the state's law?"

sentences.zh: 」太武嘉之，乃求眷孫，賜爵郡公。

translations.literal: Taiwu praised this and then sought Juan's grandson and granted him a commandery duke.
translations.idiomatic: Taiwu praised him, sought out Juan's grandson, and enfeoffed him Duke of a commandery.

sentences.zh: 輿駕征涼州，命壽輔景穆，總錄機要，內外聽焉。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage campaigned on Liang Province he ordered Shou to assist Jingmu and oversee all secrets; within and without all obeyed him.
translations.idiomatic: On the Liangzhou campaign the emperor ordered Shou to assist Jingmu and control all confidential affairs; the whole court obeyed him.

sentences.zh: 次雲中，將濟河，帝別禦靜室，召壽及司徒崔浩、尚書李順，謂壽曰：「蠕蠕吳提與牧犍連和，今聞朕征涼州，必來犯塞。

translations.literal: Halting at Yunzhong, about to cross the river, the emperor separately took the quiet chamber and summoned Shou, the Minister of Education Cui Hao, and the Master of Writing Li Shun, telling Shou, "Rouran's Wuti has joined with Mujian in alliance; now hearing that I campaign on Liangzhou he is sure to come violate the border.
translations.idiomatic: At Yunzhong, before crossing the river, the emperor withdrew to a quiet room and summoned Shou, Minister Cui Hao, and Li Shun of the Masters of Writing, telling Shou, "Wuti of the Rouran has allied with Mujian; hearing that I march on Liangzhou he will surely raid the frontier.

sentences.zh: 若伏兵漠南，殄之為易。

translations.literal: If we set ambush south of the desert, destroying them will be easy.
translations.idiomatic: Ambush him south of the desert and destruction will be easy.

sentences.zh: 牧田訖，可分伏要害，以待虜至；

translations.literal: When the pasturelands are finished, you may divide forces and lie in wait at critical points for the barbarians to arrive;
translations.idiomatic: When the pastures are grazed out, post detachments at the key passes and wait for the enemy;

sentences.zh: 引使深入，然後擊之。

translations.literal: draw them deep in, then strike.
translations.idiomatic: lure them deep, then strike.

sentences.zh: 若違朕指授，為虜侵害，朕還斬卿。

translations.literal: If you disobey my command and the barbarians harm us, on my return I shall behead you.
translations.idiomatic: Disobey my orders and let the barbarians harm the realm—I will behead you on my return.

sentences.zh: 崔浩、李順為證，非虛言也。

translations.literal: Cui Hao and Li Shun are witnesses—this is no empty word."
translations.idiomatic: Hao and Shun are witnesses; this is no idle threat."

sentences.zh: 」壽信卜筮言，謂賊不來，竟不設備。

translations.literal: Shou trusted the diviners' words that the enemy would not come and in the end made no preparations.
translations.idiomatic: Shou trusted diviners who said the enemy would not come and made no preparations.

sentences.zh: 吳提果至，京邑大駭。

translations.literal: Wuti indeed arrived and the capital was greatly alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: Wuti came as foretold and the capital was thrown into terror.

sentences.zh: 壽不知所為，欲築西郭門，請景穆避保南山，惠保太后不聽，乃止。

translations.literal: Shou did not know what to do and wished to build the western gate and ask Jingmu to avoid holding Mount Hui on the south for protection; the Empress Huibao would not listen and he stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Shou knew not what to do, proposed sealing the western gate, and asked Jingmu to hold Mount Hui in the south; Empress Huibao refused and he desisted.

sentences.zh: 遣司空長孫道生等擊之。

translations.literal: He sent the Minister of Works Changsun Daosheng and others to attack them.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Minister of Works Changsun Daosheng and others against them.

sentences.zh: 太武還，以無大損傷，故不追咎。

translations.literal: When Taiwu returned, because there was no great harm he did not pursue blame.
translations.idiomatic: Taiwu returned; as damage was slight he did not punish him.

sentences.zh: 景穆監國，壽與崔浩等輔政。

translations.literal: When Jingmu supervised the state Shou with Cui Hao and others assisted in government.
translations.idiomatic: When Jingmu supervised the realm Shou assisted government with Cui Hao and others.

sentences.zh: 人皆敬浩，壽獨陵之。

translations.literal: All respected Hao, but Shou alone towered over him.
translations.idiomatic: All honored Hao, but Shou alone looked down on him.

sentences.zh: 又自恃位任，以人莫己及。

translations.literal: He also relied on his position and office, thinking no one could match him.
translations.idiomatic: He also trusted in rank and office, believing none could equal him.

sentences.zh: 謂其子師曰：「但令吾兒及我，亦足勝人，不須苦教之。

translations.literal: He told his son Shi, "Just let my son and me suffice to surpass others—there is no need to teach him painfully."
translations.idiomatic: He told his son Shi, "Let my son and me alone surpass others—no need to drill him hard."

sentences.zh: 」遇諸父兄弟有如僕隸，夫妻並坐共食，而令諸父餕余。

translations.literal: Toward his uncles and brothers he was like toward slaves; husband and wife sat and ate together while he made his uncles eat leftovers.
translations.idiomatic: He treated uncles and brothers like slaves; he and his wife ate together while making uncles take their leftovers.

sentences.zh: 為時人鄙笑。

translations.literal: People of the time mocked him.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporaries mocked him for it.

sentences.zh: 薨，贈太尉，諡曰文宣。

translations.literal: On his death he was posthumously made Grand Commandant with posthumous title Wenzuan.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously named Grand Commandant with the title Wenzuan.

sentences.zh: 子平國襲爵，尚城陽長公主，拜駙馬都尉、侍中、中書監，為太子四輔。

translations.literal: His son Pingguo inherited the title, married the Princess of Chengyang, and was made Commandant of the Imperial Son-in-Law, Palace Attendant, Director of the Secretariat, and one of the crown prince's four tutors.
translations.idiomatic: His son Pingguo inherited the title, married the Princess of Chengyang, and became Commandant of the Imperial Son-in-Law, Palace Attendant, Director of the Secretariat, and one of the crown prince's four tutors.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 子伏幹襲，尚濟北公主，拜駙馬都尉。

translations.literal: His son Fugan inherited, married the Princess of Jibei, and was made Commandant of the Imperial Son-in-Law.
translations.idiomatic: His son Fugan inherited, married the Princess of Jibei, and became Commandant of the Imperial Son-in-Law.

sentences.zh: 卒，諡曰康。

translations.literal: On his death his posthumous title was Kang.
translations.idiomatic: He died with the posthumous title Kang.

sentences.zh: 無子。

translations.literal: He had no son.
translations.idiomatic: He left no son.

sentences.zh: 伏幹弟羆襲爵，尚新平長公主，拜駙馬都尉、武牢鎮將。

translations.literal: Fugan's younger brother Pi inherited the title, married the Princess of Xinping, and was made Commandant of the Imperial Son-in-Law and garrison general of Wulao.
translations.idiomatic: Fugan's younger brother Pi inherited the title, married the Princess of Xinping, and became Commandant of the Imperial Son-in-Law and garrison general of Wulao.

sentences.zh: 頻以下法致罪，孝文以其勳德之舊，讓而赦之。

translations.literal: Repeatedly he offended through lesser law; Xiaowen, because of his old merit and virtue, reproved him and pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly broke lesser statutes; Emperor Xiaowen, remembering old service, rebuked him and pardoned him each time.

sentences.zh: 轉吐京鎮將，深自克勵。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be commander of the Tujing garrison and strove to discipline himself deeply.
translations.idiomatic: He was made commander of the Tujing garrison and applied himself with strict self-discipline.

sentences.zh: 後改吐京鎮為汾州，仍以羆為刺史。

translations.literal: Later the Tujing garrison was changed to Fenzhou, and Pi was still appointed inspector.
translations.idiomatic: When the Tujing garrison was reorganized as Fenzhou, Pi remained its governor.

sentences.zh: 前吐京太守劉升，在郡甚有威惠，限滿還都，胡人八百餘人詣羆請之。

translations.literal: The former Tujing prefect Liu Sheng had great authority and kindness in the commandery; when his term ended and he returned to the capital, more than eight hundred Hu came to Pi to request him.
translations.idiomatic: Former prefect Liu Sheng had ruled Tujing with authority and kindness; when his term ended and he returned to court, over eight hundred Hu petitioned Pi to bring him back.

sentences.zh: 前定陽令吳平仁亦有恩信，戶增數倍。

translations.literal: The former Dingyang magistrate Wu Pingren also had grace and trust; households increased severalfold.
translations.idiomatic: Former Dingyang magistrate Wu Pingren likewise won trust, and registered households multiplied several times over.

sentences.zh: 羆以吏人懷之，並為表請，孝文皆從焉。

translations.literal: Because officials and people cherished them, Pi memorialized to request both; Emperor Xiaowen approved all.
translations.idiomatic: Pi, seeing how officials and commoners cherished them, memorialized for both appointments, and Emperor Xiaowen granted each request.

sentences.zh: 羆既頻薦升等，所部守令，咸自砥礪，威化大行。

translations.literal: Since Pi had repeatedly recommended Sheng and the rest, the prefects and magistrates under his jurisdiction all sharpened themselves; awe and transformation spread widely.
translations.idiomatic: Pi's repeated recommendations of Sheng and others spurred every prefect and magistrate under him to sharpen their conduct, and his moral authority transformed the region.

sentences.zh: 州人李軌、郭及祖七百餘人詣闕稱羆恩德。

translations.literal: More than seven hundred men of the province, Li Gui and Guo Jizu among them, went to the palace gates to praise Pi's kindness and virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Over seven hundred provincials, including Li Gui and Guo Jizu, went to the capital to praise Pi's kindness and virtue.

sentences.zh: 孝文以羆政和人悅，增秩延限。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowen, because Pi's governance was sound and the people pleased, raised his rank and extended his term.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing sound governance and a content populace, Emperor Xiaowen raised Pi's rank and extended his term of office.

sentences.zh: 後徵為光祿勳，隨例降王為魏郡公。

translations.literal: Later he was summoned as Director of the Imperial Household; according to precedent his princely title was reduced to Duke of Weijun.
