translations.idiomatic: He was later summoned to be Director of the Imperial Household and, by precedent, reduced from prince to Duke of Weijun.

sentences.zh: 累遷侍中、中書監。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Attendant-in-Ordinary and Supervisor of the Palace Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through Attendant-in-Ordinary to Supervisor of the Palace Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 穆泰之反，罷與潛通，赦後事發，削封為編戶。

translations.literal: In Mu Tai's rebellion Pi had secretly communicated with him; after an amnesty the matter came out, and his enfeoffment was stripped—he became a registered commoner.
translations.idiomatic: During Mu Tai's rebellion Pi had secretly communicated with the plotters; after an amnesty exposed the affair, his fief was revoked and he was reduced to common registration.

sentences.zh: 卒於家。

translations.literal: He died at home.
translations.idiomatic: He died at home.

sentences.zh: 宣武時，追贈鎮北將軍、恆州刺史。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Xuanwu he was posthumously made General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Hengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Xuanwu he was posthumously made General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Hengzhou.

sentences.zh: 羆弟亮，字幼輔，早有風度。

translations.literal: Pi's younger brother Liang, courtesy name Youfu, early showed bearing and style.
translations.idiomatic: Pi's younger brother Liang, courtesy name Youfu, showed refinement and presence from youth.

sentences.zh: 獻文時，起家侍御中散。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Xianwen he first entered service as Attendant Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Xianwen he began his career as Attendant Censor.

sentences.zh: 尚中山長公主，拜駙馬都尉，封趙郡王。

translations.literal: He married the Princess of Zhongshan, was appointed Commandant of the Horse Guards, and enfeoffed as Prince of Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: He married the Princess of Zhongshan, was made Commandant of the Horse Guards, and enfeoffed as Prince of Zhao.

sentences.zh: 加侍中，徙封長樂王。

translations.literal: He was made Attendant-in-Ordinary and his fief was changed to Prince of Changle.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Attendant-in-Ordinary and transferred to the princedom of Changle.

sentences.zh: 孝文時，除征南大將軍、領護西戎校尉、仇池鎮將。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Xiaowen he was appointed General Who Pacifies the South, Colonel Protector of the Western Rong, and garrison commander of Chouchi.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Xiaowen he was made General Who Pacifies the South, Colonel Protector of the Western Rong, and commander of the Chouchi garrison.

sentences.zh: 宕昌王梁彌機死，子彌博立。

translations.literal: The King of Dangchang, Liang Miji, died; his son Mibo succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Dangchang king Liang Miji died, and his son Mibo succeeded.

sentences.zh: 為吐谷渾所逼，來奔仇池。

translations.literal: Pressed by Tuyuhun, he came to flee to Chouchi.
translations.idiomatic: Harried by Tuyuhun, Mibo fled to Chouchi for refuge.

sentences.zh: 亮以彌博凶悖，氐羌所棄；

translations.literal: Liang considered Mibo violent and perverse, abandoned by the Di and Qiang;
translations.idiomatic: Liang judged Mibo violent and perverse and abandoned by the Di and Qiang tribes;

sentences.zh: 彌機兄子彌承，戎人歸樂，表請納之。

translations.literal: Miji's elder brother's son Micheng, whom the tribesmen gladly followed, memorialized asking to receive him.
translations.idiomatic: Miji's nephew Micheng, whom the tribes gladly followed, memorialized asking that he be installed instead.

sentences.zh: 孝文從焉。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowen approved.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen agreed.

sentences.zh: 於是擊走吐谷渾，立彌承而還。

translations.literal: Thereupon he routed Tuyuhun, installed Micheng, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: He then drove off Tuyuhun, installed Micheng, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 氐豪楊卜自延興以來，從軍二十一戰，前來鎮將，抑而不聞。

translations.literal: The Di chieftain Yang Bu, since Yanxing, had followed the army through twenty-one battles; former garrison commanders had suppressed him and never reported his merit.
translations.idiomatic: The Di chieftain Yang Bu had fought in twenty-one campaigns since Yanxing, yet successive garrison commanders had suppressed his record and never reported his merit.

sentences.zh: 亮表卜為廣業太守，豪右咸悅，境內大安。

translations.literal: Liang memorialized to make Bu Grand Warden of Guangye; the powerful families were all pleased, and within the borders there was great peace.
translations.idiomatic: Liang memorialized to appoint Bu Grand Warden of Guangye; local magnates were pleased and the region knew great peace.

sentences.zh: 徵為侍中、尚書左僕射。

translations.literal: He was summoned as Attendant-in-Ordinary and Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to be Attendant-in-Ordinary and Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 于時復置司州。

translations.literal: At that time Sizhou was re-established.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Sizhou was re-established.

sentences.zh: 孝文曰：「司州始立，未有寮吏，須立中正，以定選舉。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowen said: "Sizhou has just been founded and has no staff officers; a Rectifier must be appointed to fix selections.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen said, "Sizhou has only just been founded and lacks staff; we must appoint a Rectifier to govern selection."

sentences.zh: 然中正之任，必須德望兼資。

translations.literal: Yet the Rectifier's post requires both virtue and renown.
translations.idiomatic: "That office demands both virtue and public standing."

sentences.zh: 世祖時，崔浩為冀州中正，長孫嵩為司州中正，可謂得人。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Shizu, Cui Hao was Rectifier of Jizhou and Changsun Song Rectifier of Sizhou—truly men well chosen.
translations.idiomatic: "Under Emperor Shizu, Cui Hao was Rectifier of Jizhou and Changsun Song Rectifier of Sizhou—true examples of the right choice."

sentences.zh: 公卿等宜審推舉。

translations.literal: You ministers and grandees should deliberate and recommend carefully.
translations.idiomatic: "You ministers should deliberate and recommend with care."

sentences.zh: 」尚書陸睿舉亮為司州大中正。

translations.literal: Director of the Masters of Writing Lu Rui recommended Liang as Grand Rectifier of Sizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Director Lu Rui recommended Liang as Grand Rectifier of Sizhou.

sentences.zh: 後拜司空，參議律令。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed Minister of Works and took part in deliberating the code of laws.
translations.idiomatic: He was later made Minister of Works and helped draft the code of laws.

sentences.zh: 例降爵為公。

translations.literal: By precedent his noble rank was reduced to duke.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent his title was reduced to duke.

sentences.zh: 時文明太后崩，已過期月，孝文毀瘠猶甚。

translations.literal: When the Empress Dowager Wenming had died, more than a month had passed, yet Emperor Xiaowen was still emaciated from grief.
translations.idiomatic: Though more than a month had passed since Empress Dowager Wenming's death, Emperor Xiaowen remained wasted with grief.

sentences.zh: 亮表請上承金冊遺訓，下稱億兆之心。

translations.literal: Liang memorialized asking that above he uphold the golden-book testament, below he voice the heart of the hundred millions.
translations.idiomatic: Liang memorialized that the emperor should above honor the golden-book testament and below speak for the hearts of the realm.

sentences.zh: 時襲輕服，數禦常膳；

translations.literal: At the time he wore light mourning garb and repeatedly took ordinary meals;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then wore light mourning, took ordinary meals again,

sentences.zh: 修崇郊祠，垂惠咸秩。

translations.literal: restored suburban sacrifices, and extended grace in full measure.
translations.idiomatic: restored suburban sacrifices, and extended grace throughout the ranks.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「苟孝悌之至，無所不通。

translations.literal: An edict said: "If filial piety and brotherly duty reach their utmost, nothing is blocked.
translations.idiomatic: An edict said, "When filial piety and brotherly duty reach their utmost, nothing remains blocked."

sentences.zh: 今飄風亢旱，時雨不降，實由誠慕未濃，幽顯無感也。

translations.literal: Now fierce winds and great drought persist and timely rain does not fall—truly because sincere longing is not yet deep and the hidden and manifest are unmoved.
translations.idiomatic: "Yet fierce winds and drought persist while timely rain withholds itself—because your longing is not yet deep enough for hidden and manifest alike to respond."

sentences.zh: 」尋領太子太傅。

translations.literal: Soon after he also held Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He soon also became Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 時將建太極殿，帝引見群臣于太華殿，曰：「將營殿宇，今欲徙居永樂，以避囂埃。

translations.literal: When the Taiji Hall was to be built, the emperor received the ministers at Taihua Hall and said: "We are about to raise palace halls and now wish to move to Yongle to escape dust and clamor.
translations.idiomatic: When the Taiji Hall was to be built, the emperor received the ministers at Taihua Hall and said, "We are about to raise new halls and will move to Yongle to escape dust and noise."

sentences.zh: 土木雖復無心，毀之能不悽愴！

translations.literal: Though in timber and earth I am again without heart, can destroying them fail to wring grief!
translations.idiomatic: "Though I am no builder at heart, how can tearing them down fail to wring my heart!"

sentences.zh: 今故臨對卿等，與之取別。

translations.literal: Now I therefore face you and take leave together.
translations.idiomatic: "I have called you here to take leave together."

sentences.zh: 此殿乃高宗所制，爰曆顯祖，逮朕沖年，受位於此。

translations.literal: This hall was made by Emperor Gaozong, passed through Emperor Xianzu, and in my tender years I received the throne here.
translations.idiomatic: "This hall was built by Emperor Gaozong, passed through Emperor Xianzu, and in my tender years I received the throne here."

sentences.zh: 但事來奪情，將有改制。

translations.literal: But affairs seize feeling; there will be a change in design.
translations.idiomatic: "But necessity overrides sentiment, and the design must change."

sentences.zh: 仰惟疇昔，唯深悲感。

translations.literal: Looking up to days past, I am only deeply grieved.
translations.idiomatic: "Looking back on those days fills me only with grief."

sentences.zh: 」亮稽首請稽之卜筮。

translations.literal: Liang bowed his head and asked to consult divination by tortoise and milfoil.
translations.idiomatic: Liang bowed and asked to consult the oracle by tortoise and milfoil.

sentences.zh: 又以去歲役作，為功甚多，太廟、明堂，一年便就。

translations.literal: He also said that last year's labor projects had accomplished very much—the Imperial Ancestral Temple and Bright Hall were finished within a year.
translations.idiomatic: He added that last year's labor had already accomplished much—the Imperial Ancestral Temple and Bright Hall had been finished within a year.

sentences.zh: 若仍歲頻興，恐人力雕弊。

translations.literal: If works are raised year after year, I fear human strength will be carved to exhaustion.
translations.idiomatic: "If works are raised year after year, I fear the people will be exhausted."

sentences.zh: 且材幹新伐，願待餘年。

translations.literal: Moreover timber has just been freshly cut; I wish to wait further years.
translations.idiomatic: "Fresh timber has only just been cut; let it season a few more years."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「朕遠覽前王，無不興造。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "I have looked far back at former kings—none failed to build.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "I have looked far back at former kings, and none failed to build."

sentences.zh: 故有周創業，經建靈台；

translations.literal: Therefore when Zhou founded its enterprise it raised the Spirit Terrace;
translations.idiomatic: "When Zhou founded its enterprise it raised the Spirit Terrace;"

sentences.zh: 洪漢受命，未央是作。

translations.literal: when mighty Han received the Mandate, Weiyang was made.
translations.idiomatic: "when mighty Han received the Mandate, Weiyang was built."

sentences.zh: 草創之初，猶尚若此；

translations.literal: At the very founding they were still like this;
translations.idiomatic: "Even at founding they did as much;"

sentences.zh: 況朕承累聖之運，屬太平之基，欲及此時，以就大功。

translations.literal: how much more I, who inherit the fortune of many sages and stand on a foundation of great peace, wishing to seize this time to complete the great work!
translations.idiomatic: "how much more should I, inheriting many sages' fortune upon an age of great peace, seize this moment to finish the great work!"

sentences.zh: 人生定分，修短命也；

translations.literal: Man's allotted portion fixes short and long life;
translations.idiomatic: "A man's allotted span fixes short life or long;"

sentences.zh: 蓍蔡雖智，其如命何！

translations.literal: though milfoil and tortoise may be wise, what can they do against fate!
translations.idiomatic: "milfoil and tortoise may be wise, but what can they do against fate!"

sentences.zh: 當委之分，豈假卜筮。

translations.literal: What is entrusted to one's portion—how could it depend on divination!
translations.idiomatic: "What fate entrusts does not wait on divination!"

sentences.zh: 」移禦永樂宮。

translations.literal: He moved his residence to Yongle Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He moved his residence to Yongle Palace.

sentences.zh: 後帝臨朝堂，嘗謂亮曰：「三代之禮，日出視朝。

translations.literal: Later, when the emperor held court in the Hall of Audience, he once told Liang: "The rites of the Three Dynasties had the sun rise for audience at court.
translations.idiomatic: Later at the Hall of Audience the emperor told Liang, "The Three Dynasties held court as the sun rose."

sentences.zh: 自漢、魏以降，禮儀漸殺。

translations.literal: From Han and Wei downward, ceremony gradually decayed.
translations.idiomatic: "From Han and Wei onward ceremony decayed."

sentences.zh: 《晉令》有朔望集公卿於朝堂而論政事，亦無天子親臨之文。

translations.literal: The Jin ordinance had on the first and fifteenth of the month the gathering of ministers at the Hall of Audience to discuss government, yet there was no text of the Son of Heaven attending in person.
translations.idiomatic: "Jin ordinances gathered ministers on the first and fifteenth to discuss government, yet never required the Son of Heaven in person."

sentences.zh: 今因卿等日中之集，中前，卿等自論政事；

translations.literal: Now because you gather at midday, before noon you yourselves shall discuss government;
translations.idiomatic: "Now that you gather at midday, before noon you shall discuss government among yourselves;"

sentences.zh: 中後，與卿等共議可否。

translations.literal: after noon I shall deliberate with you what may or may not be done.
translations.idiomatic: "after noon I shall deliberate with you what may or may not be done."

sentences.zh: 」遂命讀奏案，帝親決之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he ordered memorials read aloud and personally decided them.
translations.idiomatic: He then had memorials read aloud and decided them himself.

sentences.zh: 及遷都，加武衛大將軍，以本官董攝中軍事。

translations.literal: At the transfer of the capital he was made Grand General of Martial Guards and, in his existing office, supervised central military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: At the capital transfer he was made Grand General of Martial Guards and, retaining his existing posts, oversaw central military affairs.

sentences.zh: 帝南伐，以亮錄尚書事，留鎮洛陽。

translations.literal: When the emperor campaigned south, Liang was put in charge of Masters of Writing affairs and left to guard Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: On the southern campaign the emperor put Liang in charge of Masters of Writing affairs and left him to guard Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 後帝自小平津氵凡舟幸石濟。

translations.literal: Later the emperor from Xiaoping Ford took a boat to Shiji.
translations.idiomatic: Later the emperor took a boat from Xiaoping Ford to Shiji.

sentences.zh: 亮諫曰：「漢帝欲乘舟渡渭，廣德將以首血污車輪，帝乃感而就橋。

translations.literal: Liang admonished: "The Han emperor wished to cross the Wei by boat; Guangde was about to stain the chariot wheels with blood from his head, and the emperor was moved and went to the bridge.
translations.idiomatic: Liang admonished, "When a Han emperor wished to cross the Wei by boat, Guangde threatened to stain the chariot wheels with his own blood, and the emperor was moved to take the bridge instead."

sentences.zh: 渭之小水，猶尚若斯，況洪河有不測之慮。

translations.literal: That small stream of the Wei was still like this—how much more the great river, with its immeasurable peril!
translations.idiomatic: "That small stream of the Wei was still so perilous—how much more this great river, with dangers no man can measure!"

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「司空言是也。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "The Minister of Works speaks rightly.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "The Minister of Works is right."

sentences.zh: 」及羆預穆泰反事覺，亮上表自劾，帝優詔還令攝事。

translations.literal: When Pi's involvement in Mu Tai's rebellion came to light, Liang submitted a memorial impeaching himself; the emperor issued a gracious edict and ordered him to resume his duties.
translations.idiomatic: When Pi's involvement in Mu Tai's rebellion came to light, Liang memorialized to impeach himself; the emperor answered graciously and ordered him to resume his duties.

sentences.zh: 亮固請，久乃許之。

translations.literal: Liang firmly refused; only after long delay was he permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Liang firmly refused; only after long insistence was permission granted.

sentences.zh: 後徙封頓丘郡公，以紹崇爵。

translations.literal: Later his fief was changed to Duke of Dunqiu to continue the ennobled line.
translations.idiomatic: His fief was later changed to Duke of Dunqiu to continue the ennobled line.

sentences.zh: 宣武即位，拜尚書令、司空公。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuanwu took the throne, Liang was appointed Director of the Masters of Writing and Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: At Emperor Xuanwu's accession he was made Director of the Masters of Writing and Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 薨，宣武親臨小斂，贈太尉，諡曰匡。

translations.literal: He died; Emperor Xuanwu personally attended the lesser obsequies, posthumously made him Grand Commandant, posthumous title Kuang.
translations.idiomatic: He died; Emperor Xuanwu personally attended the lesser obsequies, posthumously made him Grand Commandant with the posthumous title Kuang.

sentences.zh: 子紹，字永業，尚琅邪長公主，拜駙馬都尉。

translations.literal: His son Shao, courtesy name Yongye, married the Princess of Langye and was appointed Commandant of the Horse Guards.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shao, courtesy name Yongye, married the Princess of Langye and was made Commandant of the Horse Guards.

sentences.zh: 歷位秘書監、侍中、衛將軍、太常卿、中書令、七兵殿中二尚書。

translations.literal: He held in succession Director of the Secretariat, Attendant-in-Ordinary, General of the Guards, Minister of Ceremonies, Director of the Palace Secretariat, and the two Directors of the Seven Arms Hall.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as Director of the Secretariat, Attendant-in-Ordinary, General of the Guards, Minister of Ceremonies, Director of the Palace Secretariat, and both Directors of the Seven Arms Hall.

sentences.zh: 遭所生憂，免，居喪以孝聞。

translations.literal: He met with mourning for his birth mother, was dismissed, and in residence for mourning was famed for filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: When his birth mother died he left office; his mourning conduct won renown for filial piety.

sentences.zh: 又曆衛大將軍、中書監、侍中，領本邑中正。

translations.literal: He again held Grand General of the Guards, Supervisor of the Palace Secretariat, Attendant-in-Ordinary, and Rectifier of his native commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He later returned as Grand General of the Guards, Supervisor of the Palace Secretariat, Attendant-in-Ordinary, and Rectifier of his native commandery.

sentences.zh: 紹無他才能，而資性方重，罕接賓客，稀造人門。

translations.literal: Shao had no other talent, but his nature was square and weighty; he rarely received guests and seldom crossed others' thresholds.
translations.idiomatic: Shao had no special talent, but his nature was square and grave; he rarely received guests and seldom crossed another man's threshold.

sentences.zh: 領軍元叉當權薰灼，曾往紹宅，紹迎送下階而已。

translations.literal: The commander Yuan Cha, when power blazed, once went to Shao's residence; Shao merely met and escorted him down the steps.
translations.idiomatic: When Commander Yuan Cha's power blazed, he once visited Shao's house; Shao merely met him at the gate and saw him down the steps.

sentences.zh: 時人歎尚之。

translations.literal: Men of the time admired and exalted this.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporaries admired him for it.

sentences.zh: 及靈太后欲黜叉，猶豫未決，紹贊成之。

translations.literal: When the Empress Dowager Ling wished to depose Cha but hesitated and had not decided, Shao urged approval.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Dowager Ling wished to depose Cha but hesitated, Shao urged her to act.

sentences.zh: 以功加特進、侍中。

translations.literal: For this merit he was given special advancement and Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: For this service he received special advancement and Attendant-in-Ordinary.

sentences.zh: 元順與紹同直，嘗因醉入寢所。

translations.literal: Yuan Shun and Shao shared duty; once, drunk, he entered Shao's sleeping quarters.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shun shared duty with Shao; once, drunk, he entered Shao's sleeping quarters.

sentences.zh: 紹擁被而起，正色讓順曰：「老身二十年侍中，與卿先君亟連職事，縱卿後進，何宜相排突也！

translations.literal: Shao threw off the quilt and rose, sternly reproaching Shun: "This old man has been Attendant-in-Ordinary twenty years and with your late father repeatedly held office together; though you are junior in rank, how may you crowd and affront me!
translations.idiomatic: Shao threw off his quilt and rose, sternly reproaching him: "I have been Attendant-in-Ordinary twenty years and served repeatedly with your late father; though you are junior in rank, how dare you crowd and affront me!"

sentences.zh: 」遂謝事還家，詔喻乃起。

translations.literal: He thereupon resigned and returned home; only after an edict admonished him did he rise.
translations.idiomatic: He thereupon resigned and went home; only when an edict admonished him did he return to office.

sentences.zh: 除侍中，托疾未起，故免河陰之害。

translations.literal: He was again made Attendant-in-Ordinary but pleaded illness and did not rise; therefore he escaped the calamity at Heyin.
translations.idiomatic: He was again made Attendant-in-Ordinary but pleaded illness and did not take up the post, and so escaped the massacre at Heyin.

sentences.zh: 莊帝立，爾硃榮征之。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhuang was established, Erzhu Rong summoned him.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhuang was enthroned, Erzhu Rong summoned him.

sentences.zh: 紹以為必死，哭辭家廟。

translations.literal: Shao thought he would surely die and wept before the family shrine in farewell.
translations.idiomatic: Shao believed he would surely die and wept farewell before the family shrine.

sentences.zh: 及見榮，捧手不拜。

translations.literal: When he met Rong he clasped his hands and did not bow.
translations.idiomatic: Meeting Rong, he clasped his hands and did not bow.

sentences.zh: 榮亦矯意禮之，顧謂人曰：「穆紹不虛作大家兒。

translations.literal: Rong also affected courtesy toward him and, turning to others, said: "Mu Shao does not falsely bear the name of a great house.
translations.idiomatic: Rong likewise affected courtesy and said to those around him, "Mu Shao does not falsely bear the name of a great house."

sentences.zh: 」車駕入宮，尋授尚書令、司空，進爵為王，給班劍四十人，仍加侍中。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage entered the palace, he was soon appointed Director of the Masters of Writing and Minister of Works, advanced to prince, given forty halberds of the imperial guard, and still made Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor entered the palace he was soon made Director of the Masters of Writing and Minister of Works, advanced to prince, granted forty halberds of the imperial guard, and retained Attendant-in-Ordinary.

sentences.zh: 時河南尹李獎往詣紹。

translations.literal: At that time the Governor of Henan, Li Jiang, went to call on Shao.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Li Jiang, Governor of Henan, went to call on Shao.

sentences.zh: 獎以紹郡人，謂必致敬。

translations.literal: Jiang, as a fellow townsman of Shao, thought he would surely receive a bow.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang, as Shao's fellow townsman, expected a bow in return.

sentences.zh: 紹又恃封邑是獎國主，匡坐待之，不為動膝。

translations.literal: Shao also relied on his fief being Jiang's sovereign state and sat upright waiting for him, not bending his knees.
translations.idiomatic: Shao also relied on his fief being Jiang's sovereign state and sat upright awaiting him without rising.

sentences.zh: 獎憚其位望，致拜而還。

translations.literal: Jiang feared his rank and standing, performed a bow and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang, fearing his rank and standing, bowed and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 議者兩譏焉。

translations.literal: Critics on both sides reproached them.
translations.idiomatic: Observers reproached them both.

sentences.zh: 未幾，降王，復本爵。

translations.literal: Before long he was reduced from prince and restored to his former noble rank.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was reduced from princely rank and restored to his former title.

sentences.zh: 普泰元年，除驃騎大將軍、開府、青州刺史，加都督。

translations.literal: In the first year of Putai he was appointed General of Agile Cavalry, Opener of the Government, and Inspector of Qingzhou, with overall command added.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Putai he was made General of Agile Cavalry, Opener of the Government, and Inspector of Qingzhou with overall command.

sentences.zh: 未行而薨，贈大將軍、尚書令、太保，諡曰文獻。

translations.literal: Before he set out he died; posthumously made Grand General, Director of the Masters of Writing, and Grand Guardian, posthumous title Wenxian.
translations.idiomatic: He died before setting out and was posthumously made Grand General, Director of the Masters of Writing, and Grand Guardian with the posthumous title Wenxian.

sentences.zh: 子長嵩，字子嶽，襲爵，位光祿少卿。

translations.literal: His son Changsong, courtesy name Ziyue, inherited the fief and held Vice Director of the Imperial Household.
translations.idiomatic: His son Changsong, courtesy name Ziyue, inherited the fief and served as Vice Director of the Imperial Household.

sentences.zh: 平國弟正國，尚長樂公主，拜駙馬都尉。

translations.literal: Pingguo's younger brother Zhengguo married the Princess of Changle and was appointed Commandant of the Horse Guards.
translations.idiomatic: Pingguo's younger brother Zhengguo married the Princess of Changle and was made Commandant of the Horse Guards.

sentences.zh: 正國子平城，早卒。

translations.literal: Zhengguo's son Pingcheng died young.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengguo's son Pingcheng died young.

sentences.zh: 孝文時，始平公主薨于宮，追贈平城駙馬都尉，與公主冥婚。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Xiaowen, when the Princess of Shiping died in the palace, Pingcheng was posthumously made Commandant of the Horse Guards and given a posthumous marriage with the princess.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Xiaowen, when the Princess of Shiping died in the palace, Pingcheng was posthumously made Commandant of the Horse Guards and given a posthumous marriage with her.

sentences.zh: 壽弟多侯，封長寧子，位司衛監。

translations.literal: Shou's younger brother Duohou was enfeoffed as Marquis of Changning and held Supervisor of the Palace Guards.
translations.idiomatic: Shou's younger brother Duohou was enfeoffed as Marquis of Changning and served as Supervisor of the Palace Guards.

sentences.zh: 文成崩，乙渾專權，召司徒陸麗。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wencheng died, Yi Hun monopolized power and summoned Minister of Works Lu Li.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wencheng died, Yi Hun seized power and summoned Minister of Works Lu Li.

sentences.zh: 麗時在溫湯療疾，多侯謂曰：「渾有無君心。

translations.literal: Li was then at a hot spring treating illness; Duohou told him: "Hun has a heart that disowns his lord.
translations.idiomatic: Li was then taking the waters for illness; Duohou told him, "Hun harbors treason against his sovereign."

sentences.zh: 大王，眾所望也，去必危。

translations.literal: Your Highness is what the masses look to; if you go you will surely be in peril.
translations.idiomatic: "Your Highness is whom the realm looks to; if you go you will surely be in peril."

sentences.zh: 宜徐歸而圖之。

translations.literal: You should return slowly and plot against him.
translations.idiomatic: "Return slowly and plot against him."

sentences.zh: 」麗不從，遂為渾害。

translations.literal: Li did not follow and was thereupon killed by Hun.
translations.idiomatic: Li did not listen and was killed by Hun.

sentences.zh: 多侯亦見殺。

translations.literal: Duohou was also killed.
translations.idiomatic: Duohou was killed as well.

sentences.zh: 觀弟翰，平原鎮將、西海王。

translations.literal: Guan's younger brother Han was garrison commander of Pingyuan and Prince of Xihai.
translations.idiomatic: Guan's younger brother Han was garrison commander of Pingyuan and Prince of Xihai.

sentences.zh: 薨。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 子龍兒襲爵，降為公。

translations.literal: His son Long'er inherited the fief and was reduced to duke.
translations.idiomatic: His son Long'er inherited the fief and was reduced to duke.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 子弼，有風格，善自位置，涉獵經史，與長孫承業、陸希道等齊名。

translations.literal: His son Bi had style and presence, knew how to place himself, ranged through the classics and histories, and was famed with Changsun Chengye, Lu Xidao, and others.
translations.idiomatic: His son Bi had style and presence, knew his place, ranged through the classics and histories, and stood equal in renown with Changsun Chengye, Lu Xidao, and others.

sentences.zh: 然而矜己陵物，頗以此損焉。

translations.literal: Yet he prized himself and looked down on others, and lost ground by this.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he prized himself and looked down on others, and suffered for it.

sentences.zh: 孝文定氏族，欲以弼為國子助教，弼辭以為屈。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowen fixed the clans, he wished to make Bi Assistant Director of the Imperial Academy; Bi declined, saying it would be demeaning.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowen fixed the clans he wished to make Bi Assistant Director of the Imperial Academy; Bi declined as beneath his station.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「朕欲敦勵胄子，屈卿先之。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "I wish to encourage and exhort the sons of the nobility; I humble you to go first.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "I wish to encourage the sons of the nobility; I humble you to go first."

sentences.zh: 白玉投泥，豈能相汙！

translations.literal: White jade cast in mud—how can it be stained!
translations.idiomatic: "White jade cast in mud cannot be stained!"

sentences.zh: 」弼曰：「既遇明時，恥沈泥滓。

translations.literal: Bi said: "Having met a bright age, I would be ashamed to sink in the mire.
translations.idiomatic: Bi said, "In a bright age I would be ashamed to sink in the mire."

sentences.zh: 」會司州牧咸陽王禧入。

translations.literal: It happened that Prince of Xianyang Wang Xi entered.
translations.idiomatic: Just then Prince of Xianyang Wang Xi entered.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「朕與卿作州督，舉一主簿。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "I make you and the prince provincial overseers; choose one chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "I appoint you and the prince provincial overseers; choose one chief clerk."

sentences.zh: 」即命弼謁之。

translations.literal: He immediately ordered Bi to pay his respects to him.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately ordered Bi to pay his respects to the prince.

sentences.zh: 因為帝所知。

translations.literal: Thus he came to the emperor's notice.
translations.idiomatic: Thus he came to the emperor's notice.

sentences.zh: 宣武初，為廣平王懷國郎中令，數有匡諫之益。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xuanwu's reign he was Director of the Household of Prince of Guangping Huai and often had the benefit of corrective admonition.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Emperor Xuanwu's reign he was Director of the Household of Prince of Guangping Huai and often offered useful corrective counsel.

sentences.zh: 除中書舍人，卒于華州刺史，諡曰懿。

translations.literal: He was made Palace Secretariat Attendant and died as Inspector of Huazhou, posthumous title Yi.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Palace Secretariat Attendant and died as Inspector of Huazhou with the posthumous title Yi.

sentences.zh: 翰弟顗，有才力。

translations.literal: Han's younger brother Yan had talent and strength.
translations.idiomatic: Han's younger brother Yan had talent and strength.

sentences.zh: 以侍御郎從太武征赫連昌。

translations.literal: As Attendant Cavalry he followed Emperor Taiwu in the campaign against Helian Chang.
translations.idiomatic: As Attendant Cavalry he followed Emperor Taiwu against Helian Chang.

sentences.zh: 勇冠一時，賜爵泥陽子，拜司衛監。

translations.literal: His courage led the age; he was given the fief of Marquis of Niyang and appointed Supervisor of the Palace Guards.
translations.idiomatic: His courage led the age; he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Niyang and made Supervisor of the Palace Guards.

sentences.zh: 從太武由崞山，有虎突出，顗搏而獲之。

translations.literal: Later he followed Emperor Taiwu from Mount Guo; a tiger burst out and Yan wrestled and captured it.
translations.idiomatic: Later, following Emperor Taiwu from Mount Guo, a tiger burst out and Yan wrestled it down.

sentences.zh: 帝歎曰：「《詩》云：'有力如虎 '，顗乃過之！

translations.literal: The emperor sighed: "The Odes say, 'Strong as a tiger'—Yan surpasses it!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor exclaimed, "The Odes say, 'Strong as a tiger'—Yan surpasses even that!"

sentences.zh: 」後從征白龍，討蠕蠕，以功進爵建安公。

translations.literal: Later he followed campaigns against Bailong and in punitive expeditions against the Rouran; for merit his rank was advanced to Duke of Jian'an.
translations.idiomatic: He later campaigned at Bailong and against the Rouran and, for merit, was advanced to Duke of Jian'an.

sentences.zh: 後拜殿中尚書，出鎮涼州。

translations.literal: Later he was made Director of the Palace Secretariat and went out to garrison Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was later made Director of the Palace Secretariat and sent to garrison Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 還，加散騎常侍、領太倉尚書。

translations.literal: On his return he was made Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary and concurrent Director of the Imperial Granary.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was made Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary and concurrent Director of the Imperial Granary.

sentences.zh: 文成時，為征西大將軍，督諸軍西征吐谷渾。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Wencheng he was General Who Pacifies the West and supervised all armies in the western expedition against Tuyuhun.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Wencheng he was General Who Pacifies the West and commanded the western expedition against Tuyuhun.

sentences.zh: 坐擊賊不進，免官爵，徙邊。

translations.literal: Because in striking the enemy he did not advance, he was stripped of office and rank and banished to the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Because he failed to press the attack, he was stripped of office and rank and banished to the frontier.

sentences.zh: 文成以顗著勳前朝，徵為內都大官。

translations.literal: Emperor Wencheng, because Yan had shown merit in the former dynasty, summoned him as Grand Inner Custodian.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wencheng, remembering Yan's merit under the former emperor, recalled him as Grand Inner Custodian.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈征西大將軍、建安王，諡曰康。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously made General Who Pacifies the West and Prince of Jian'an, posthumous title Kang.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made General Who Pacifies the West and Prince of Jian'an with the posthumous title Kang.

sentences.zh: 子寄生襲。

translations.literal: His son Jisheng inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jisheng inherited.

sentences.zh: 崇宗人醜善，道武初，率部歸附，與崇同心戮力，捍禦左右。

translations.literal: A clansman of Chong, Choushan, at the beginning of Emperor Daowu led his division to submit and, with Chong, joined hearts and shared strength to defend left and right.
translations.idiomatic: Chong's clansman Choushan, at the beginning of Emperor Daowu, led his division to submit and, with Chong, fought side by side in defense of the throne.

sentences.zh: 拜天部大人，居東蕃。

translations.literal: He was appointed Grandee of the Heavenly Division and dwelt in the Eastern Barbarian quarter.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Grandee of the Heavenly Division and dwelt in the eastern quarter.

sentences.zh: 子莫提，從平中原，位相州刺史、假陵陽侯。

translations.literal: His son Moti followed in pacifying the Central Plains and held Inspector of Xiangzhou and Acting Marquis of Lingyang.
translations.idiomatic: His son Moti followed in pacifying the Central Plains and held Inspector of Xiangzhou with acting rank as Marquis of Lingyang.

sentences.zh: 其子孫位亦通顯。

translations.literal: His descendants' offices were also illustrious.
translations.idiomatic: His descendants likewise rose to illustrious office.

sentences.zh: 奚斤，代人也，世典馬牧。

translations.literal: Xi Jin was a man of Dai; his family for generations managed the imperial horse herds.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Jin was a man of Dai; his family had for generations managed the imperial horse herds.

sentences.zh: 父簞。

translations.literal: His father Dan.
translations.idiomatic: His father was Dan.

sentences.zh: 有寵于昭成皇帝。

translations.literal: He had favor with Emperor Zhaocheng.
translations.idiomatic: He enjoyed favor under Emperor Zhaocheng.

sentences.zh: 時國有良馬曰騶駠，一夜忽逸。

translations.literal: At that time the state had a fine horse called Zouliu; one night it suddenly bolted.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the state owned a fine horse called Zouliu; one night it suddenly bolted.

sentences.zh: 後知南部大人劉庫仁所盜，養於窟室。

translations.literal: Later it was learned that the Southern Division Grandee Liu Kuren had stolen it and kept it in a cave dwelling.
translations.idiomatic: It was later learned that Southern Division Grandee Liu Kuren had stolen it and hidden it in a cave dwelling.

sentences.zh: 簞聞而馳往取馬，庫仁以國甥恃寵，慚而逆擊簞，簞捽其發落，傷其一乳。

translations.literal: Dan heard and galloped to take the horse; Kuren, as the emperor's nephew-in-law relying on favor, was ashamed and turned to strike Dan; Dan seized his hair and tore it out, wounding one nipple.
translations.idiomatic: Dan heard and galloped to reclaim the horse; Kuren, the emperor's nephew-in-law relying on favor, struck back in shame; Dan seized his hair and tore it out, wounding one nipple.

sentences.zh: 及符堅使庫仁與衛辰分領國部，簞懼，遂奔衛辰。

translations.literal: When Fu Jian sent Kuren and Wei Chen to divide and lead the state's tribes, Dan was afraid and fled to Wei Chen.
translations.idiomatic: When Fu Jian sent Kuren and Wei Chen to divide leadership of the tribes, Dan fled in fear to Wei Chen.

sentences.zh: 及道武滅衛辰，簞晚乃得歸，故名位後於舊臣。

translations.literal: When Emperor Daowu destroyed Wei Chen, Dan only then was able to return, and therefore his name and rank came after the old ministers.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Daowu destroyed Wei Chen, Dan returned only late, and therefore his rank fell behind the old ministers.

sentences.zh: 斤機辯有識度。

translations.literal: Jin was quick-witted and had judgment.
translations.idiomatic: Jin was quick-witted and discerning.

sentences.zh: 登國初，與長孫肥等俱統禁兵。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Dengguo he, with Changsun Fei and others, together commanded the forbidden troops.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Dengguo he, with Changsun Fei and others, jointly commanded the forbidden troops.

sentences.zh: 後以為侍郎，親近左右。

translations.literal: Later he was made Attendant and drew near at the emperor's left and right.
translations.idiomatic: He was later made Attendant and served close at the emperor's side.

sentences.zh: 從征慕容寶於參合。

translations.literal: He followed the campaign against Murong Bao at Canhe.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the campaign against Murong Bao at Canhe.

sentences.zh: 皇始初，拜越騎校尉，典宿衛禁旅。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Huangshi he was appointed Colonel of Valiant Cavalry and managed the night guards and forbidden brigades.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Huangshi he was made Colonel of Valiant Cavalry and managed the night guards and forbidden brigades.

sentences.zh: 車駕還京師，博陵、勃海、章武諸郡群盜並起，斤與略陽西元遵等討平之。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage returned to the capital, bandits rose together in Boling, Bohai, and Zhangwu commanderies; Jin, with Lueyang's Xi Yuanzun and others, pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor returned to the capital, bandits rose in Boling, Bohai, and Zhangwu; Jin, with Xi Yuanzun of Lueyang and others, suppressed them.

sentences.zh: 從征，破高車諸部。

translations.literal: He followed campaigns and broke the Gaoche tribes.
translations.idiomatic: He followed campaigns and broke the Gaoche tribes.

sentences.zh: 又破庫狄、宥連部，徙其別部諸落于塞南。

translations.literal: He again broke the Kudi and Youlian tribes and moved their separate tribal settlements south of the passes.
translations.idiomatic: He again broke the Kudi and Youlian tribes and moved their separate settlements south of the passes.

sentences.zh: 又進擊侯莫陳部，至大峨穀，置戍而還。

translations.literal: He advanced again against the Houmochen tribe, reached Da'e Valley, set a garrison, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced again against the Houmochen, reached Da'e Valley, set a garrison, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 遷都水使者，出為晉兵將軍、幽州刺史，賜爵山陽侯。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Commissioner of the Imperial Waterways, went out as General of Jin Troops and Inspector of Youzhou, and enfeoffed as Marquis of Shanyang.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Commissioner of the Imperial Waterways, sent out as General of Jin Troops and Inspector of Youzhou, and enfeoffed as Marquis of Shanyang.

sentences.zh: 明元即位，為鄭兵將軍。

translations.literal: When Emperor Mingyuan took the throne, he was General of Zheng Troops.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Mingyuan took the throne, he was General of Zheng Troops.

sentences.zh: 詔以斤世忠孝，贈其父簞長寧子。

translations.literal: An edict said that because Jin's family for generations had been loyal and filial, his father Dan was posthumously given Marquis of Changning.
translations.idiomatic: An edict noted that Jin's family had been loyal and filial for generations and posthumously enfeoffed his father Dan as Marquis of Changning.

sentences.zh: 明元幸雲中，斤留守京師。

translations.literal: When Emperor Mingyuan visited Yunzhong, Jin remained to guard the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Mingyuan visited Yunzhong, Jin remained to guard the capital.

sentences.zh: 昌黎王慕容伯兒謀反，斤召入天安殿東廡下，誅之。

translations.literal: Prince of Changli Murong Bo'er plotted rebellion; Jin summoned him into the eastern wing of Tian'an Hall and executed him.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Changli Murong Bo'er plotted rebellion; Jin summoned him to the eastern wing of Tian'an Hall and executed him.

sentences.zh: 詔與南平公長孫嵩等俱坐朝堂，錄決囚徒。

translations.literal: An edict ordered him, with Duke of Nanping Changsun Song and others, to sit together in the Hall of Audience and record and decide on prisoners.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered him, with Duke of Nanping Changsun Song and others, to sit in the Hall of Audience and decide criminal cases.

sentences.zh: 明元大閱於東郊。

translations.literal: Emperor Mingyuan held a great review at the eastern suburb.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Mingyuan held a great military review at the eastern suburb.

sentences.zh: 講武，以斤行左丞相，大蒐于石會山。

translations.literal: In martial exercises Jin acted as Left Chancellor; a great hunt was held at Mount Shihui.
translations.idiomatic: At the martial exercises Jin acted as Left Chancellor; a great hunt was held at Mount Shihui.

sentences.zh: 車駕西巡，詔斤先驅，討越勒部于鹿那山，大破之。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage toured the west, an edict ordered Jin to go ahead as vanguard and attack the Yuele tribe at Mount Lu'na, routing them greatly.
translations.idiomatic: On the western tour an edict ordered Jin ahead as vanguard to attack the Yuele at Mount Lu'na, routing them decisively.

sentences.zh: 又詔斤與長孫嵩等八人坐止車門左，聽理萬機。

translations.literal: Another edict ordered Jin, with Changsun Song and eight others, to sit to the left of the stopping chariot gate and hear and decide the myriad affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Another edict seated Jin with Changsun Song and eight others to the left of the stopping-chariot gate to hear and decide the myriad affairs of state.

sentences.zh: 拜天部大人，進爵為公。

translations.literal: He was appointed Grandee of the Heavenly Division and his rank advanced to duke.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Grandee of the Heavenly Division and advanced to duke.

sentences.zh: 命斤出入乘軺軒，備威儀導從。

translations.literal: He was ordered to enter and leave in a light carriage with full guard of honor and attendants.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to enter and leave in a light carriage with full guard and attendants.

sentences.zh: 太武之為皇太子，臨朝聽政，以斤為左輔。

translations.literal: When Emperor Taiwu was crown prince and held court to hear government, Jin was made Left Assistant.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taiwu was crown prince and held court, Jin was made Left Assistant.

sentences.zh: 宋廢主義符立，其國內離阻。

translations.literal: When the deposed ruler of Song Yifu was established, his state was inwardly divided and obstructed.
translations.idiomatic: When Song's deposed ruler Yifu was restored, that realm was inwardly divided and obstructed.

sentences.zh: 乃遣斤收河南地，假斤節，都督前鋒諸軍事、司空、晉兵大將軍、行揚州刺史。

translations.literal: Thereupon Jin was sent to recover the lands south of the Yellow River; he was given credentials, overall command of vanguard military affairs, Minister of Works, Grand General of Jin Troops, and acting Inspector of Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Jin was then sent to recover lands south of the Yellow River with credentials, overall command of the vanguard, the post of Minister of Works, Grand General of Jin Troops, and acting Inspector of Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 率吳兵將軍公孫表等南征。

translations.literal: He led General of Wu Troops Gongsun Biao and others south.
translations.idiomatic: He led General of Wu Troops Gongsun Biao and others south.

sentences.zh: 用表計攻滑台，不拔，求濟師。

translations.literal: Using Biao's plan he attacked Huatai but could not take it and requested reinforcements.
translations.idiomatic: Following Biao's plan he attacked Huatai but could not take it and requested reinforcements.

sentences.zh: 帝怒其不先略地，切責之。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry that he had not first seized territory and sharply reproached him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, angry that he had not first seized territory, sharply reproached him.

sentences.zh: 乃親南巡，次中山，斤自滑台趣洛陽，長驅至武牢，遂平兗、豫諸郡。

translations.literal: He then personally toured south, halting at Zhongshan; Jin from Huatai pressed toward Luoyang, driving hard to Wulao, and thereupon pacified Yan and Yu commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: He then toured south in person, halting at Zhongshan; Jin pressed from Huatai toward Luoyang, driving hard to Wulao, and pacified Yan and Yu commanderies.

sentences.zh: 還圍武牢。

translations.literal: He returned to besiege Wulao.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to besiege Wulao.

sentences.zh: 及武牢潰，斤置守宰以撫之。

translations.literal: When Wulao fell, Jin set garrison officials to pacify it.
translations.idiomatic: When Wulao fell, Jin set garrison officials to pacify the region.

sentences.zh: 自魏初大將行兵，唯長孫嵩拒宋武，斤征河南，獨給漏刻及十二牙旗。

translations.literal: From the beginning of Wei, when great generals marched, only Changsun Song resisted Song Wu; when Jin campaigned in Henan he alone was given water clocks and the twelve yak-tail banners.
translations.idiomatic: Since the founding of Wei, when great generals took the field only Changsun Song had resisted Song Wu; when Jin campaigned in Henan he alone received water clocks and the twelve yak-tail banners.

sentences.zh: 太武即位，進爵宜城王，仍為司空。

translations.literal: When Emperor Taiwu took the throne, his rank was advanced to Prince of Yicheng and he still held Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taiwu took the throne, Jin was advanced to Prince of Yicheng while retaining Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 太武征赫連昌，遣斤率義兵將軍封禮等襲蒲阪。

translations.literal: When Emperor Taiwu campaigned against Helian Chang he sent Jin to lead General of Righteous Troops Feng Li and others in a surprise attack on Puban.
translations.idiomatic: Campaigning against Helian Chang, the emperor sent Jin to lead General of Righteous Troops Feng Li and others in a surprise attack on Puban.

sentences.zh: 斤又西據長城，秦、雍氐羌皆來歸附。

translations.literal: Jin again held the Long Wall in the west; the Di and Qiang of Qin and Yong all came to submit.
translations.idiomatic: Jin again held the Long Wall in the west, and the Di and Qiang of Qin and Yong all submitted.

sentences.zh: 斤與赫連定相持，累戰破定。

translations.literal: Jin stood in stalemate with Helian Ding, repeatedly fighting and breaking Ding.
translations.idiomatic: Jin stood in stalemate with Helian Ding, repeatedly fighting and defeating him.

sentences.zh: 定聞昌敗，走上邽。

translations.literal: When Ding heard that Chang had been defeated, he fled up to Shanggui.
translations.idiomatic: When Ding heard Chang had been defeated, he fled to Shanggui.

sentences.zh: 斤追至雍，不及而還。

translations.literal: Jin pursued to Yong but could not overtake him and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Jin pursued to Yong but could not overtake him and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 詔斤班師，斤請因其危平之，乃進討安定。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Jin to withdraw the army; Jin asked to take advantage of their peril to pacify them and advanced to attack Anding.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered withdrawal; Jin asked to exploit their peril and pacify them, and advanced on Anding.

sentences.zh: 昌退保平涼，斤屯軍安定，以糧竭馬死，深壘自固。

translations.literal: Chang retreated to defend Pingliang; Jin encamped at Anding, and because grain was exhausted and horses died, he deeply fortified and held firm.
translations.idiomatic: Chang retreated to defend Pingliang; Jin encamped at Anding; when grain ran out and horses died, he fortified deeply and held firm.

sentences.zh: 監軍侍御史安頡擊昌，禽之。

translations.literal: Supervising Army Attendant Censor An Gu attacked Chang and captured him.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Army Attendant Censor An Gu attacked Chang and captured him.

sentences.zh: 昌眾復立昌弟定為主，守平涼。

translations.literal: Chang's troops again made Chang's younger brother Ding master and defended Pingliang.
translations.idiomatic: Chang's troops then made his younger brother Ding master and defended Pingliang.

sentences.zh: 斤恥以元帥而禽昌之功更不在己，乃舍輜重，追定於平涼。

translations.literal: Jin was ashamed that as commander-in-chief the merit of capturing Chang was not his; he abandoned baggage and pursued Ding at Pingliang.
translations.idiomatic: Jin was ashamed that as commander-in-chief the capture of Chang was not his merit; he abandoned baggage and pursued Ding at Pingliang.

sentences.zh: 定眾將出，會一小將有罪，亡入賊，具告其實。

translations.literal: Ding's troops were about to sally forth when a minor officer guilty of a fault fled into the enemy and fully reported the truth.
translations.idiomatic: Ding's troops were about to sally when a minor officer guilty of a fault fled to the enemy and told all.

sentences.zh: 定知斤軍無糧乏水，乃邀斤前後。

translations.literal: Ding knew Jin's army lacked grain and water and thereupon intercepted Jin front and rear.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that Jin's army lacked grain and water, Ding intercepted him front and rear.

sentences.zh: 斤眾大潰，斤及將娥清、劉拔為定所禽。

translations.literal: Jin's troops were greatly routed; Jin and the generals E Qing and Liu Ba were captured by Ding.
translations.idiomatic: Jin's army was routed; Jin and his generals E Qing and Liu Ba were captured by Ding.

sentences.zh: 後太武克平涼，斤等得歸。

translations.literal: Later when Emperor Taiwu took Pingliang, Jin and the rest were able to return.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Emperor Taiwu took Pingliang, Jin and the others were released and returned.

sentences.zh: 免為宰人，使負酒食從駕還京師以辱之。

translations.literal: He was demoted to cook and made to carry wine and food, following the imperial carriage back to the capital to shame him.
translations.idiomatic: He was demoted to palace cook and made to carry wine and food behind the imperial carriage back to the capital as a public shame.

sentences.zh: 尋拜安東將軍，降爵為公。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed General Who Pacifies the East and his noble rank was reduced to duke.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made General Who Pacifies the East and reduced to duke.

sentences.zh: 太延初，為衛尉，改為恆農王。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taiyan he was Commandant of the Guards and changed to Prince of Hengnong.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Taiyan he was Commandant of the Guards and made Prince of Hengnong.

sentences.zh: 後為萬騎大將軍。

translations.literal: Later he was Grand General of Ten Thousand Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: He later became Grand General of Ten Thousand Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 太武議伐涼州，斤等三十餘人議以為不可，帝不從。

translations.literal: When Emperor Taiwu deliberated attacking Liangzhou, Jin and more than thirty others argued it could not be done; the emperor did not follow.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taiwu deliberated attacking Liangzhou, Jin and more than thirty others argued against it; the emperor overruled them.

sentences.zh: 涼州平，以戰功賜僮隸七十戶。

translations.literal: When Liangzhou was pacified, for battle merit he was given seventy households of bond servants.
translations.idiomatic: When Liangzhou fell, he was rewarded with seventy households of bond servants for battle merit.

sentences.zh: 又以斤元老，賜安車，平決獄訟，諮訪朝政。

translations.literal: Also because Jin was an elder of the founding age, he was given a comfort carriage, decided prison cases, and was consulted on court government.
translations.idiomatic: As an elder of the founding age he was also given a comfort carriage, authority to decide lawsuits, and a voice in court government.

sentences.zh: 斤聰辯強識，善於談論，遠說先朝故事，雖未皆是，時有所得，聽者歎美之。

translations.literal: Jin was clever, argumentative, and of strong memory; skilled in discourse, when speaking at length of former-dynasty affairs, though not all were correct, he sometimes hit the mark, and listeners sighed and praised.
translations.idiomatic: Clever, argumentative, and retentive, Jin was skilled in discourse; recounting former-dynasty affairs he did not always get things right, yet often struck home, and listeners marveled.

sentences.zh: 每議大政，多見從用，朝廷稱焉。

translations.literal: Whenever great government was deliberated, his views were often followed; the court praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever great affairs of state were debated, his counsel was often followed, and the court praised him.

sentences.zh: 真君九年，薨，時年八十九。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Zhenjun he died, aged eighty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Zhenjun he died at eighty-nine.

sentences.zh: 太武親臨哀慟，諡曰昭王。

translations.literal: Emperor Taiwu personally came to mourn in grief, posthumous title Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taiwu came in person to mourn him deeply and gave him the posthumous title Zhao.

sentences.zh: 斤有數十婦，子男二十餘人。

translations.literal: Jin had several tens of wives and more than twenty sons.
translations.idiomatic: Jin had several dozen wives and more than twenty sons.

sentences.zh: 長子他觀襲爵。

translations.literal: His eldest son Taguan inherited the fief.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Taguan inherited the fief.

sentences.zh: 太武曰：「斤西征之敗，國有常刑。

translations.literal: Emperor Taiwu said: "Jin's defeat in the western expedition carries the state's regular penalty.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taiwu said, "Jin's defeat on the western expedition carried the state's regular penalty."

sentences.zh: 以其佐命先朝，故復其爵秩，將收孟明之效。

translations.literal: Because he aided the Mandate in the former dynasty, his rank and office were restored, intending to reap the effect of Meng Ming.
translations.idiomatic: "Because he aided the Mandate under the former emperor, his rank and office were restored, intending to reap the redemption of Meng Ming."

sentences.zh: 今斤終其天年，君臣之分全矣。

translations.literal: Now Jin has ended his natural years—the distinction of ruler and minister is complete.
translations.idiomatic: "Now Jin has ended his natural span, and the distinction of ruler and minister stands complete."

sentences.zh: 」於是降他觀爵為公。

translations.literal: Thereupon Taguan's rank was reduced to duke.
translations.idiomatic: Taguan's title was thereupon reduced to duke.

sentences.zh: 傳國至孫緒，無子，國除。

translations.literal: The fief passed to his grandson Xu; he had no son and the state was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: The fief passed to his grandson Xu; Xu had no heir and the line was abolished.

sentences.zh: 太和中，孝文追錄先朝功臣，以斤配饗廟庭。

translations.literal: In the Taihe era Emperor Xiaowen posthumously recorded the meritorious ministers of the former dynasty and granted Jin a share in the temple sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: In the Taihe era Emperor Xiaowen recorded the meritorious ministers of former reigns and granted Jin a share in the temple sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 宣武繼絕世，以緒弟子監紹其後。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanwu continued an extinguished line, making Xu's nephew Jian heir to continue the descent.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanwu continued the extinguished line by making Xu's nephew Jian heir to the house.

sentences.zh: 叔孫建，代人也。

translations.literal: Shu Sun Jian was a man of Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Shu Sun Jian was a man of Dai.

sentences.zh: 父骨，為昭成母王太后所養，與皇子同列。

translations.literal: His father Gu was reared by Empress Dowager Wang, mother of Emperor Zhaocheng, and ranked with the princes.
translations.idiomatic: His father Gu was reared by Empress Dowager Wang, mother of Emperor Zhaocheng, and ranked with the imperial sons.

sentences.zh: 建少以智通著稱。

translations.literal: Jian in youth was famed for penetrating intelligence.
translations.idiomatic: Jian was famed from youth for penetrating intelligence.

sentences.zh: 道武之幸賀蘭部，常從左右。

translations.literal: When Emperor Daowu visited the Helan tribe he constantly followed at left and right.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Daowu visited the Helan tribe he constantly attended him.

sentences.zh: 登國初，為外朝大人，與安同等十三人迭典庶事，參軍國之謀。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Dengguo he was Outer Court Grandee; with An Tong and twelve others he took turns managing common affairs and took part in the state's stratagems.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Dengguo he was Outer Court Grandee; with An Tong and twelve others he took turns managing routine affairs and advised on state strategy.

sentences.zh: 隨秦王觚使慕容垂，曆六載乃還。

translations.literal: He followed Prince of Qin Gu as envoy to Murong Chui; six years passed before he returned.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Prince of Qin Gu as envoy to Murong Chui and was away six years before returning.

sentences.zh: 累遷中領軍，賜爵安平公，出為并州刺史。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Central Camp Commander, enfeoffed as Duke of Ping'an, and sent out as Inspector of Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Central Camp Commander, was enfeoffed as Duke of Ping'an, and sent out as Inspector of Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 後以公事免，守鄴城園。

translations.literal: Later he was dismissed for a public matter and guarded the Ye city gardens.
translations.idiomatic: He was later dismissed over a public matter and guarded the Ye city gardens.

sentences.zh: 明元即位，念前功，以為正直將軍、相州刺史。

translations.literal: When Emperor Mingyuan took the throne, remembering former merit, he was made General of Uprightness and Inspector of Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Mingyuan took the throne, remembering his former service, he was made General of Uprightness and Inspector of Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 饑胡劉武等聚黨叛。

translations.literal: Starving Hu Liu Wu and others gathered factions and rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: Starving Hu led by Liu Wu gathered factions and rebelled.

sentences.zh: 明元假建前號、安平公，督公孫表等以討武。

translations.literal: Emperor Mingyuan lent Jian his former title and Duke of Ping'an and ordered Gongsun Biao and others to attack Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Mingyuan restored Jian's former title as Duke of Ping'an and ordered Gongsun Biao and others to attack Wu.

sentences.zh: 斬首萬餘級，餘眾奔走，投沚水死，水為不流。

translations.literal: More than ten thousand heads were cut off; the rest fled in panic, threw themselves into the Zhi River and drowned—the water ceased to flow.
translations.idiomatic: More than ten thousand heads were taken; the rest fled into the Zhi River and drowned until the water ceased to flow.

sentences.zh: 晉將劉裕伐姚泓，令其部將王仲德為前鋒，將逼滑台。

translations.literal: The Jin general Liu Yu attacked Yao Hong and ordered his subordinate Wang Zhongde as vanguard to press on Huatai.
translations.idiomatic: Jin general Liu Yu attacked Yao Hong and sent his subordinate Wang Zhongde as vanguard against Huatai.

sentences.zh: 兗州刺史尉建率所部棄城濟河。

translations.literal: Inspector of Yanzhou Wei Jian led his command and abandoned the city to cross the river.
translations.idiomatic: Inspector of Yanzhou Wei Jian led his forces to abandon the city and cross the river.

sentences.zh: 仲德遂入滑台，乃宣言曰：「晉本意欲以布帛七萬匹假道于魏，不謂魏之守將便爾棄城。

translations.literal: Zhongde thereupon entered Huatai and proclaimed: "Jin's original intent was to borrow passage with seventy thousand bolts of cloth and silk from Wei—not expecting Wei's garrison commander to abandon the city so readily.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongde entered Huatai and proclaimed, "Jin meant only to borrow passage with seventy thousand bolts of cloth and silk from Wei—not expecting Wei's commander to abandon the city at once."

sentences.zh: 」明元聞之，詔建度河曜威，斬尉建，投其屍於河。

translations.literal: When Emperor Mingyuan heard, he ordered Jian to cross the river and display might, executed Wei Jian, and cast his corpse into the river.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Mingyuan heard, he ordered Jian to cross the river and display Wei power, executed Wei Jian, and cast his corpse into the river.

sentences.zh: 呼仲德軍人與語，詰其侵境之狀。

translations.literal: He called Zhongde's soldiers to speak and questioned them on the offense of invading the borders.
translations.idiomatic: He summoned Zhongde's soldiers, questioned them, and rebuked their border violation.

sentences.zh: 尋遷廣阿鎮將，威名甚著。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to garrison commander of Guang'a; his martial name was very renowned.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to garrison commander of Guang'a, where his martial renown was great.

sentences.zh: 久之，除使持節、都督前鋒諸軍事、楚兵將軍、徐州刺史。

translations.literal: After long service he was made Bearer of the Staff, Commander-in-Chief of the Vanguard, General of Chu Troops, and Inspector of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After long service he was made Bearer of the Staff, Commander-in-Chief of the Vanguard, General of Chu Troops, and Inspector of Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 率眾自平原濟河，徇下青、兗諸郡。

translations.literal: He led troops across the river from Pingyuan and swept down the commanderies of Qing and Yan.
translations.idiomatic: He led troops across the river from Pingyuan and swept the commanderies of Qing and Yan.

sentences.zh: 遂東入青州，圍宋刺史竺夔于東陽城。

translations.literal: He then entered Qingzhou eastward and besieged Song Inspector Zhu Kui at Dongyang city.
translations.idiomatic: He then entered Qingzhou and besieged Song inspector Zhu Kui at Dongyang.

sentences.zh: 宋遣將檀道濟、王仲德救夔，建不克而還。

translations.literal: Song sent the generals Tan Daoji and Wang Zhongde to rescue Kui; Jian could not take the city and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Song sent Tan Daoji and Wang Zhongde to relieve Kui; Jian failed to take the city and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 以功賜爵壽光公。

translations.literal: For merit he was given the fief of Duke of Shouguang.
translations.idiomatic: For merit he was enfeoffed as Duke of Shouguang.

sentences.zh: 與汝陰公長孫道生濟河而南，仲德等自清入濟，東走青州。

translations.literal: With Duke of Ruyin Changsun Daosheng he crossed the river south; Zhongde and the rest from Qing entered Ji eastward and fled toward Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: With Duke of Ruyin Changsun Daosheng he crossed south; Zhongde and others entered Ji from Qing and fled east toward Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 太武以建威名南震，為宋所憚，除平原鎮大將，封丹楊王，加征南大將軍。

translations.literal: Emperor Taiwu, because Jian's martial name shook the south and Song feared him, made him Grand General of the Pingyuan Garrison, enfeoffed as Prince of Danyang, and added General Who Pacifies the South.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taiwu, because Jian's name shook the south and Song feared him, made him Grand General of the Pingyuan Garrison, Prince of Danyang, and General Who Pacifies the South.

sentences.zh: 先是，簡幽、易以南戍兵集於河上，一道討洛陽，一道攻滑台。

translations.literal: Earlier, frontier troops south of You and Yi were gathered on the river—one route to attack Luoyang, one to attack Huatai.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, frontier troops south of You and Yi had been gathered on the river—one column to strike Luoyang, one Huatai.

sentences.zh: 宋將檀道濟、王仲德救滑台。

translations.literal: Song generals Tan Daoji and Wang Zhongde rescued Huatai.
translations.idiomatic: Song generals Tan Daoji and Wang Zhongde marched to relieve Huatai.

sentences.zh: 建與汝陰公道生拒擊之。

translations.literal: Jian and Duke of Ruyin Daosheng resisted and struck them.
translations.idiomatic: Jian and Duke of Ruyin Daosheng met and repulsed them.

sentences.zh: 建分軍挾戰，縱輕騎邀其前後，焚燒穀草以絕其糧道。

translations.literal: Jian divided the army for flanking battle, sent light cavalry to intercept front and rear, and burned grain and fodder to cut their supply route.
translations.idiomatic: Jian divided his forces for flanking attacks, sent light cavalry to harry front and rear, and burned grain and fodder to sever their supply line.

sentences.zh: 道濟兵饑，叛者相繼。

translations.literal: Daoji's troops were hungry; deserters followed one after another.
translations.idiomatic: Daoji's army starved; deserters followed one after another.

sentences.zh: 由是安頡等得拔滑台。

translations.literal: By this An Gu and the rest were able to lift the siege of Huatai.
translations.idiomatic: Thus An Gu and the others were able to lift the siege of Huatai.

sentences.zh: 建沈敏多智，東西征伐，常為謀主，容貌清整，號曰嚴明。

translations.literal: Jian was deep, keen, and full of stratagems; in eastern and western campaigns he was constantly chief planner; his bearing was clear and ordered, and he was styled Severe and Bright.
translations.idiomatic: Deep, keen, and full of stratagems, Jian was constantly chief planner in eastern and western campaigns; clear in bearing, he was styled Severe and Bright.

sentences.zh: 又雅尚人倫，禮賢愛士。

translations.literal: He also elegantly valued human relations, honored the worthy, and loved scholars.
translations.idiomatic: He also valued human relations, honored the worthy, and loved scholars.

sentences.zh: 在平原十餘年，綏懷內外，甚得邊稱。

translations.literal: At Pingyuan for more than ten years he soothed within and without and won great border praise.
translations.idiomatic: At Pingyuan for more than ten years he soothed subjects within and without and won high praise on the frontier.

sentences.zh: 魏初名將，鮮有及之。

translations.literal: Among the famed generals at the beginning of Wei, few could match him.
translations.idiomatic: Among Wei's early famed generals, few could match him.

sentences.zh: 南方憚其威略，青、兗輟不為寇。

translations.literal: The south feared his martial stratagems; Qing and Yan for long ceased raiding.
translations.idiomatic: The south feared his stratagems, and Qing and Yan long ceased their raids.

sentences.zh: 太延三年，薨，時年七十三，諡曰襄，賜葬金陵。

translations.literal: In the third year of Taiyan he died, aged seventy-three; posthumous title Xiang, burial granted at Jinling.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Taiyan he died at seventy-three with the posthumous title Xiang and burial at Jinling.

sentences.zh: 初，俊卒，明元命其妻桓氏曰：「夫生既共榮，沒宜同穴，能殉葬者，可任意。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Jun died, Emperor Mingyuan told his wife Lady Huan: "In life you shared glory together; in death you should share one tomb—whoever can follow in burial may do as she wishes.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Jun died, Emperor Mingyuan told his wife Lady Huan, "In life you shared glory; in death you should share one tomb—whoever will follow him in burial may choose freely."

sentences.zh: 」桓氏乃縊，遂合葬焉。

translations.literal: Lady Huan thereupon strangled herself and they were buried together.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Huan strangled herself and they were buried together.

sentences.zh: 俊既為安城公，俊弟鄰襲父爵，降為丹楊公，位尚書令、涼州鎮大將。

translations.literal: Since Jun had been Duke of Ancheng, Jun's younger brother Lin inherited their father's fief, was reduced to Duke of Danyang, and held Director of the Masters of Writing and Grand General of the Liangzhou Garrison.
translations.idiomatic: Jun having been Duke of Ancheng, his younger brother Lin inherited their father's fief, was reduced to Duke of Danyang, and served as Director of the Masters of Writing and Grand General of the Liangzhou Garrison.

sentences.zh: 與鎮副將奚牧，並以貴戚子弟，競貪財貨，遂相糾，坐誅。

translations.literal: With the garrison deputy Xi Mu, both as noble kinsmen's sons, they vied in greed for wealth and goods, then denounced each other, and were executed for the offense.
translations.idiomatic: He and garrison deputy Xi Mu, both noble kinsmen, vied in greed for wealth, denounced each other, and were executed.

sentences.zh: 安同，遼東胡人也。

translations.literal: An Tong was a man of the Hu of Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: An Tong was a man of the Hu of Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 其先祖曰世高，漢時以安息王侍子入洛。

translations.literal: His remote ancestor was called Shigao; in Han times he entered Luoyang as the attendant son of the King of Parthia.
translations.idiomatic: His remote ancestor Shigao entered Luoyang in Han times as the attendant son of the King of Parthia.

sentences.zh: 曆魏至晉，避亂遼東，遂家焉。

translations.literal: Through Wei to Jin, fleeing turmoil he went to Liaodong and there made his home.
translations.idiomatic: Through Wei and Jin, fleeing turmoil, he settled in Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 父屈，仕慕容痈。

translations.literal: His father Qu served Murong Yong.
translations.idiomatic: His father Qu served Murong Yong.

sentences.zh: 痈為苻堅所滅，屈友人公孫眷妹沒入苻氏宮，出賜劉庫仁為妻，庫仁貴寵之。

translations.literal: When Yong was destroyed by Fu Jian, Qu's friend Gongsun Juan's younger sister was taken into the Fu clan palace and later given out to Liu Kuren as wife; Kuren favored and cherished her.
translations.idiomatic: When Yong fell to Fu Jian, Qu's friend Gongsun Juan's younger sister was taken into Fu Jian's palace and later given to Liu Kuren as wife; Kuren favored her deeply.

sentences.zh: 同隨眷商販，見道武有濟世才，遂留奉侍。

translations.literal: Tong followed Juan in trade; seeing that Emperor Daowu had talent to save the age, he remained to serve.
translations.idiomatic: Tong followed Juan in trade, saw in Emperor Daowu the talent to save the age, and remained to serve him.

sentences.zh: 性端嚴明惠，好長者之言。

translations.literal: His nature was upright, severe, bright, and discerning; he loved the words of elders.
translations.idiomatic: Upright, severe, bright, and discerning, he loved the counsel of elders.

sentences.zh: 登國初，道武徵兵于慕容垂，同頻使稱旨。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Dengguo Emperor Daowu raised troops from Murong Chui; Tong repeatedly went as envoy and pleased the intent.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Dengguo, when Emperor Daowu raised troops from Murong Chui, Tong repeatedly went as envoy and pleased him.

sentences.zh: 為外朝大人，與和跋等出入禁中，迭典庶事。

translations.literal: He was Outer Court Grandee; with He Ba and others he entered and left within the forbidden precincts, taking turns managing common affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was Outer Court Grandee; with He Ba and others he moved within the forbidden precincts, taking turns managing routine affairs.

sentences.zh: 從征姚平于柴壁，姚興悉眾救平，同進計曰：「汾東有蒙坑，東西三百餘里，徑路不通。

translations.literal: Following the campaign against Yao Ping at Chaibi, when Yao Xing mustered all his forces to rescue Ping, Tong advanced a plan: "East of the Fen there is Meng Pit, more than three hundred li east to west, with no path through.
translations.idiomatic: Campaigning against Yao Ping at Chaibi, when Yao Xing mustered all his forces to rescue Ping, Tong proposed, "East of the Fen lies Meng Pit, more than three hundred li across with no path through."

sentences.zh: 姚興來，必從汾西，乘高臨下，直至柴壁，如此則寇內外勢接。

translations.literal: When Yao Xing comes he is sure to come by the west of the Fen, taking the high ground to look down, going straight to Chaibi—thus the enemy within and without will join their strength.
translations.idiomatic: "When Yao Xing comes he will surely take the west bank, hold the high ground, and strike straight for Chaibi—then enemy within and without will join strength."

sentences.zh: 宜截汾為南北浮橋，乘西岸築圍。

translations.literal: We should cut the Fen into north and south floating bridges and build a rampart on the west bank.
translations.idiomatic: "Cut the Fen with north and south floating bridges and build a rampart on the west bank."

sentences.zh: 西圍既固，賊至無所施其智力矣。

translations.literal: Once the western rampart is firm, when the enemy arrives he will have nowhere to deploy his stratagems.
translations.idiomatic: "Once the western rampart stands firm, the enemy will have nowhere to deploy his stratagems."

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: They followed this.
translations.idiomatic: They followed his plan.

sentences.zh: 興果視平屠滅而不能救。

translations.literal: Xing indeed watched Ping slaughtered and could not save him.
translations.idiomatic: Xing indeed watched Ping destroyed and could not save him.

sentences.zh: 以謀功，賜爵北新侯。

translations.literal: For stratagem merit he was given the fief of Marquis of Beixin.
translations.idiomatic: For this stratagem he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Beixin.

sentences.zh: 太武監國，臨朝聽政，以同為左輔。

translations.literal: When Emperor Taiwu supervised the state and held court to hear government, Tong was made Left Assistant.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taiwu supervised the state and held court, Tong was made Left Assistant.

sentences.zh: 及即位，進爵高陽公，冀青二州刺史。

translations.literal: At his accession his rank was advanced to Duke of Gaoyang and he held the two provinces Ji and Qing.
translations.idiomatic: At his accession Tong was advanced to Duke of Gaoyang and governed Ji and Qing.

sentences.zh: 同長子屈，明元時，典太倉事，盜官粳米數石，欲以養親。

translations.literal: Tong's eldest son Qu, under Emperor Mingyuan, managed Imperial Granary affairs; he stole several piculs of official husked rice, intending to support his parents.
translations.idiomatic: Tong's eldest son Qu, under Emperor Mingyuan, managed the Imperial Granary; he stole several piculs of official rice to support his parents.

sentences.zh: 同大怒，求戮屈，自劾不能訓子。

translations.literal: Tong was greatly angry, asked to execute Qu, and impeached himself for failing to instruct his son.
translations.idiomatic: Tong was furious, asked to execute Qu, and impeached himself for failing to instruct his son.

sentences.zh: 帝嘉而恕之，遂詔長給米。

translations.literal: The emperor praised this and pardoned him; thereupon an edict long supplied rice.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised his integrity and pardoned Qu, then ordered rice supplied in perpetuity.

sentences.zh: 同在官明察，長於校閱，家法修整，為世所稱。

translations.literal: Tong in office was bright in perception and skilled at auditing; his household rules were strict and ordered, and he was praised by the age.
translations.idiomatic: In office Tong was bright in perception and skilled at audit; his household rules were strict, and the age praised him.

sentences.zh: 及在冀州，年老，頗殖財貨，大興寺塔，為百姓所苦。

translations.literal: When he was in Jizhou, old in years, he greatly accumulated wealth and goods and raised temple towers on a grand scale, to the suffering of the common people.
translations.idiomatic: In Jizhou, old in years, he amassed wealth and raised temple towers on a grand scale, to the people's suffering.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈高陽王，諡曰恭惠。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously made Prince of Gaoyang, posthumous title Gonghui.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made Prince of Gaoyang with the posthumous title Gonghui.

sentences.zh: 屈弟原，雅性矜嚴，沈勇多智略。

translations.literal: Qu's younger brother Yuan had an elegant nature, stern and reserved, deep courage, and many stratagems.
translations.idiomatic: Qu's younger brother Yuan was elegant, stern, reserved, deeply courageous, and full of stratagems.

sentences.zh: 明元時，為獵郎，出監雲中軍事。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Mingyuan he was Hunt Officer and went out to supervise Yunzhong military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Mingyuan he was Hunt Officer and supervised Yunzhong military affairs.

sentences.zh: 時赫連屈丐犯河西，原以數十騎擊之，殺十餘人。

translations.literal: At that time Helian Qubuqin invaded Hexi; Yuan with several tens of horsemen struck him and killed more than ten men.
translations.idiomatic: When Helian Qubuqin invaded Hexi, Yuan with several dozen horsemen struck him and killed more than ten of his men.

sentences.zh: 帝以原輕敵，違節度，加罪。

translations.literal: The emperor, because Yuan treated the enemy lightly and violated command, added punishment.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor punished him for treating the enemy lightly and violating command.

sentences.zh: 然知原驍勇，遂任以為將，鎮雲中。

translations.literal: Yet knowing Yuan was fierce and brave, he then entrusted him as general and garrisoned Yunzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Yet knowing Yuan's fierceness, he then entrusted him as general at Yunzhong.

sentences.zh: 蠕蠕犯塞，原輒破之，以功賜爵武原侯，加魯兵將軍。

translations.literal: When the Rouran invaded the frontier, Yuan repeatedly broke them; for merit he was given Marquis of Wuyuan and made General of Lu Troops.
translations.idiomatic: When the Rouran invaded the frontier Yuan repeatedly routed them and, for merit, was made Marquis of Wuyuan and General of Lu Troops.

sentences.zh: 弟頡，辯慧多策略，最有父風。

translations.literal: His younger brother Yan was eloquent, discerning, and full of strategy, most having his father's manner.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Yan was eloquent, discerning, and strategic, most in his father's manner.

sentences.zh: 明元初，為內侍長，令察舉百寮，糾刺奸慝，無所回避。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Mingyuan he was Chief Inner Attendant and ordered to inspect and recommend the hundred offices, impeaching wickedness, sparing none.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Emperor Mingyuan he was Chief Inner Attendant, ordered to inspect the hundred offices and impeach wickedness without sparing anyone.

sentences.zh: 嘗告其父陰事，帝以為忠，特親寵之。

translations.literal: He once reported his father's private affairs; the emperor considered this loyal and especially favored him.
translations.idiomatic: He once reported his father's private misconduct; the emperor deemed this loyalty and favored him especially.

sentences.zh: 宜城王奚斤自長安追赫連昌至安定，頡為監軍侍御史。

translations.literal: When Prince of Yicheng Xi Jin from Chang'an pursued Helian Chang to Anding, Yan was Supervising Army Attendant Censor.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince of Yicheng Xi Jin pursued Helian Chang from Chang'an to Anding, Yan was Supervising Army Attendant Censor.

sentences.zh: 斤以馬多疫死，士眾乏糧，乃築壘自固。

translations.literal: Jin, because many horses died of plague and the soldiers lacked grain, fortified deeply and held firm.
translations.idiomatic: Jin, with plague killing many horses and grain running short, fortified deeply and held firm.

sentences.zh: 遣太僕丘堆等督租於人間，為昌所敗。

translations.literal: He sent the Grand Master of the Stud Qiu Dui and others to supervise tax grain among the people; they were defeated by Chang.
