translations.idiomatic: He sent Grand Master of the Stud Qiu Dui and others to levy grain among the people; Chang defeated them.

sentences.zh: 昌遂驕矜，日來侵掠。

translations.literal: Chang thereupon grew arrogant and proud, coming daily to raid and plunder.
translations.idiomatic: Chang then grew arrogant and came daily to raid and plunder.

sentences.zh: 頡曰：「等死，當戰死！

translations.literal: Ji said: "Equal death—one ought to die fighting!
translations.idiomatic: Ji said, "We all face death—let it be in battle!

sentences.zh: 寧可坐受囚乎？

translations.literal: How can one sit and accept imprisonment?
translations.idiomatic: Would you rather sit here and be taken prisoner?"

sentences.zh: 」斤猶以馬死為辭。

translations.literal: Jin still used the horses' deaths as his excuse.
translations.idiomatic: Jin still pleaded the epidemic among the horses.

sentences.zh: 頡乃陰與尉眷等謀，選騎焉。

translations.literal: Ji then secretly plotted with Wei Juan and others, and selected horsemen.
translations.idiomatic: Ji secretly conspired with Wei Juan and the rest and picked out cavalry.

sentences.zh: 昌來攻壘，頡出應之，昌馬蹶而墜。

translations.literal: When Chang came to attack the stockade, Ji went out to meet him; Chang's horse stumbled and he fell.
translations.idiomatic: Chang attacked the fort; Ji rode out to meet him, and Chang's horse stumbled and threw him.

sentences.zh: 頡禽昌送京師，賜爵西平公，代堆統攝諸軍。

translations.literal: Ji captured Chang and sent him to the capital, was enfeoffed Duke of Xiping, and replaced Dui in commanding all armies.
translations.idiomatic: Ji seized Chang and sent him to the capital, was made Duke of Xiping, and replaced Qiu Dui as commander of the armies.

sentences.zh: 赫連定將復入長安，詔頡鎮蒲阪以拒之。

translations.literal: He Lian Ding was about to re-enter Chang'an; an edict ordered Ji to garrison Puban to resist him.
translations.idiomatic: As He Lian Ding prepared to retake Chang'an, Ji was ordered to hold Puban against him.

sentences.zh: 宋將到彥之寇河南以援定，列守南岸，至於衡關。

translations.literal: The Song general Dao Yanzhi raided Henan to aid Ding, arraying guards along the south bank as far as Heng Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Song's Dao Yanzhi invaded Henan in Ding's support and lined the south bank with garrisons as far as Heng Pass.

sentences.zh: 太武西征定，以頡為冠軍將軍，督諸軍擊彥之。

translations.literal: Emperor Taiwu campaigned west against Ding and made Ji Champion General, directing the armies against Yanzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taiwu marched west against Ding and made Ji Champion General to command the attack on Yanzhi.

sentences.zh: 遂濟河，攻洛陽，拔之。

translations.literal: He then crossed the river, attacked Luoyang, and took it.
translations.idiomatic: He crossed the Yellow River, stormed Luoyang, and took it.

sentences.zh: 進攻武牢，武牢潰。

translations.literal: Advancing to attack Wulao, Wulao collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: He pressed Wulao until its defenses gave way.

sentences.zh: 又與琅邪王司馬楚之平滑台，禽宋將硃修之、李元德及東郡太守申謨。

translations.literal: He also, with Prince of Langye Sima Chuzhi, pacified Pingtai, capturing the Song generals Zhu Xiuzhi and Li Yuande and the Administrator of Dongjun Shen Mo.
translations.idiomatic: With Prince of Langye Sima Chuzhi he pacified Pingtai and took the Song generals Zhu Xiuzhi and Li Yuande and Dongjun's administrator Shen Mo.

sentences.zh: 乃振旅還京師，進爵為王。

translations.literal: Then he led the army back to the capital and was advanced to princely rank.
translations.idiomatic: He led the army home and was raised to princely rank.

sentences.zh: 卒，諡曰襄。

translations.literal: He died; posthumous name Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously titled Xiang.

sentences.zh: 頡為將善綏士眾，及卒，宋士卒降者無不嘆惜。

translations.literal: Ji as a general was skilled at soothing troops; when he died, every Song soldier who had surrendered sighed in regret.
translations.idiomatic: Ji knew how to steady his men; at his death not one surrendered Song soldier failed to mourn him.

sentences.zh: 庾業延，代人也，後賜名嶽。

translations.literal: Yu Yeyan, a man of Dai, was later granted the name Yue.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Yeyan of Dai was later granted the name Yue.

sentences.zh: 其父及兄和辰世典畜牧，稍轉中部大人。

translations.literal: His father and elder brother Hechen for generations managed the imperial herds and were gradually promoted to Grand Chief of the Central Tribes.
translations.idiomatic: His father and elder brother Hechen had long overseen the royal herds and rose to Grand Chief of the Central Tribes.

sentences.zh: 昭成崩，苻氏內侮，事難之間，收斂畜產，富擬國君。

translations.literal: When Zhaocheng died, the Fu clan made trouble within; amid the crisis he gathered livestock until his wealth rivaled a ruler's.
translations.idiomatic: At Zhaocheng's death, as Former Qin stirred within, he amassed herds in the turmoil until his wealth rivaled a prince's.

sentences.zh: 劉顯謀逆，道武外幸，和辰奉獻明太后歸道武，又得其資用。

translations.literal: Liu Xian plotted rebellion; Emperor Daowu was away on campaign, and Hechen escorted the Empress Dowager Xianming back to Daowu and also supplied his resources.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Xian rebelled, Hechen brought Empress Dowager Xianming to Daowu on his western tour and furnished supplies.

sentences.zh: 以和辰為內侍長。

translations.literal: Hechen was made Chief Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Hechen was made Chief Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 和辰分別公私舊畜，頗不會旨，道武由是恨之。

translations.literal: Hechen divided public and private herds of old and greatly missed the mark; Daowu therefore resented him.
translations.idiomatic: Hechen's sorting of old public and private herds missed the mark, and Daowu came to hate him.

sentences.zh: 岳獨恭慎修謹，善處危難之間，道武嘉之。

translations.literal: Yue alone was respectful, cautious, and disciplined, skilled in perilous moments, and Daowu praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Yue alone was respectful and steady in crisis; Daowu praised him.

sentences.zh: 與王建等俱為外朝大人，參預軍國。

translations.literal: With Wang Jian and others he became a senior minister of the outer court and took part in military and state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He joined Wang Jian and others as senior ministers of the outer court in military and civil counsel.

sentences.zh: 從平中原，拜安遠將軍。

translations.literal: Following the pacification of the Central Plains, he was appointed General Who Pacifies the Distance.
translations.idiomatic: After the Central Plains were pacified he was made General Who Pacifies the Distance.

sentences.zh: 官軍之警于柏肆也，賀蘭部帥附力眷、紇突鄰部帥匿物尼、紇奚部帥叱奴根等聞之，反于陰館。

translations.literal: When the army was alarmed at Baixi, the Helan chieftain Fuli Juan, the Getuolin chieftain Niwuni, and the Hexi chieftain Chinugen heard of it and rebelled at Yinguan.
translations.idiomatic: When the army was checked at Baixi, Helan Fuli Juan, Getuolin Niwuni, and Hexi Chinugen rebelled at Yinguan.

sentences.zh: 南安西元順討之，不克，詔嶽。

translations.literal: The Western Pacification General Yuan Shun of Nan'an attacked them but could not overcome them; an edict summoned Yue.
translations.idiomatic: Nan'an's Western Pacification General Yuan Shun failed to crush them, and Yue was summoned.

sentences.zh: 討破離石叛胡帥呼延鐵、西河叛胡帥張崇等。

translations.literal: He defeated and broke the rebel Hu chieftains of Lishi, Huyan Tie, and Xihe, Zhang Chong, and others.
translations.idiomatic: He broke the Lishi rebel Hu leader Huyan Tie, the Xihe rebel Hu leader Zhang Chong, and others.

sentences.zh: 以功賜爵西昌公，遷鄴行台。

translations.literal: For merit he was enfeoffed Duke of Xichang and transferred to the Ye Field Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: For merit he was made Duke of Xichang and moved to the Ye Field Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 岳為將有謀略，士眾服其智勇，名冠諸將。

translations.literal: Yue as a general had stratagem; troops obeyed his wisdom and courage, and his name stood above the generals.
translations.idiomatic: As a commander he was resourceful; men followed his wit and courage, and his name topped the generals.

sentences.zh: 及罷鄴行台，以所統六郡置相州，即拜岳為刺史。

translations.literal: When the Ye Field Secretariat was abolished, the six commanderies he had governed were made into Xiang Province, and Yue was at once appointed its governor.
translations.idiomatic: When the Ye Field Secretariat was dissolved, his six commanderies became Xiang Province and he was made its governor.

sentences.zh: 秉法平當，百姓稱之。

translations.literal: He held the law evenly, and the people praised him.
translations.idiomatic: He applied the law evenly, and the people praised him.

sentences.zh: 鄴舊有圓池，時果初熟，丞吏送之，嶽不受，曰：「果未進禦，吾何得先食！

translations.literal: Ye had an old round pond; when the season's fruit first ripened, clerks sent some; Yue would not accept it, saying, "The fruit has not yet been presented to the court—how may I eat first!
translations.idiomatic: Ye had an old round pond; when the first fruit ripened, clerks brought him some. Yue refused: "Fruit not yet sent to the palace—how should I taste it first?

sentences.zh: 」其謹如此。

translations.literal: His scruple was such as this.
translations.idiomatic: So scrupulous was he.

sentences.zh: 遷司空。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 岳兄子路，有罪，諸父兄弟悉誅，特赦岳父子。

translations.literal: Yue's nephew's son Lu had committed a crime; all paternal uncles and brothers were executed, but Yue and his son alone were specially pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: His nephew's son Lu offended; every uncle and brother was put to death, yet Yue and his son alone were spared.

sentences.zh: 候官告嶽衣服鮮麗，行止風采擬儀人君。

translations.literal: The inspectorate reported that Yue's dress was splendid and his bearing and grace rivaled an emperor's.
translations.idiomatic: Inspectors reported Yue's dress too fine and his bearing princely.

sentences.zh: 遇道武不豫，多所猜忌，遂誅之。

translations.literal: Daowu was unwell and full of suspicion; he was therefore executed.
translations.idiomatic: Daowu, ill and suspicious, had him executed.

sentences.zh: 時人咸冤惜焉。

translations.literal: All at the time deemed it a wrongful death and mourned him.
translations.idiomatic: All who knew him called it injustice and grieved.

sentences.zh: 嶽葬在代西善無界。

translations.literal: Yue was buried on the western border of Shanyang in Dai.
translations.idiomatic: He was buried west of Shanyang in Dai.

sentences.zh: 後太武征赫連氏，經其墓宅，愴然改容，遂下詔為立廟，令一川之人，四時致祭。

translations.literal: Later, when Emperor Taiwu campaigned against the Helian, he passed the tomb and grave; his face changed in sorrow, and he issued an edict to erect a temple and ordered the people of the whole valley to offer sacrifice in the four seasons.
translations.idiomatic: Later Taiwu, campaigning against the Helian, passed his tomb, grieved, ordered a temple built, and commanded the valley to sacrifice each season.

sentences.zh: 求其子孫任為帥者，得其子陵。

translations.literal: He sought a descendant fit to serve as commander and found his son Ling.
translations.idiomatic: He sought a descendant to lead the line and found his son Ling.

sentences.zh: 從征有功，聽襲爵。

translations.literal: Following campaigns with merit, he was permitted to inherit the title.
translations.idiomatic: Ling served with merit and was allowed to inherit the title.

sentences.zh: 王建，廣寧人也。

translations.literal: Wang Jian, a man of Guangning.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jian was from Guangning.

sentences.zh: 祖姑為平文後，生昭成皇帝。

translations.literal: His father's aunt was consort to Emperor Pingwen and bore Emperor Zhaocheng.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather's sister was consort to Emperor Pingwen and bore Emperor Zhaocheng.

sentences.zh: 伯祖豐，以帝舅貴重。

translations.literal: His grand-uncle Feng, as the emperor's maternal uncle, was greatly honored.
translations.idiomatic: His grand-uncle Feng, the emperor's uncle by marriage, stood in high honor.

sentences.zh: 豐子支，尚昭成女，甚見親待。

translations.literal: Feng's son Zhi married Zhaocheng's daughter and was treated with great intimacy.
translations.idiomatic: Feng's son Zhi married a daughter of Zhaocheng and was held close.

sentences.zh: 建少尚公主。

translations.literal: Jian in youth married a princess.
translations.idiomatic: Jian in youth married a princess.

sentences.zh: 登國初，為外朝大人。

translations.literal: At the founding of the state he was a senior minister of the outer court.
translations.idiomatic: At the state's founding he was a senior minister of the outer court.

sentences.zh: 與和跋等十三人迭典庶事，參與計謀。

translations.literal: With He Ba and twelve others he took turns managing routine affairs and joined in planning.
translations.idiomatic: With He Ba and twelve others he rotated through daily affairs and state counsel.

sentences.zh: 道武遣使慕容垂，建辭色高亢，垂壯之。

translations.literal: Emperor Daowu sent an envoy to Murong Chui; Jian's words were lofty and Chui admired him.
translations.idiomatic: Daowu sent him to Murong Chui; Jian spoke boldly and Chui admired him.

sentences.zh: 還為左大夫。

translations.literal: On return he was made Left Grand Master.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was made Left Grand Master.

sentences.zh: 建兄回，時為大夫，諸子多不慎法，建具以狀聞，回父子伏誅。

translations.literal: Jian's elder brother Hui was then a grand master; his sons often did not heed the law, and Jian reported the facts in full—Hui and his sons were executed.
translations.idiomatic: His brother Hui was a grand master; Hui's sons broke the law, and Jian reported them—Hui and his sons were executed.

sentences.zh: 其訐直如此。

translations.literal: His blunt uprightness was such as this.
translations.idiomatic: So blunt was his uprightness.

sentences.zh: 從征伐諸國，破二十餘部。

translations.literal: In campaigns against the various states he broke more than twenty tribes.
translations.idiomatic: In campaigns he broke more than twenty tribal states.

sentences.zh: 又從征衛辰，破之。

translations.literal: He also followed the campaign against Wei Chen and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the campaign against Wei Chen and defeated him.

sentences.zh: 為中部大人。

translations.literal: He was made Grand Chief of the Central Tribes.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Grand Chief of the Central Tribes.

sentences.zh: 破慕容寶於參合，帝乘勝將席捲南夏。

translations.literal: Murong Bao was defeated at Canhe; the emperor, pressing the victory, meant to sweep Southern Xia.
translations.idiomatic: Bao was crushed at Canhe; the emperor meant to sweep the south in pursuit.

sentences.zh: 於是簡擇俘眾，有才能者留之；

translations.literal: Thereupon the captives were sifted and those with ability were kept;
translations.idiomatic: Captives with talent were kept;

sentences.zh: 其餘欲悉給衣糧遣歸，令中州之人咸知恩德。

translations.literal: the rest were to be given clothes and grain and sent home, so that the people of the central provinces might all know grace.
translations.idiomatic: the rest were to be clothed, fed, and sent home so the central lands would know Wei's mercy.

sentences.zh: 建以為寶覆敗於此，國內空虛，獲而歸之，縱敵生患，不如殺之。

translations.literal: Jian held that Bao had been overthrown here, the state within was empty, and to capture and release them would let the foe breed trouble—it was better to kill them.
translations.idiomatic: Jian argued that Bao's realm was hollow, and mercy would breed enemies—they should be killed.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「若從建言，非伐罪吊人之義。

translations.literal: The emperor said, "If I follow Jian's counsel, it is not the righteousness of punishing crime and comforting the people."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "That would betray the war of punishment and comfort."

sentences.zh: 」諸將咸以建言為然。

translations.literal: The generals all held Jian's counsel right.
translations.idiomatic: The generals sided with Jian.

sentences.zh: 建又固執，乃坑之。

translations.literal: Jian again insisted, and they were buried alive.
translations.idiomatic: Jian pressed again, and they were buried alive.

sentences.zh: 帝既而悔焉。

translations.literal: The emperor afterward regretted it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor soon regretted it.

sentences.zh: 并州既平，車駕出井陘，次常山。

translations.literal: Bing Province having been pacified, the imperial carriage exited Jingxing Pass and halted at Changshan.
translations.idiomatic: Bingzhou pacified, the court passed Jingxing and halted at Changshan.

sentences.zh: 諸郡皆降，唯中山、鄴、信都三城不下。

translations.literal: Every commandery surrendered except Zhongshan, Ye, and Xindu, which would not fall.
translations.idiomatic: Every commandery submitted save Zhongshan, Ye, and Xindu.

sentences.zh: 乃遣衛王儀南攻鄴，建攻信都等城。

translations.literal: The Prince of Wei, Yi, was sent south against Ye; Jian attacked Xindu and other cities.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Wei Yi attacked Ye; Jian besieged Xindu and the rest.

sentences.zh: 建等攻城六十餘日，不能克，士卒多傷。

translations.literal: Jian and the others besieged for more than sixty days without taking them; many soldiers were wounded.
translations.idiomatic: Sixty days of siege failed; casualties mounted.

sentences.zh: 帝自中山幸信都，降之。

translations.literal: The emperor himself came from Zhongshan to Xindu and it surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor came from Zhongshan to Xindu and it yielded.

sentences.zh: 車駕幸钜鹿，破寶眾于柏肆塢，遂圍中山。

translations.literal: The imperial carriage reached Julu and broke Bao's forces at Baixi Stockade, then besieged Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: At Julu he broke Bao at Baixi Stockade and besieged Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 寶棄城走和龍，城內無主，將夜入乘勝據守其門。

translations.literal: Bao abandoned the city and fled to Helong; within the city there was no lord, and the generals meant to enter by night and seize the gates in victory.
translations.idiomatic: Bao fled to Helong; the city was headless, and the generals meant to rush the gates by night.

sentences.zh: 建貪而無謀，意在虜獲。

translations.literal: Jian was greedy and without plan, his mind on plunder.
translations.idiomatic: Jian, greedy and planless, thought only of loot.

sentences.zh: 恐士卒肆掠，盜亂府庫，請候天明，帝乃止。

translations.literal: Fearing the soldiers would plunder wildly and pillage the treasuries, he asked to wait until dawn; the emperor then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing looting of the treasuries, he begged to wait for dawn; the emperor held the army.

sentences.zh: 是夜，徒何人共立慕容普驎為主，遂閉門固守。

translations.literal: That night, refugees together set up Murong Pulin as lord and closed the gates to hold firm.
translations.idiomatic: That night refugees made Murong Pulin ruler and barred the gates.

sentences.zh: 帝乃悉眾攻之，使人登巢車臨城，招其眾。

translations.literal: The emperor then attacked with his full force, sent men up nest carts overlooking the walls, and summoned the people.
translations.idiomatic: He assaulted in force, sent men up siege towers to call the city in.

sentences.zh: 皆曰：「但恐如參合之眾，故求全月日命耳。

translations.literal: All said, "We only fear becoming like the host at Canhe, and so beg a full month of life."
translations.idiomatic: They answered, "We fear the fate of Canhe and beg only to live out the month."

sentences.zh: 」帝聞之，顧視建而唾其面。

translations.literal: Hearing this, the emperor turned, looked at Jian, and spat in his face.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing this, the emperor turned and spat in Jian's face.

sentences.zh: 中山平，賜建爵濮陽公。

translations.literal: Zhongshan was pacified; Jian was enfeoffed Duke of Puyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongshan fell; Jian was made Duke of Puyang.

sentences.zh: 遷太僕，徙真定公，加散騎常侍、冀青二州刺史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Grand Master of the Herds, then to Duke of Zhending, with additional posts as Regular Attendant and Governor of Ji and Qing.
translations.idiomatic: He became Grand Master of the Herds, then Duke of Zhending, Regular Attendant, and governor of Ji and Qing.

sentences.zh: 卒，陪葬金陵。

translations.literal: He died and was buried with honor at Jinling.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was buried with honor at Jinling.

sentences.zh: 羅結，代人也。

translations.literal: Luo Jie, a man of Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Jie was from Dai.

sentences.zh: 其先世領部落，為魏附臣。

translations.literal: His ancestors for generations led their tribe as Wei's attached subjects.
translations.idiomatic: His line had led their tribe as Wei subjects for generations.

sentences.zh: 劉顯之逆，結從道武幸賀蘭部。

translations.literal: At Liu Xian's rebellion, Jie followed Daowu on his visit to the Helan.
translations.idiomatic: At Liu Xian's revolt Jie followed Daowu to the Helan.

sentences.zh: 後賜爵屈蛇侯。

translations.literal: Later he was enfeoffed Marquis of Qushe.
translations.idiomatic: He was later made Marquis of Qushe.

sentences.zh: 太武初，累遷侍中、外都大官，總三十六曹事。

translations.literal: In the early Taiwu reign he was repeatedly promoted to Palace Attendant and Grand Officer of the Outer Capital, overseeing the thirty-six bureaus.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Taiwu he rose to Palace Attendant and Grand Officer of the Outer Capital over thirty-six bureaus.

sentences.zh: 年一百七歲，精爽不衰。

translations.literal: At one hundred seven his spirit was undiminished.
translations.idiomatic: At one hundred seven his mind was still clear.

sentences.zh: 太武以其忠愨，甚信待之。

translations.literal: Taiwu for his loyalty and honesty greatly trusted him.
translations.idiomatic: Taiwu trusted him deeply for his loyalty.

sentences.zh: 監典後宮，出入臥內，因除長秋卿。

translations.literal: Overseeing the inner palace, entering and leaving the sleeping quarters, he was therefore made Director of the Palace Harem.
translations.idiomatic: He oversaw the inner palace, went in and out of the royal bedchamber, and was made Director of the Palace Harem.

sentences.zh: 年一百一十，詔聽歸老。

translations.literal: At one hundred ten an edict permitted him to retire.
translations.idiomatic: At one hundred ten he was allowed to retire.

sentences.zh: 賜大寧東川為私第別業。

translations.literal: Great Ning and the Eastern River were granted as a private estate and separate residence.
translations.idiomatic: Great Ning and Eastern River were granted as his private estate.

sentences.zh: 並為築城，即號曰羅侯城。

translations.literal: A city was also built for him, called Luo Marquis City.
translations.idiomatic: A city was built for him, called Luo Marquis City.

sentences.zh: 朝廷每有大事，驛馬詢問焉。

translations.literal: Whenever the court had a great affair, a post horse was sent to inquire of him.
translations.idiomatic: On great affairs of state a courier was sent to ask his counsel.

sentences.zh: 年一百二十，卒，諡曰貞。

translations.literal: At one hundred twenty he died; posthumous name Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: At one hundred twenty he died, posthumous name Zhen.

sentences.zh: 子斤，從太武討赫連昌，力戰有功，歷位四部尚書。

translations.literal: His son Jin followed Taiwu against He Lian Chang, fought fiercely with merit, and rose to Director of the Four Bureaus.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jin campaigned against He Lian Chang with fierce merit and rose to Director of the Four Bureaus.

sentences.zh: 從平涼州，以功賜爵帶方公，除長安鎮都大將。

translations.literal: Following the pacification of Liang Province, for merit he was enfeoffed Duke of Daifang and made Grand General of Chang'an Garrison.
translations.idiomatic: After Liangzhou was pacified he was made Duke of Daifang and Grand General of Chang'an Garrison.

sentences.zh: 會蠕蠕侵境，除柔玄鎮都大將。

translations.literal: When the Rouran invaded the frontier, he was made Grand General of Rouxuan Garrison.
translations.idiomatic: When the Rouran raided the border he was made Grand General of Rouxuan Garrison.

sentences.zh: 卒，諡曰靜，陪葬金陵。

translations.literal: He died; posthumous name Jing, buried with honor at Jinling.
translations.idiomatic: He died, posthumous name Jing, and was buried with honor at Jinling.

sentences.zh: 子敢襲爵，位庫部尚書。

translations.literal: His son Gan inherited the title and held the post of Director of the Storehouse Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: His son Gan inherited the title and became Director of the Storehouse Bureau.

sentences.zh: 卒，子伊利襲。

translations.literal: He died; his son Yili inherited.
translations.idiomatic: He died; his son Yili inherited.

sentences.zh: 子真襲，降爵為公。

translations.literal: His son Zhen inherited and was demoted from marquis to duke.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhen inherited and was reduced from marquis to duke.

sentences.zh: 真弟大拔，封钜鹿子。

translations.literal: Zhen's younger brother Daba was enfeoffed as Baron of Julu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen's younger brother Daba was made Baron of Julu.

sentences.zh: 大拔孫寶，字道成，性淳樸，好讀書。

translations.literal: Daba's grandson Bao, style Daocheng, was plain and honest and loved reading.
translations.idiomatic: Daba's grandson Bao, styled Daocheng, was plain, honest, and fond of books.

sentences.zh: 明帝時，仕至朔州刺史。

translations.literal: In Emperor Ming's time he served to Governor of Shuozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Ming he rose to governor of Shuozhou.

sentences.zh: 時邊事屢興，人多流散。

translations.literal: Border affairs flared repeatedly and many people were displaced.
translations.idiomatic: Border wars drove many into flight.

sentences.zh: 及寶至，稍安集之。

translations.literal: When Bao arrived, he gradually brought them back and settled them.
translations.idiomatic: When Bao arrived he gradually gathered and settled them.

sentences.zh: 殘壞舊宅，皆命葺構；

translations.literal: Ruined old dwellings—he ordered them all repaired;
translations.idiomatic: Ruined houses he ordered rebuilt;

sentences.zh: 人歸繼路，歲考為天下最。

translations.literal: people returned in an unbroken stream, and his yearly assessment ranked first in the realm.
translations.idiomatic: refugees returned in streams, and his yearly rating ranked first in the realm.

sentences.zh: 後隨大都督源子邕討擊葛榮。

translations.literal: Later he followed the Grand Commander Yuan Ziyong in attacking Ge Rong.
translations.idiomatic: Later he followed Grand Commander Yuan Ziyong against Ge Rong.

sentences.zh: 王師敗績。

translations.literal: The imperial army suffered defeat.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial army was routed.

sentences.zh: 寶囚于榮軍，變姓名，匿于戎伍，以免害。

translations.literal: Bao was taken prisoner in Rong's army; he changed his name, hid among the soldiers, and escaped harm.
translations.idiomatic: Bao was taken by Rong's army; he changed his name, hid among the ranks, and survived.

sentences.zh: 久之。

translations.literal: A long time passed.
translations.idiomatic: A long time passed.

sentences.zh: 賊中有朔州人識寶者，謂寶曰：「使君寧自苦至此？

translations.literal: Among the rebels a man of Shuozhou recognized Bao and said to him, "My lord, would you truly torment yourself to this point?
translations.idiomatic: A Shuozhou man among the rebels knew him and said, "My lord, must you suffer so?

sentences.zh: 」遂將詣榮。

translations.literal: He was therefore taken to Rong.
translations.idiomatic: They took him to Rong.

sentences.zh: 笑曰：「婁公，吾方圖事，何相見之晚！

translations.literal: Rong laughed and said, "Master Lou, I am just now plotting affairs—how late you come to see me!
translations.idiomatic: Rong laughed: "Master Lou, I am plotting great things—how late you come!

sentences.zh: 」因顧謂人曰：「此公行善，天道報之，得免亂兵，即其驗也。

translations.literal: He then turned and told others, "This gentleman does good; heaven rewards him—escaping the marauders is proof."
translations.idiomatic: He told his men, "This man does good; heaven spared him from the mob—that is proof."

sentences.zh: 」寶遇逃者，密啟賊形勢，規為內應。

translations.literal: When Bao met fugitives he secretly reported the rebels' situation and plotted to act as an inside agent.
translations.idiomatic: Bao secretly sent word on rebel strength through fugitives and plotted as an inside man.

sentences.zh: 天子感其壯志，召寶第二子景賢，授員外散騎常侍郎。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven was moved by his stalwart will and summoned Bao's second son Jingxian, appointing him Supernumerary Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, moved by his courage, summoned Bao's second son Jingxian and made him Supernumerary Regular Attendant.

sentences.zh: 葛榮滅，寶始得還。

translations.literal: When Ge Rong was destroyed, Bao at last returned.
translations.idiomatic: When Ge Rong fell, Bao at last came home.

sentences.zh: 永安中，除假員外散騎常侍，使蠕蠕。

translations.literal: In the Yongan era he was made Acting Supernumerary Regular Attendant and sent to the Rouran.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongan he was made Acting Supernumerary Regular Attendant and sent to the Rouran.

sentences.zh: 先是，蠕蠕稱籓上表，後以中州不競，書為敵國之儀。

translations.literal: Earlier the Rouran had called themselves vassals and submitted a memorial, but later, seeing the central provinces in disorder, they wrote in the forms of a hostile state.
translations.idiomatic: The Rouran had once submitted as vassals, but later, seeing the central lands in turmoil, wrote as to an equal enemy.

sentences.zh: 寶責之。

translations.literal: Bao rebuked them.
translations.idiomatic: Bao rebuked them.

sentences.zh: 蠕蠕主大驚，自知惡，謝曰：「此作書人誤。

translations.literal: The Rouran ruler was greatly alarmed, knew himself in the wrong, and apologized, saying, "The scribe who drafted this letter erred."
translations.idiomatic: The Rouran ruler was alarmed, confessed fault, and said the letter was a clerk's mistake.

sentences.zh: 」遂更稱籓。

translations.literal: They then again called themselves vassals.
translations.idiomatic: They again styled themselves vassals.

sentences.zh: 孝武帝立，敕寶與行台長孫子彥鎮恆農。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu was enthroned, an edict ordered Bao and Field Secretariat Chief Zhangsun Ziyan to garrison Hengnong.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu rose, Bao and Field Secretariat Chief Zhangsun Ziyan were ordered to hold Hengnong.

sentences.zh: 後從入關，封廣甯縣伯。

translations.literal: Later he followed the court into Guanzhong and was enfeoffed Baron of Guangning.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the court into Guanzhong and was made Baron of Guangning.

sentences.zh: 大統元年，詔領著作郎，監修國史事，別封平城縣子。

translations.literal: In the first year of Datong, an edict put him in charge of the Director of Literature, overseeing the compilation of the national history, with a separate enfeoffment as Baron of Pingcheng.
translations.idiomatic: In Datong 1 he was put over the Director of Literature to oversee the national history and enfeoffed Baron of Pingcheng.

sentences.zh: 後授國子祭酒、侍中，進儀同三司，兼太子太傅，攝東宮詹事。

translations.literal: Later he was made Director of the National University, Palace Attendant, advanced to Pillar of State, concurrently Tutor of the Crown Prince, and acting Supervisor of the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Later he became Director of the National University, Palace Attendant, Pillar of State, Tutor of the Crown Prince, and acting Supervisor of the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 寶為人清簡少言，頗諳舊事。

translations.literal: Bao as a man was pure, sparing of words, and well versed in old affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Bao was spare of speech, pure in manner, and versed in precedent.

sentences.zh: 位曆師傅，守靖謙恭，以此為人所敬。

translations.literal: His posts were those of a teacher; he kept to quiet respect and was therefore honored by others.
translations.idiomatic: He held the posts of a teacher and kept quiet respect, and men honored him.

sentences.zh: 後行涇州事，卒於州。

translations.literal: Later he administered Jing Province and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: Later he administered Jing Province and died there.

sentences.zh: 閭大肥，蠕蠕人也。

translations.literal: Lu Dafei, a man of the Rouran.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Dafei was a Rouran.

sentences.zh: 道武時歸魏，尚華陽公主，賜爵其思子。

translations.literal: In Emperor Daowu's time he came over to Wei, married Princess Huayang, and was enfeoffed Baron of Qisi.
translations.idiomatic: In Daowu's time he submitted to Wei, married Princess Huayang, and was made Baron of Qisi.

sentences.zh: 與弟並為上賓，入八議。

translations.literal: With his younger brother he became a senior guest and entered the Eight Deliberations.
translations.idiomatic: He and his brother became senior guests and entered the Eight Deliberations.

sentences.zh: 明元即位，為內都大官，進爵為侯。

translations.literal: When Emperor Mingyuan took the throne, he was made Grand Officer of the Inner Capital and advanced to marquis.
translations.idiomatic: When Mingyuan took the throne he was made Grand Officer of the Inner Capital and raised to marquis.

sentences.zh: 宜城王奚斤之攻武牢，大肥與娥清領十二軍出中道。

translations.literal: When Prince of Yicheng Xi Jin attacked Wulao, Dafei and E Qing led twelve armies on the middle route.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince of Yicheng Xi Jin attacked Wulao, Dafei and E Qing led twelve armies on the center road.

sentences.zh: 太武初，復與奚斤出雲中白道討大檀，破之。

translations.literal: In early Taiwu he again campaigned with Xi Jin by the White Road from Yunzhong against Da Tan and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Taiwu he again marched with Xi Jin from Yunzhong by the White Road against Da Tan and defeated him.

sentences.zh: 後從討赫連昌，以功授榮陽公。

translations.literal: Later he followed the campaign against He Lian Chang and for merit was made Duke of Xingyang.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the campaign against He Lian Chang and was made Duke of Xingyang.

sentences.zh: 公主薨，復尚護澤公主。

translations.literal: When the princess died, he again married Princess Huzhe.
translations.idiomatic: When his princess died he married Princess Huzhe.

sentences.zh: 太武將拜大肥為王，遇疾卒。

translations.literal: Taiwu was about to enfeoff Dafei as king when he fell ill and died.
translations.idiomatic: Taiwu was about to make him a king when illness took him.

sentences.zh: 奚牧，代人也。

translations.literal: Xi Mu, a man of Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Mu was from Dai.

sentences.zh: 重厚有智謀，道武寵遇之，稱曰仲兄。

translations.literal: Heavy, steady, and full of stratagem, Daowu favored him and called him Second Brother.
translations.idiomatic: Steady and resourceful, Daowu favored him and called him Second Brother.

sentences.zh: 初，劉顯害帝，梁眷知之，潛使牧與穆崇至七個山以告。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Liu Xian harmed the emperor, Liang Juan knew it and secretly sent Mu with Mu Chong to Seven Mountains to report.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Xian harmed the emperor, Liang Juan knew and secretly sent Mu with Mu Chong to Seven Mountains to warn Daowu.

sentences.zh: 帝錄先帝舊臣，又以牧告顯功，使敷奏政事，參與計謀。

translations.literal: The emperor recorded the old ministers of the former emperor; because Mu had reported Xian's deed, he was made to present memorials on government and join in planning.
translations.idiomatic: Daowu honored old service and, for Mu's warning of Xian, set him to memorials and counsel.

sentences.zh: 從征慕容寶，以功拜并州刺史，賜爵任城公。

translations.literal: In the campaign against Murong Bao he was for merit made Governor of Bingzhou and enfeoffed Duke of Rencheng.
translations.idiomatic: Against Murong Bao he was made governor of Bingzhou and Duke of Rencheng.

sentences.zh: 州與姚興接界，興頗寇邊。

translations.literal: The province bordered Yao Xing, and Xing often raided the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Bingzhou bordered Yao Xing, who often raided.

sentences.zh: 牧乃與興書，稱頓首，均禮抗之，責興侵邊不直之意。

translations.literal: Mu then wrote Xing, styling himself with bowed head yet matching him in ritual, rebuking Xing's unjust border raids.
translations.idiomatic: Mu wrote Xing, bowing his head in form yet matching him in rank, and rebuked his raids.

sentences.zh: 興以與國和通，恨之，有言于道武，道武戮之。

translations.literal: Xing, wishing peace with the state, resented it and spoke to Daowu; Daowu executed Mu.
translations.idiomatic: Xing, wanting peace, complained to Daowu, and Daowu had Mu executed.

sentences.zh: 和跋，代人也。

translations.literal: He Ba, a man of Dai.
translations.idiomatic: He Ba was from Dai.

sentences.zh: 世領部落，為魏附臣。

translations.literal: For generations his line led their tribe as Wei's attached subjects.
translations.idiomatic: His line had led their tribe as Wei subjects for generations.

sentences.zh: 至跋，以才辯知名。

translations.literal: At Ba's time he was famed for talent and eloquence.
translations.idiomatic: In Ba's time he was famed for eloquence and wit.

sentences.zh: 道武擢為外朝大人，參軍國大謀，雅有智算，賜爵日南公。

translations.literal: Daowu promoted him to senior minister of the outer court, joining in great state counsel; he had elegant wisdom and calculation and was enfeoffed Duke of Rinan.
translations.idiomatic: Daowu made him a senior outer-court minister in great counsel; he was enfeoffed Duke of Rinan.

sentences.zh: 從平中原，以功進為尚書，鎮鄴。

translations.literal: Following the pacification of the Central Plains, for merit he was advanced to Director of the Imperial Secretariat and garrisoned Ye.
translations.idiomatic: After the Central Plains were pacified he became Director of the Imperial Secretariat and held Ye.

sentences.zh: 以破慕容德軍，改封定陵公。

translations.literal: For defeating Murong De's army he was re-enfeoffed Duke of Dingling.
translations.idiomatic: For breaking Murong De's army he was re-enfeoffed Duke of Dingling.

sentences.zh: 與常山王遵討賀蘭部別帥木易千，破之。

translations.literal: With Prince of Changshan Zun he attacked the Helan splinter chieftain Muyiqian and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: With Prince of Changshan Zun he defeated the Helan splinter chief Muyiqian.

sentences.zh: 出為平原太守。

translations.literal: He went out as Administrator of Pingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: He went out as administrator of Pingyuan.

sentences.zh: 道武寵跋于諸將。

translations.literal: Daowu favored Ba above the other generals.
translations.idiomatic: Daowu favored Ba above other generals.

sentences.zh: 群臣皆敦尚恭儉，而跋好修虛譽，炫曜于時。

translations.literal: The ministers all prized respectful frugality, but Ba loved to cultivate empty reputation and dazzle the age.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers prized frugality; Ba courted empty fame and dazzled his age.

sentences.zh: 性尤奢淫，帝戒之不革。

translations.literal: His nature was especially extravagant and dissolute; the emperor admonished him but he did not reform.
translations.idiomatic: He was extravagant; the emperor warned him in vain.

sentences.zh: 後車駕北狩豺山，收跋，刑之路側。

translations.literal: Later, when the imperial carriage hunted north at Mount Shi, Ba was arrested and executed by the roadside.
translations.idiomatic: Later, on a northern hunt at Mount Shi, Ba was seized and executed by the road.

sentences.zh: 妻劉氏自殺以從。

translations.literal: His wife Lady Liu killed herself to follow him.
translations.idiomatic: His wife Lady Liu killed herself to follow.

sentences.zh: 初將刑跋，道武命其諸弟毗等視訣。

translations.literal: When Ba was first to be executed, Daowu ordered his younger brothers Pi and others to witness the farewell.
translations.idiomatic: Before the execution Daowu ordered his brothers Pi and others to witness his farewell.

sentences.zh: 跋謂毗曰：「氵壘北地瘠，可居水南，就耕良田，廣為產業，各相勸勵。

translations.literal: Ba told Pi, "The land north of the Luo is poor; you may settle south of the water, take good fields in cultivation, broaden your estates, and urge one another on."
translations.idiomatic: Ba told Pi, "North of the Luo the land is poor—settle south of the river, till good fields, and build your estates."

sentences.zh: 」令之背己，曰：「汝曹何忍視吾之死！

translations.literal: Turning his back on them he said, "How can you bear to watch my death!
translations.idiomatic: Turning away he cried, "How can you bear to watch me die!

sentences.zh: 」毗等解其微意，詐稱使者，奔長安。

translations.literal: Pi and the others grasped his subtle intent, falsely claimed to be envoys, and fled to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Pi and the others read his hint, pretended to be envoys, and fled to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 道武誅其家。

translations.literal: Daowu exterminated his family.
translations.idiomatic: Daowu exterminated his family.

sentences.zh: 後太武幸豺山校獵，忽暴霧四塞，怪問之。

translations.literal: Later, when Emperor Taiwu hunted at Mount Shi, sudden thick fog closed in on every side; in wonder he asked the cause.
translations.idiomatic: Later Taiwu hunted at Mount Shi; sudden fog closed every side, and he asked why.

sentences.zh: 群下僉言跋世居此，祠塚猶存，或者能致斯變。

translations.literal: The crowd all said Ba had dwelt here and his shrine tomb still stood—perhaps he could bring such change.
translations.idiomatic: All said Ba had lived there and his tomb still stood—perhaps he caused it.

sentences.zh: 帝遣建興公古弼祭以三牲，霧即除。

translations.literal: The emperor sent Duke of Jianxing Gu Bi to sacrifice with the three beasts; the fog at once lifted.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Duke of Jianxing Gu Bi with the triple offering; the fog lifted.

sentences.zh: 後太武蒐狩之日，每先遣祭之。

translations.literal: Afterward, on every day of Taiwu's hunts, he first sent men to sacrifice to him.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward, on every hunt, Taiwu first sent sacrifice to Ba.

sentences.zh: 莫題，代人也。

translations.literal: Mo Ti, a man of Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Mo Ti was from Dai.

sentences.zh: 多智，有才用。

translations.literal: Full of wisdom and able in office.
translations.idiomatic: He was clever and capable.

sentences.zh: 初為幢將，領禁兵。

translations.literal: At first he was a standard-bearer general commanding the guard troops.
translations.idiomatic: At first he was a standard-bearer general over the guard.

sentences.zh: 道武之征慕容寶，寶夜犯營，軍人驚駭。

translations.literal: In Daowu's campaign against Murong Bao, Bao attacked the camp by night and the army was alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: When Daowu campaigned against Murong Bao, Bao raided the camp by night and the army panicked.

sentences.zh: 遂有亡還京師者，言官軍敗于柏肆。

translations.literal: Some fled back to the capital, saying the imperial army had been defeated at Baixi.
translations.idiomatic: Some fled to the capital reporting defeat at Baixi.

sentences.zh: 京師不安，南安西元順因欲攝國事。

translations.literal: The capital was uneasy; the Western Pacification General Yuan Shun of Nan'an therefore meant to seize state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The capital shook; Nan'an's Yuan Shun meant to seize power.

sentences.zh: 題曰：「大事不可輕爾，不然，禍將及矣！

translations.literal: Ti said, "Great affairs must not be treated lightly—otherwise calamity will come!
translations.idiomatic: Ti said, "Great affairs are not to be seized lightly—or disaster follows!

sentences.zh: 」順乃止。

translations.literal: Shun then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Shun then stopped.

sentences.zh: 後封高邑公。

translations.literal: Later he was enfeoffed Duke of Gaoyi.
translations.idiomatic: He was later made Duke of Gaoyi.

sentences.zh: 窟咄寇南鄙，題時貳於帝，遺箭於窟咄，謂之曰：「三歲犢豈勝重載！

translations.literal: When Kudou raided the southern marches, Ti at the time was disloyal to the emperor and sent Kudou an arrow, telling him, "Can a three-year calf bear a heavy load!
translations.idiomatic: When Kudou raided the south, Ti, then disloyal, sent him an arrow: "Can a three-year calf bear a heavy load?

sentences.zh: 」言窟咄長而帝少也。

translations.literal: The words meant Kudou was grown and the emperor still young.
translations.idiomatic: He meant Kudou was grown and the emperor young.

sentences.zh: 帝既銜之，後有告題居處倨傲，擬則人主。

translations.literal: The emperor bore a grudge; later someone reported that Ti's bearing was arrogant and modeled on a ruler's.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor remembered; later someone reported Ti's arrogance and princely bearing.

sentences.zh: 帝乃使人示之箭，告之曰：「三歲犢能勝重載不？

translations.literal: The emperor then had men show him the arrow and tell him, "Can a three-year calf bear a heavy load or not?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor showed him the arrow and asked, "Can a three-year calf bear a heavy load?

sentences.zh: 」題奉昭，父子對泣。

translations.literal: Ti received the edict; father and son wept facing each other.
translations.idiomatic: Ti took the edict; father and son wept together.

sentences.zh: 詰朝，乃刑之。

translations.literal: At the next court session he was executed.
translations.idiomatic: At the next audience he was executed.

sentences.zh: 賀狄幹，代人也。

translations.literal: He Digan, a man of Dai.
translations.idiomatic: He Digan was from Dai.

sentences.zh: 家本小族，世忠厚，為將以平當稱。

translations.literal: His family was originally of a small clan; for generations they were honest and steady, and as generals they were famed for fairness.
translations.idiomatic: His clan was small and for generations honest; as a commander he was famed for fairness.

sentences.zh: 稍遷北部大人。

translations.literal: He was gradually promoted to Grand Chief of the Northern Tribes.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Grand Chief of the Northern Tribes.

sentences.zh: 登國初，與長孫嵩為對。

translations.literal: At the founding of the state he was paired with Zhangsun Song.
translations.idiomatic: At the state's founding he was paired with Zhangsun Song.

sentences.zh: 明于聽察，為人愛敬。

translations.literal: Clear in hearing and judgment, he was loved and respected by men.
translations.idiomatic: Keen of ear and judgment, he was loved and respected.

sentences.zh: 道武遣狄幹致馬千匹，結婚于姚萇。

translations.literal: Daowu sent Digan to present a thousand horses and conclude a marriage with Yao Chang.
translations.idiomatic: Daowu sent Digan with a thousand horses to seal marriage with Yao Chang.

sentences.zh: 會萇死，興立，因止狄幹而絕婚。

translations.literal: Chang died and Xing took the throne; he therefore detained Digan and broke the betrothal.
translations.idiomatic: Chang died; Xing detained Digan and broke the match.

sentences.zh: 興弟平寇平陽，道武討平之，禽其將狄伯支、唐小方等四十餘人。

translations.literal: Xing's younger brother Pingkou pacified Pingyang; Daowu campaigned, pacified him, and captured his generals Di Bozhi, Tang Xiaofang, and more than forty others.
translations.idiomatic: Xing's brother Pingkou held Pingyang; Daowu defeated him and took Di Bozhi, Tang Xiaofang, and forty more.

sentences.zh: 後興以駿馬千匹贖伯支，而遣狄幹還，帝許之。

translations.literal: Later Xing offered a thousand fine horses to ransom Bozhi and sent Digan back; the emperor permitted it.
translations.idiomatic: Later Xing offered a thousand horses for Bozhi and returned Digan; the emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 幹在長安，因習讀書史，通《論語》、《尚書》諸經，舉止風流，有似儒者。

translations.literal: While in Chang'an, Digan studied histories and mastered the Analects, Documents, and other classics; his bearing was elegant, like a Confucian's.
translations.idiomatic: In Chang'an he studied histories and the Analects and Documents; his bearing grew elegant, like a scholar's.

sentences.zh: 初，帝普封功臣，狄幹雖為姚興所留，遙賜狄幹爵襄武侯，加秦兵將軍。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the emperor enfeoffed the meritous in general, though Digan was detained by Yao Xing, he was enfeoffed from afar as Marquis of Xiangwu and made General of Qin Troops.
translations.idiomatic: When merit was rewarded, though Xing still held him, Digan was enfeoffed from afar as Marquis of Xiangwu and General of Qin Troops.

sentences.zh: 及狄幹至，帝見其言語衣服類中國，以為慕而習之，故忿焉，既而殺之。

translations.literal: When Digan arrived, the emperor saw his speech and dress resembled the central lands and thought he had admired and learned them; he was therefore angry and soon killed him.
translations.idiomatic: When Digan returned, the emperor saw his speech and dress like the central lands, thought him a mimic, grew angry, and killed him.

sentences.zh: 李栗，雁門人也。

translations.literal: Li Li, a man of Yanmen.
translations.idiomatic: Li Li was from Yanmen.

sentences.zh: 昭成時，父祖入北。

translations.literal: In Zhaocheng's time his father and grandfather entered the north.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhaocheng's time his father and grandfather came north.

sentences.zh: 栗少辯捷，有才能兼將略。

translations.literal: Li in youth was eloquent and quick, with talent and also military stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: Li in youth was quick and eloquent, gifted in arms as well as wit.

sentences.zh: 初隨道武幸賀蘭部，愛其藝能。

translations.literal: At first he followed Daowu on his visit to the Helan; Daowu loved his arts.
translations.idiomatic: At first he followed Daowu to the Helan; Daowu loved his skill.

sentences.zh: 時王業草創，爪牙心腹，多任親近，唯栗一介遠寄，兼非戚舊。

translations.literal: At the time the royal enterprise was newly founded; claws and heart, the close and trusted, were mostly kin appointed—only Li alone was sent far, and he was not a relative by marriage.
translations.idiomatic: The realm was newly forged; intimates were kin—only Li was posted far away, no marriage tie to the throne.

sentences.zh: 數有戰功，拜左軍將軍。

translations.literal: He had repeated battle merit and was appointed General of the Left Army.
translations.idiomatic: Repeated merit made him General of the Left Army.

sentences.zh: 栗性簡慢，矜寵，不率禮度。

translations.literal: Li's nature was blunt and careless, proud of favor, and he did not observe ritual propriety.
translations.idiomatic: Li was blunt and proud of favor and scorned ritual.

sentences.zh: 每在道武前舒放倨傲，不自祗肅，笑唾任情。

translations.literal: Before Daowu he stretched himself insolently without self-restraint, laughing and spitting as he pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Before Daowu he lounged insolent, laughing and spitting at will.

sentences.zh: 道武即其宿過誅之。

translations.literal: Daowu seized on his old offenses and executed him.
translations.idiomatic: Daowu seized his old offenses and executed him.

sentences.zh: 於是威嚴始厲，制勒群下盡卑謙之禮，自栗始也。

translations.literal: Thereupon majesty first grew stern; restraining the court to full humility began with Li.
translations.idiomatic: From Li onward majesty grew stern and the court learned humility.

sentences.zh: 奚眷，代人也。

translations.literal: Xi Juan, a man of Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Juan was from Dai.

sentences.zh: 少有將略。

translations.literal: In youth he had military stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he had military stratagem.

sentences.zh: 道武世，有戰功。

translations.literal: In Daowu's reign he had battle merit.
translations.idiomatic: Under Daowu he won battle merit.

sentences.zh: 明元時，為武牢鎮將，為寇所憚。

translations.literal: In Mingyuan's time he was garrison commander of Wulao, and raiders feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Under Mingyuan he held Wulao; raiders feared him.

sentences.zh: 太武時，賜爵南陽公。

translations.literal: In Taiwu's time he was enfeoffed Duke of Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Under Taiwu he was made Duke of Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 及征蠕蠕，眷以都曹尚書督偏將出別道。

translations.literal: On the campaign against the Rouran, Juan as Director of the Capital Bureau supervised detached generals on a separate route.
translations.idiomatic: Campaigning against the Rouran, Juan as Director of the Capital Bureau led detached columns on a separate road.

sentences.zh: 詔會鹿渾海，眷與中山王辰等諸大將俱後期，斬于都南，爵除。

translations.literal: An edict ordered a rendezvous at Luhun Sea; Juan, Prince of Zhongshan Chen, and the other great generals were all late; he was beheaded south of the capital and his title abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Ordered to meet at Luhun Sea, Juan, Prince of Zhongshan Chen, and other great generals were all late; he was beheaded south of the capital and his title struck.

sentences.zh: 論曰：帝王之興，雖則天命，經綸所說，咸藉股肱。

translations.literal: Discussion says: The rise of emperors, though heaven's mandate, in what the classics teach all rely on worthy arms.
translations.idiomatic: The commentators say: Emperors rise by heaven's mandate, yet every classic teaches they lean on worthy arms.

sentences.zh: 神元、桓、穆之際，王跡未顯，操、含托身馳驟之秋，自立功名之地，可謂志識之士矣。

translations.literal: In the days of Emperor Shenyuan and Emperors Huan and Mu the royal trace was not yet bright; in the season when Cao and Han raced to establish themselves, they made their own ground of merit—men of resolve and insight indeed.
translations.idiomatic: In the age of Shenyuan and Huan and Mu the throne was still dim; in the rush of founding, men of resolve carved their own merit.

sentences.zh: 而劉庫仁兄弟忠以為心，盛衰不二。

translations.literal: Yet the brothers Liu Kuren took loyalty as heart and did not waver in rise or fall.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Liu Kuren and his brother held loyalty through rise and fall.

sentences.zh: 純節所存，其意蓋遠，而並貽非命，惜乎！

translations.literal: The purity they kept looked far ahead; yet both met untimely death—pity!
translations.idiomatic: Their purity aimed far; both died untimely—pity!

sentences.zh: 尉真兄弟忠勇奮發，義以忘生。

translations.literal: The brothers Wei Zhen were loyal and brave, rousing themselves, righteousness making them forget life.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zhen and his brothers were loyal and brave, righteousness making them forget life.

sentences.zh: 眷威略著時，增隆家業。

translations.literal: Juan's martial renown stood in his age and enlarged the family estate.
translations.idiomatic: Juan's renown in arms enlarged his house.

sentences.zh: 穆崇夙奉龍顏，早著誠款，遂膺寵眷，位極台司。

translations.literal: Mu Chong long served the dragon countenance, early showing sincere devotion, and therefore received favor to the summit of the secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Mu Chong long served the throne, showed early loyalty, and rose to the secretariat's peak.

sentences.zh: 至乃身豫逆謀，卒蒙全護，從享於廟，抑亦尚功。

translations.literal: He even took part in treasonous plotting yet in the end was wholly spared and shared sacrifice in the temple—this too honored merit.
translations.idiomatic: He even joined treason yet was spared and shared the temple rites—merit still counted.

sentences.zh: 世載公卿，弈弈青紫，盛矣！

translations.literal: Generation after generation of dukes and ministers, rank on rank of purple and blue—how grand!
translations.idiomatic: Generation on generation of ministers in purple and blue—how grand!

sentences.zh: 奚斤世稱忠孝，征伐有克。

translations.literal: Xi Jin for generations was called loyal and filial; in campaigns he had victories.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Jin was called loyal and filial for generations and won his battles.

sentences.zh: 平涼之役，師殲身虜，雖敗崤之責已赦，封屍之效靡立，而恩禮隆渥，沒祀廟廷。

translations.literal: In the Pingliang campaign the army was destroyed and he was taken captive; though the blame of defeat at Yao was pardoned and the rite of returning the corpse was not achieved, favor and rites were still lavish and he was sacrificed in the temple hall.
translations.idiomatic: At Pingliang his army was lost and he was captured; though Yao's blame was pardoned and his corpse never came home, rites and favor were lavish and he was honored in the temple.

sentences.zh: 叔孫建少展誠勤，終著庸伐，臨邊有術，威震夷楚。

translations.literal: Shu Sun Jian in youth showed sincere diligence and in the end achieved service; on the frontier he had method, his might shaking Yi and Chu.
translations.idiomatic: Shu Sun Jian showed early loyalty and earned lasting service; on the frontier his method shook Yi and Chu.

sentences.zh: 俊委節明元，義彰顛沛，察硃提之變，有日磾之風，加以柔而能正，見美朝野。

translations.literal: Jun held to his pledge under Mingyuan, righteousness shining in hardship; discerning the change at Zhuti, he had the air of Jin Midi—added to softness that could correct, he was praised in court and countryside.
translations.idiomatic: Jun kept faith under Mingyuan in hardship; reading Zhuti's change, he had Jin Midi's spirit—soft yet upright, praised in court and field.

sentences.zh: 安同異類之人，智識入用，任等時俊，當有由哉！

translations.literal: An Tong, a man of another stock, yet his wisdom entered use and his appointment matched the age's best—there was reason indeed!
translations.idiomatic: An Tong, of alien stock, yet his wit was used and his rank matched the age's best—no accident!

sentences.zh: 頡禽赫連昌，摧宋氏眾，遂為名將，未易輕也。

translations.literal: Ji captured He Lian Chang and broke the Song hosts—he became a famed general not lightly matched.
translations.idiomatic: Ji seized He Lian Chang and broke Song's armies—a general not lightly matched.

sentences.zh: 庾業延見紀危難之中，受事草創之際，智勇既申，功名尤舉，而不免傾覆，蓋亦其命。

translations.literal: Yu Yeyan is recorded for peril and for service in the founding hour; wisdom and courage both shown, merit and name both raised—yet he could not escape ruin; that too was his fate.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Yeyan shone in peril and founding; wit and courage, merit and name—yet ruin took him; fate, perhaps.

sentences.zh: 王建位遇既高，訐以求直，參合之役，不其罪歟！

translations.literal: Wang Jian's rank and favor were already high; he sought uprightness by denunciation—in the affair of Canhe, was it not his crime?
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jian stood high; he sought uprightness by accusation—at Canhe, was the crime not his?

sentences.zh: 羅結枝附葉從，子孫榮祿。

translations.literal: Luo Jie's branch clung to the trunk; sons and grandsons enjoyed rank and stipend.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Jie's line clung to power; sons and grandsons fed on rank.

sentences.zh: 婁伏連、閭大肥並征代著績，策名前代。

translations.literal: Lou Fulian and Lu Dafei both won fame campaigning in Dai and left their names to earlier ages.
translations.idiomatic: Lou Fulian and Lu Dafei both won fame in Dai and left names to earlier ages.

sentences.zh: 奚牧、和跋、莫題、賀狄幹、李栗、奚眷有忠勤征伐之效，不能以功名自卑，俱至誅夷，亦各其命也。

translations.literal: Xi Mu, He Ba, Mo Ti, He Digan, Li Li, and Xi Juan had loyal, diligent merit in campaign yet could not humble themselves before merit and fame—all came to execution; each had his fate.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Mu, He Ba, Mo Ti, He Digan, Li Li, and Xi Juan served loyally in war yet would not bow before fame—all were executed; each had his fate.
